subclassFeature.name: Path of the Cirque
entries: The sand of the arena, the dirt and cobblestone of the streets, the creaking boards of a makeshift stage – these liminal spaces amidst the margins of civilization are your home. The crowds that encircle you demand entertainment, and by the gods, you will give it to them. They won't know what hit them.

You are a barbarian not of the natural wilds but of the wilds of society. Perhaps you are a street performer, performing feats of strength and acrobatics for passersby, or perhaps you are a professional fighter in the style of the Roman gladiators and charioteers of old, meting out death and destruction amidst the braying chants of a ravenous crowd.

entries.name: The Revel
entries: Instead of the Rage ability of other Barbarians, you have an ability called Revel. You channel your focus and talent for crowd work into a frenzied, ecstatic performative state. Wherever your Barbarian abilities mention Rage, you will use your Revel instead, but there is no fundamental difference between the two. For example, when entering your Revel state, you still do extra damage, but instead it is referred to as “Revel bonus damage.” Moreover, your Revel state will grant you many abilities at Level 3, 6, 10, and 14.

subclassFeature.name: Natural Showstopper
entries: At 3rd level, you are used to having eyes on you, and your inner power is put onto the stage more easily. You have access to these features:

items: When you choose this Primal Path, you may add your Charisma modifier instead of Dexterity to your Unarmored Defense.
You gain proficiency in two of these skills: {@skill Performance}, {@skill Persuasion}, or {@skill Intimidation}.
You know the {@spell thaumaturgy} cantrip. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this and other spells.

While in your Revel, you can make a {@skill Performance}, {@skill Persuasion}, {@skill Intimidation}, {@skill Acrobatics}, or {@skill Athletics} check with advantage. This advantage can be used once per Revel.

subclassFeature.name: Signature Move
entries: You are becoming famous enough that the crowd knows to look out for the special flourishes in your performance. Choose two features from the list below. These become your Signature Moves. You can use a Signature Move a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier. You regain one expended use when you enter Revel, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

For the purposes of this ability and the following ones in this subclass, “crowd” or “audience” or “onlookers” is defined as non-hostile creatures who can see you and are not involved in the fight or action you are undertaking. For instance, if your adventuring companions are engaged in the same combat as you, they are not part of the audience. Additionally, the audience members must have Intelligence scores of 4 or higher. You cannot perform your abilities in front of a herd of cows, for instance.

subclassFeature.name: Revel and Ruin
entries: At 6th level, your abilities grow ever stronger and you are more confident in your talents. You gain one more Signature Move and add it to your repertoire. In addition, you gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Stage Spirit
entries: You grow ever more powerful while basking in the adoration, horror, and fascination of your audience. If you have an audience, you deal more damage for each successive hit until the end of your Revel. Add +1 to your Revel damage for each hit after the first, up to a total of +5 bonus. If you miss, this resets.

entries.name: Fear and Inspiration
entries: Your stage presence strikes fear in the heart of some, and elation in the hearts of others. Choose either the {@spell bane} or {@spell bless} spell. You can cast this spell once per day without needing a spell slot or material components. You cannot cast it while in Revel, but you can cast it beforehand and maintain concentration while in the Revel.

entries.name: Warm up Routine
entries: You can undergo a rehearsal to attempt to rally a crowd, or at least the sensation of performing in front of a crowd, when you are in the absence of one. You must spend at least 10 minutes preparing a small area to perform – work with the GM on what this would look like, but some suggestions would be candles, a block of pine resin, and sand to spread on the ground. You must then engage in physical activity (stretching, lifting, running, etc.); after that, you are “fired up” and may take actions as if you have an audience for the next hour.

subclassFeature.name: Are You Not Entertained?
entries: Your frenzied energy has the potential to spread like wildfire through a crowd. You can attempt to influence others to fight with a devil-may-care disregard: you can spur your allies to fight harder, or turn a crowd into a brawl. During your Revel, you can use your bonus action to choose 6 creatures within 30 feet of you; they can each use your Reckless Attack feature before the end of your next turn. You can do this a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1) before a long rest.

Alternatively, you can choose up to 6 creatures within 30 feet of you; they must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus) or become entranced by you. On a failed save, their speed becomes 0, they are considered {@condition charmed}, and they spend their turns watching you do your work. A creature with immunity to charms or a creature with an Intelligence score less than 4 automatically succeeds on the saving throw. Affected targets may repeat the saving throw at the end of each of their turns, and the effect ends if any of them take damage or when your Revel ends.

subclassFeature.name: Champion of Revels
entries: Your ability to ignite the energy of a crowd and incite it into a conflagration have reached legendary status.

items: Your charm effects on other creatures negate any advantages against being {@condition charmed}. For example, creatures with Fey Ancestry do not have advantage against your charm effect.
You can cast {@spell mass suggestion} once per day without needing a spell slot or material components.

Your Revel and Ruin ability now does even more damage. With each successive hit while Reveling and while in front of an audience, add +2 to your Revel damage bonus. This resets if you miss. You can go up to +10 bonus. If you already boost your damage from feats or other features, you must choose one.
You may choose one more Signature move. All rolls for Signature moves cannot be lower than 10.

subclassFeature.name: College of the Masquerade
entries: “You have never been yourself,” a voice in your head speaks. “You always wore a mask, always hidden in the crowd, in plain sight.” The voice speaks the truth: a mask has always been your identity, your strong side and your greatest weakness.

Perhaps you were raised on the stage, among the festivals, always moving in line with a great group of actors and singers, or you were raised in dark corners, always shunned by the light, and to trick it, you always had to hide your face. You may have constantly needed a mask to hide who you are or some of your features. Nevertheless, the mask is who you are and an actual part of you.

subclassFeature.name: The Masquerade
entries: When you reach 3rd level, the nature of your inspirational magic fuses with your mask and its identity. You can craft special masks that enhance your abilities. Choose two of the following options: Diabolica, Angelico, Fiabesca, Umano.

You can assume the form of a creature that you have seen before related to the mask you chose. For example, you can turn into an Imp if you choose Diabolica. It can be a creature that has a maximum of CR 1 (It will increase to 3 at later levels). Only your Intelligence score, memories, and alignment stay the same. Aside from these, all of your statistics change to the chosen creature.

entries.name: Stronger Effects:
entries: If an ability refers to a DC, it uses your spell save DC instead of the creature's.
Many stat blocks that College of the Masquerade Bards can use are in the SRD 5.1 and in the Bestiary chapter of this book. The suitable stat blocks presented in this setting guide are listed here:

entries.name: Fiend:
entries: {@creature L'anima Vuota|EchoesOfRenaissance|L'anima Vuota, Hollow Skin (CR 1/8)}; {@creature Red Hand of Mammon|EchoesOfRenaissance|Red Hand of Mammon (CR 1/4)}; {@creature Il Rosso|EchoesOfRenaissance|Il Rosso, The Crimson Fiend (CR 1/2)}; {@creature Il Caduto|EchoesOfRenaissance|Il Caduto, The Fallen Demon (CR 2)}

entries.name: Fey:
entries: {@creature Vivo|EchoesOfRenaissance|Vivo, Bright Fairy (CR 1/4)}; {@creature Arcobaleno|EchoesOfRenaissance|Arcobaleno, The Rainbow Fairy (CR 1/2)}

entries.name: Celestial:
entries: {@creature Fated One|EchoesOfRenaissance|Angelo, The Fated One (CR 1/4)}, {@creature Hidden One|EchoesOfRenaissance|Angelo, The Hidden One (CR 1)}, {@creature Radiant One|EchoesOfRenaissance|Angelo, The Radiant One (CR 1)}

When you transform, you also assume the creature's Hit Points and Hit Dice. When you revert to your normal form, you return to the number of hit points you had before you transformed. However, if you revert as a result of dropping to 0 hit points, any excess damage carries over to your normal form. For example, if you take 10 damage in a creature's form and have only 1 hit point left, you revert and take 9 damage. As long as the excess damage doesn't reduce your normal form to 0 hit points, you aren't knocked {@condition unconscious}.

You can't cast spells, and your ability to speak or take any action that requires hands is limited to the capabilities of your creature form. If the creature can cast spells, however, you can cast those spells within the limitations stated before. Additionally, you can't concentrate on spells that you've cast before turning. You don't retain your other class abilities, other than Bardic Inspiration, or other racial abilities.

You choose whether your equipment falls to the ground in your space, merges into your new form, or is worn by it. Worn equipment functions as normal, but the GM decides whether it is practical for the new form to wear a piece of equipment, based on the creature's shape and size. Your equipment doesn't change size or shape to match the new form, and any equipment that the new form can't wear must either fall to the ground or merge with it. Equipment that merges with the form has no effect until you leave the form.

You can use a mask's shapeshifting ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest. If you have no uses left, you can expend a spell slot of 2nd level or higher to gain another use (no action required).
If the chosen forms have any weapons or armor, they are created by the mask's magic as well and disappear after the time is over.
You can use the mask's ability to turn into a creature using a bonus action on your turn.

entries.name: Lending the Mask:
entries: You can lend your mask to another humanoid. The humanoid must not have a negative Charisma modifier, and you must also spend a Bardic Inspiration die for that humanoid to be able to use the mask.
If any of the masks are destroyed, you can spend 1 hour (can be implemented in a short rest) and use specific dye and wood in the process to create a new one.

entries.name: Maschera Diabolica
entries: You can choose to put on a mask resembling the depths of hell and their vicious guardians. You can assume the form of a fiend for 10 minutes.
In addition, you have resistance to fire damage when you put on the mask and in your original form.

entries.name: Maschera Angelico
entries: You choose to put on a mask resembling the fields of Elysium, green gardens above and silk-like wings of the angels depicted in the most beautiful canvases. You can assume the form of a celestial for 10 minutes.
In addition you can cast the {@spell sacred flame} cantrip when you put on the mask and in your original form.

entries.name: Maschera Fiabesco
entries: You choose to put on a mask that would make those beholding you feel like they are in an enchanted forest, speaking to the Fairy Queen herself. You can assume the form of a fey for 10 minutes.
In addition, you are immune to being {@condition charmed} when you put on the mask and in your original form.

entries.name: Maschera Umano
entries: You choose to put on a mask that would resemble the creature with the most potential: a humanoid. You can assume your new form for 10 minutes.
In addition, whenever you put on the mask for the first time in a day, you choose a skill, or tool, and gain proficiency in it.

subclassFeature.name: The Hidden Power
entries: Your maximum CR for the masks becomes 3.
Each mask is more powerful now and gains new benefits when you put them on while in your original form.

entries.name: Diabolica
entries: You can see in magical darkness (120 ft.) as if it were daylight.

entries.name: Angelico
entries: All of your attacks deal an additional {@damage 1d6} radiant damage.

entries.name: Fiabesco
entries: You can use your bonus action to cast {@spell misty step} without the use of a spell slot. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier and regain expended uses when you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Umano
entries: You gain Expertise in a skill you are proficient in. If you already have Expertise in that skill from another source, you can't use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Masked Potential Unleashed
entries: Once you reach 14th level, your bond with your mask and its form reaches its epitome. Your time in a creature form is extended to 1 hour.
In addition, your masks are at their absolute power.

entries.name: Diabolica
entries: You are immune to fire and cold damage.

entries.name: Angelico
entries: You understand when you hear a lie.

entries.name: Fiabesco
entries: Instead of casting {@spell misty step}, you can expend one use of it as a bonus action and choose a creature within 60 ft. of you to swap places with. The creature must succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC or they swap places with you. A creature can choose to fail this saving throw, such as an ally.

entries.name: Umano
entries: While wearing it, you are proficient with a saving throw of your choice. You can choose a new one when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Art Domain
entries: A woman wrapped in colorful fabrics dancing at the edge of a canal, her mind only focused on her heart and her art. The movements carry a melody belonging to the stars unveiled, and it reminds those watching her of whatever belief lies in their spirits and minds. The art is heavenly. The woman understands it better than anyone. She believes in herself and lets her faith find its true nature through her hands and takes shape in the fabric of the world as the opus she fleshes out.

In an atelier nearby, a sculptor molds what the earth has given him: stone and soil. Sweating and working hard on a hot summer's day to finalize the touches of his hammer, he can finally call the statue his magnum opus. The shape mesmerizes its viewers and invokes the deepest feelings within viewers' hearts and offers a glimpse into a world they believe in. The power of the hand's craft is one of the best ways to put faith out to everyone, for every believer.

Art is more than an inspirational calling to you: it is the search for the divine itself. By expressing your ideas, your thoughts, your imagination with all the colors in your mind, you find a divine calling in your heart. Your belief finds its way through your art. Your talents show your dedication, your art pieces prove your faith, and through you, whichever power, ideal or deity you believe in finds its voice and presence in the world.

Art domain clerics could be followers of Apollo, Dionysus, Aphrodite, Artemis, Athena, or Hephaestus from Hellenic mythology (or their Roman counterparts), Odin or Bragi from Norse mythology, or a deity of the arts from another pantheon. They could also follow the footsteps of great artists, singers, and poets in the ancient world, such as Orpheus, Homer, Sappho, or the West African griots. Work with your GM to find a divine inspiration that fits into your game.

subclassFeature.name: Art Domain Spells
entries: At each indicated cleric level, you add the listed spells to your spells prepared:

entries.caption: Art Domain Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell marvelous performance|EchoesOfRenaissance}, {@spell illusory taunt|EchoesOfRenaissance}
3rd
{@spell amplify feelings|EchoesOfRenaissance}, {@spell calm emotions}
5th
{@spell majestic performance|EchoesOfRenaissance}, {@spell slow}
7th
{@spell fabricate}, {@spell freedom of movement}
9th
{@spell disrupt one's weave|EchoesOfRenaissance}, {@spell telekinesis}

subclassFeature.name: Beauty of the Art
entries: You choose an aspect of the art and channel your divine inspiration with it.

subclassFeature.name: Sculpture
entries: Your touch becomes a deadly one and invokes the beauty captured in stillness. You have proficiency with {@item mason's tools|PHB} and {@item woodcarver's tools|PHB}, and you have access to the following abilities:

items: You have the ability to momentarily immobilize your enemies, by turning their limbs to stone for a very limited time. When you hit a creature with an attack, you can expend a spell slot to force them to succeed on a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it loses half of its movement speed. If you score a critical hit, its speed is reduced to 0. You can concentrate on this as if you are concentrating on a spell for 1 minute. You can only have 1 creature affected by this at the same time.

If you spend 250 gp worth of materials (e.g.: the blood of a fiend killed under the moonlight, an enchanted whetstone, etc.) and perform a 10 minute ritual with those materials, you can end the {@condition petrified} condition on a creature.

You learn the {@spell mending} cantrip, and it doesn't count against your known cantrips. It is a cleric cantrip for you. You choose a portion of dirt or stone that you can see within 60 ft. and that fits within a 1-foot cube. You manipulate it and cause it to have shapes and writings appear on them, or make a surface made of stone (5-foot cube) difficult terrain for 10 minutes.

Your unarmed melee attacks deal double damage to objects. Additionally, once per day as a bonus action, you can make your hands take on a hard, marblelike form. While like this, you can make two unarmed melee attacks when you take the {@action Attack} action; these unarmed strikes use your Wisdom modifier and deal {@damage 1d6} + your Wisdom modifier bludgeoning damage. Your hands revert to their original form immediately after you make your unarmed attacks, or after a number of minutes equal to your Wisdom modifier. You can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Painting
entries: Your connection with colors, light, paintings, drawings, and the visible world increases significantly. You have proficiency with {@item painter's supplies|PHB} and have access to the following abilities:

items: You learn the {@spell minor illusion} cantrip. It's a cleric cantrip for you, and it doesn't count against the cantrips you know; you can also cast the {@spell silent image} spell at will; it also doesn't count against the spells you can prepare each day.
You have advantage on ability checks to detect illusions.

You can invoke your divine inspiration by spreading the colorful world of the canvases to your enemies or your allies. You learn the {@spell color spray} spell, which does not count against the number of spells you know. You can cast it at 1st level without expending a spell slot or material components once per long rest.

entries: Select a color that you can see within 120 ft. of you. For the next 10 minutes, each creature carrying this color within 60 ft. of you is affected by one of the following effects. You can use this a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier and regain all expended uses on a long rest.

items: They must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, they experience the illusions chosen by you as if they were real. Their reaction towards the chosen illusions are determined by the GM. They remain affected until they are no longer carrying the chosen color or until they leave your 60 ft. range. On a successful save, the target is immune to this effect for 24 hours.
All have advantage against being {@condition charmed}.
All have advantage on {@skill Stealth} checks.

subclassFeature.name: Music
entries: Either by singing or playing an instrument (or both), you invoke the divine notes that fill your heart with devotion and bring down wrath upon your enemies. You gain proficiency in a musical instrument of your choice and gain the abilities below. You have access to these abilities as long as you can speak.

items: You ignore somatic components for cleric spells.

entries: You gain the ability to use the following Orisons. You can use them a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and regain expended uses when you finish a long rest. You can also use one of them if you expend a spell slot.

items.name: Stunning Orison:
entries: As an action, you force an enemy that can hear your music within 60 ft. to succeed on a Wisdom saving throw; on a failure, they can only use one of the following for its next turn: bonus action, action, or reaction.

items.name: Charming Orison:
entries: As an action, you force an enemy that can hear your music within 60 ft. to succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or they can't attack an ally of your choice, can't target them with a harmful or negative affecting spell, or include them in a harmful spell or similar effect until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Dancing
entries: Your devotion and dedication can't fit in your body and must be expressed with divine movements. You gain the following abilities:

items: Your movement speed increases by 10 ft.
Your Armor Class increases by 2 unless your speed becomes 0.
When you are forced to make a saving throw other than Wisdom, you add your Wisdom modifier to the roll.

subclassFeature.name: Actions of the Wise
entries: You gain proficiency in a Charisma skill of your choice. You can use Wisdom instead of Charisma for that skill, representing your mental fortitude and confidence in your divine cause.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Expression of Desires
entries: Starting at Level 2, you can simply gaze into someone's soul and understand it better. You force a creature within 5 ft. of you to succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC or you learn their alignment and their intent toward you. If they fail by 5 or more, they speak aloud a desire from their heart that they are reluctant to share with most people.

subclassFeature.name: Allure of the Art
entries: By level 6, your abilities in your pursuit have flourished greatly. Your chosen aspect gets more powerful in the following ways:

entries.name: Sculpture
entries: Your connection with the myriad shapes and grains of stone increases.

Two times a day, you can attempt to touch a creature with a melee spell attack. On a hit, it is marked by you and starts to become {@condition petrified}. If you hit the marked creature two more times in the next minute, it is completely {@condition petrified}. Your first hit causes the creature to lose 10 ft. of movement until the end of your next turn, and the second hit causes the creature to lose half of their movement. On the third hit, makes the target completely {@condition petrified} for 1 hour. If you expend a 3rd level spell slot right after the third hit as a reaction, the {@condition petrified} condition's duration can be increased up to 8 hours.

entries.name: Painting
entries: Your way with the colors of the world greatly increases.

When you choose a color not carried or worn by creatures, you can choose an object or surface within 60 ft. of you. It may act as a point of origin for your spells for 1 minute; for example, even if you are 20 ft. away from a creature who is within 5 ft. of the selected point, you can cast a touch spell on it. In addition, you can cause a 10-foot cube surface or wall that has the chosen color to be affected by one of the options below:

items: It is ignited by fire. Any creature within 5 ft. of the area must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 2d6} fire damage and {@damage 2d6} radiant damage or half as much on a successful save.
If it's a surface, it is covered with ice. It is now difficult terrain, and creatures that spend at least 5 ft. of movement there must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or fall {@condition prone}.

You can make any shape, color, writing or similar appear for 10 minutes. It can be a moving picture, but it can't leave the area of effect. For example, you can simulate a devil's mouth that is moving.

entries: In addition, when you cast a spell, you can ignore verbal components. You can do so two times and regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Music
entries: Your song reaches the clouds and carries the tone of your devotions.
When you use an Orison, you can expend a spell slot to increase its duration to 1 minute, but you must concentrate on it as if you are concentrating on a spell, and you must be able to speak.

entries.name: Dancing
entries: Your movements carry the essences of your divinity better than before.
You can take the {@action Dodge} action as a bonus action on your turn unless your speed is 0.

subclassFeature.name: Pursuit of Greatness
entries: Rather than taking an Allure of the Art ability, you can choose another aspect from Level 1: Beauty of the Art.

subclassFeature.name: Blessed by the Art
entries: Your artistic expression affects your battle prowess. When a creature takes damage from one of your cantrips or weapon attacks, you can also deal {@damage 1d8} radiant damage to that creature. Once you deal this damage, you can't use this feature again until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Arte Magnifica
entries: The power of expression is supreme within you, and it cannot be contained. You can invoke a word as an action to restore all of your expended spell slots that are 5th level or lower. For each slot that was not expended when you use this feature, you gain 2 temporary hit points for each level that is unused. For example, if you have 4 of the 1st level spell slots and 1 of the 3rd level spell slots that were unexpended when you use this feature, you gain 14 temporary hit points. Alternatively, you can give these temporary hit points to an ally of your choice within 60 ft. of you that you can see.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Benandanti
entries: When the malandanti arrived long ago and began destroying people's crops and livestock, the benandanti rose to combat them. As those baleful witches rode their sorghum brooms and spread ill fortune, the benandanti wielded fennel wands and took to the skies, in animal forms or riding animal spirits, and in so doing kept the evil at bay.

You are a member of the circle of “Good Walkers,” benandanti, gentle yet vigilant folk who travel out of their bodies to struggle against the malandanti, malevolent witches who threaten to destroy the crops and livelihoods of the folk of Friuli, a region in Venice's mainland domains.. Originally your Circle could only perform these rites while sleeping at night, but over the years, as strife has encircled the land, your community has tapped into more powerful magic and found ways to extend spirit shifts to waking moments as well.

Now the tradition has grown even further afield beyond the borders of Friuli as the specter of evil has metastasized: you may have joined the circle after you were born with a caul and chosen. Perhaps you joined and trained as an apprentice. Or perhaps you were a druid of a different land, and upon arriving in Terraferma, you saw fit to join a more pressing fight against darkness.

subclassFeature.name: Circle Spells
entries: Your powers unleashed by your soul and ability to influence the material realm grant you access to certain spells. At 2nd level, you learn the {@spell chill touch} cantrip. At 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th level you gain access to the spells listed for that level in the Circle of Benandanti Spells table.

Once you gain access to one of these spells, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn't appear on the druid spell list, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you.

entries.caption: Circle of Benandanti Spells
rows: 3rd
{@spell detect evil and good}, {@spell moongaze|EchoesOfRenaissance}
5th
{@spell moonbeam}, {@spell adept ears|EchoesOfRenaissance}
7th
{@spell dreamcatcher|EchoesOfRenaissance}, {@spell sense intent|EchoesOfRenaissance}
9th
{@spell Ficino's unity of the soul|EchoesOfRenaissance}, {@spell freedom of movement}

subclassFeature.name: Spirit Shift
entries: Starting at 2nd level, your power over your spirit is unleashed on the material world. You gain the ability to temporarily leave your body and act as your spirit or a version of your wildshape. As a bonus action during your turn in combat, you can transport your spirit up to 30 ft. away from your body. Your body stays stationary (its speed is 0) and cannot act independently of your spirit. It can take damage as normal. Your spirit form gains your movement types and speed..

In your Spirit Form, you are resistant to piercing, slashing, and bludgeoning damage from nonmagical sources. You can attack or cast spells while in Spirit Form, and your Spirit Form has hit points equal to your druid level + your Wisdom modifier. You can enter the Spirit Form a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier + 1 before taking a long rest. If you transport into a Wild Shape form, it does not count against your Wild Shape uses while in Spirit Form. At the end of your next turn, your spirit must return to your body. Any excessive damage to your Spirit Form does not transfer to your original body.
Your attacks in this form are considered magical even if your weapons normally are not.

{@b Optional Feature for all Druids:} They can use their {@b Wild Shape} to turn into a specific spirit shape by following the rules of Wild Shape stated in the core rules. Each time their proficiency bonus increases, they can choose one more shape that they can turn into.

subclassFeature.name: Spirit Ascendant
entries: Your Spirit Form grows in power as your devotion to protecting the people and the harvest does. You can use Spirit Shift while in your Wild Shape form.
In addition, choose one from the following options when you enter your Spirit Form:

entries.name: Spirit of Reunion:
entries: {@b } If you are within 60 ft. of your body while in Spirit Form when it ends, your body is teleported to the point your spirit occupies and you are reunited with your body.

entries.name: Spirit of Retribution:
entries: {@b } When your spirit returns to your body, creatures caught in the line your spirit travels must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 3d10} force damage, half on a success.

entries.name: Spirit of Sanctuary:
entries: {@b } While your spirit is outside your body, your physical form has a protective caul around it. This makes it harder for enemies to target your physical form, and any enemies which do target it will pay the price. Enemies have disadvantage on attack rolls against your original body, and if an attacker hits your body, they must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or take {@damage 4d6} psychic damage as your caul attempts to suffocate them. They take half damage on a successful save.

entries.name: Spirit of Recovery:
entries: {@b } While your spirit goes forth from your body or returns, you can choose any allies within 5 ft. of the line your spirit travels, and they regain hit points equal to your druid level.

subclassFeature.name: Spirit of Night's Reach
entries: By the time you reach Level 10, your Spirit Form grows ever more powerful. You can choose two abilities from Level 6 when you enter a Spirit Form.
You are now able to pick up small objects while in your Spirit Form.
Additionally, by tapping into the night visions of your Circle, your powers have become stronger in darkness:

items: Your spirit can now travel up to 60 ft. from your body.

You can now choose to stay away from your body for longer periods of time. As a bonus action, you can return. You can stay away from your body for a number of minutes equal to your Wisdom modifier. If you want to extend your time as a spirit beyond that, you run the risk of harming yourself. Once your spirit shift time is expended, you begin taking damage until you return to your body. For the first minute you are not back in your body, you take {@damage 1d6} psychic damage, and the damage increases by {@damage 1d6} for each passing minute. You can't regain hit points until you return to your body.

subclassFeature.name: Spirit Transcendent
entries: At Level 14, you stand as an epitome of the good walkers and gain the following benefits:

items: You can now fly as part of your Spirit Shift. Your flying speed is equal to your walking speed.

You can stay out of your body for a number of days equal to your Wisdom modifier. If you want to extend your time as a spirit beyond that, you run the risk of harming yourself. Once your spirit shift time is expended, you have a number of minutes equal to your Constitution modifier to return, otherwise you risk organ failure and death. After the time is up, you must succeed on a DC 20 Constitution saving throw or take one level of {@condition exhaustion} each round.

Your spirit is wreathed in the primordial power of the moon in the face of darkness, of spring in the face of a late frost. Once per day while in Spirit Form, you can erupt in a shimmering caterwaul of energy. As a bonus action, choose a number of creatures equal to your Wisdom modifier within 60 feet of you. These creatures must make a Wisdom saving throw or take {@damage 5d10} psychic damage and {@damage 5d10} force damage, half on a success. Additionally, those creatures who failed the save find their souls have left their bodies momentarily, and they are {@condition stunned} until the end of their next turn.

subclassFeature.name: The Pavesarii
entries: The ground shakes with the thundering of rapidly approaching hooves and boots. As the enemy crests the ridge into view, you slam your pavise shield into the earth in front of you. As you quickly load your crossbow, you whisper an incantation. Suddenly, the image on your shield shimmers and grows into a huge, illusory dragon, sparking panic and confusion amongst the onrushing cavalry. Horses buck their riders, and in the tumult, you find your target and let loose your bolt.

You are a Pavesarii, an expert in using the pavise tower shield as a mobile battle station. With origins on the battlefields of the Classical era, the late Middle Ages and Renaissance have taken the shield and bowman combination to new lethal heights, and you have taken it one step further, imbuing your attacks and defense with arcane prowess.

subclassFeature.name: Steadfast Aegis
entries: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain certain abilities that can change the tides of a battle, and you gain a tower shield. You also can use Strength when attacking with a crossbow instead of Dexterity.

entries.name: Bonding with the Shield
entries: You can spend 10 minutes with a tower shield to bond with it magically. If you are not willing, nothing can make you drop the shield. If it is somehow more than 10 ft. away from you, you can summon it back to your free hand as a reaction. You can don the shield with the same reaction.

entries.name: Solid Defense
entries: Your skills with tower shields are legendary. While holding a tower shield, it grants +3 Armor Class instead of +2.

As a bonus action, you can slam your tower shield into the ground and gain cover for your attacks. When you do so, ranged attacks against you are counted as if you are behind three quarters cover until the start of your next turn. In doing so, your movement speed is halved.

subclassFeature.name: Shield Stratagems
entries: Your shield can be used for nearby crowd control or to gain an advantage on the battlefield. As a bonus action you can choose one of the following, and you can do this a number of times equal to your Strength modifier before taking a short or long rest:

items.name: Staggering Bash:
entries: {@b } Make a melee attack against a target with your shield. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage. If you rolled 16 or more on the d20 when you hit the target, the target's Armor Class is reduced by an amount equal to your Strength modifier until the start of its next turn.

items.name: Abolishing Bash:
entries: {@b } Make a melee attack with your shield against a target who cast a spell in their last turn. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage. If you rolled 16 or more on the d20 when you hit the target, the target can't speak until the start of your next turn. If it is concentrating on a spell, it has disadvantage on the Constitution saving throw against your damage.

subclassFeature.name: Shimmering Aegis
entries: Your magical bond with your tower shield grows. Choose two of the following spells. Your DC for any spell effects is: 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice): {@spell color spray}, {@spell mirror image}, {@spell entangle}, {@spell faerie fire}, {@spell grease}, {@spell heat metal}, or {@spell hold person}.
You can cast each of the spells once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Inspiring Aegis
entries: You may choose two more spells from the Shield spell list. In addition, your shield can shed even more powerful auras. Choose one of the following from the Upgraded Spell List. You can cast it once per day: {@spell hallucinatory terrain}, {@spell cloudkill}, {@spell ice storm}, {@spell insect plague}, {@spell confusion} (5th level).

entries.name: Upgraded Shield Stratagems
entries: At Level 10, your Staggering Bash and Abolishing Bash now do damage equal to {@damage 1d8} + your Strength modifier. You also gain a bonus to your speed equal to your Strength Modifier when you perform one of the Stratagems.

subclassFeature.name: Commanding Aegis
entries: Your shield now stands as a rallying call for your allies and a symbol of terror for your foes. You can choose one more spell from the Upgraded Spell List. Also, as a bonus action, you can cast {@spell heroism} at 5th level. You can do this a number of times equal to your Strength modifier. You regain all uses of {@spell heroism} when you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Enraged Shield Stratagems
entries: Your Staggering Bash and Abolishing Bash now have the potential to cause extreme physical or psychological harm. Your damage for these abilities now equals {@damage 1d10} + your Strength modifier. In addition, if you score a critical hit with your shield, roll a {@dice d10}. Consult the following Shield Effects Table for the special damage effect to the target.

entries.caption: Shield Effects Table
rows: You knock the enemy's weapon out of their hand. If they have two weapons, you choose which weapon is knocked loose.
Your shield strikes a critical blow to one of your target's arms, breaking it. That arm is now useless until that target can be healed and take a long rest.

Your shield strikes a critical blow to one of your target's legs, breaking it. The target's speed is now halved, and they take {@damage 3d10} piercing damage at the start of every turn for a number of rounds equal to your Strength modifier.
Your shield hits the target with stored magic coursing through it. The target becomes fall under the effect of the {@spell polymorph} spell. The GM chooses the form for the enemy.
The target becomes the center of a {@spell delayed blast fireball}.
The target becomes the center of a {@spell circle of death} spell, targeting only your enemies, including the target.
The target becomes the center of a {@spell divine word} spell, and you choose the new targets within range.
The target is under the effect of the {@spell flesh to stone} spell.

You knock the target out. They are {@condition incapacitated} for 1 minute, and cannot be woken up by normal means: only damage or a spell that removes deleterious effects, such as {@spell lesser restoration} or {@spell remove curse}, can rouse the target before the 1 minute is up.

The target takes {@damage 8d10 + 40} necrotic damage that can't be reduced in any way. This damage also reduces their hit point maximum by an amount equal to the damage dealt until they finish a long rest. The target is decapitated if it dies from this damage.

subclassFeature.name: Paramount Aegis
entries: Your ability to sway a battlefield with your magical shield has reached unparalleled levels. Choose one of the following spells. You can cast it once per day without needing a spell slot: {@spell sunburst}, {@spell incendiary cloud}. You can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Ultimate Shield Stratagems:
entries: Your shield now deals damage equal to {@damage 1d12} + your Strength modifier. In addition, if you roll an 18 or higher on your shield attack, it counts as a critical hit. On a critical hit, you can now roll twice on the Shield Effects Table and choose which effect you want to occur.

subclassFeature.name: Way of the Marionette
entries: A sudden feeling of power rushes from your heart as the crowd cheers. You are away from your body, extending through strings to objects designed in the shape of humanoids. You control them, you even give them life; they act with your will and do not question your orders. You are powerful with your strings, and they are powerful with your breath.

You see the strings of the world like no one can. You always felt your ability to move within the strings and move them yourself. The streets welcomed you as an artist, and the shadows saluted you for the strings you attached to the darkness. Your inner connection with the world, and your manifestation of Ki, is unleashed with your ability to control things around you: objects and humans alike.

subclassFeature.name: The Strings Unseen
entries: When you reach 3rd level in this class, your natural attunement with the strings of the world enhances. You can spend your Ki points when you hit a creature with an attack. The numbers in parentheses designate the Ki points you must spend, and the text explains the ability.

items: {@b (1)} By spending a Ki point as a bonus action, you can force the creature to succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Ki save DC or fall under the effects of the {@spell command} spell without expending a spell slot. You can only target one creature per turn.

{@b (1)} You force them to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they can't move further than 30 ft. away from you. Whenever they try to, they take {@damage 1d4} psychic damage. This effect lasts for 1 minute, but the creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns.
{@b (1)} The creature has disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity ability checks until the end of your next turn.
{@b (2)} The creature has disadvantage on Strength and Dexterity saving throws until the end of your next turn.

entries: In addition, you have advantage against being {@condition charmed} and spells that belong to the enchantment school.

subclassFeature.name: Manipulated Strings
entries: When you reach 3rd level in this class, your ability to infuse items with a part of your soul reaches to inanimate objects. You can use your bonus action to manipulate objects from afar, like a puppet master. However, you can't deal damage with such objects. The objects must be within 45 ft. of you, and must not weigh more than 20 pounds.

subclassFeature.name: The Mindbind
entries: When you reach 6th level, your strings go deep within one's soul and mind. When you hit a creature with an attack and spend 2 Ki Points, you can force the creature to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature's mind is clouded with your strings; it can't discern friends from foes and spends its action to make an attack. You can exclude 2 creatures from the attacks. If you spend more Ki points, you can exclude one more creature for each Ki point spent. This process lasts for 1 minute, but the creature repeats the saving throw at the end of each of its turns.
In addition, you can cast the {@spell hold person} (2), {@spell charm monster} (4), and {@spell dominate beast} (4) spells by spending the Ki points designated in the parentheses.

subclassFeature.name: The Soulbind
entries: When you reach 11th level in this class, your ability to reach deep into one's soul with your strings increases further. By spending 5 Ki Points, you can cast the {@spell dominate person} spell. Even if you or your allies are fighting with the creature, it does not have advantage on the save.

subclassFeature.name: Total Domination
entries: When you reach 17th level in this class, you stand at the zenith of marionette mastery. You can spend an extra 2 Ki points once to extend the {@spell dominate person} spell to another creature within range.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of the Embertide
entries: Dating back to pre-Christian times of feasting and the progression of seasons, The Ember Days are three special days of the Western Christian calendar dedicated to prayer, fasting, and helping the needy. However, the importance of those days stretches deeper than that – they are special periods when, as the season turns to a new season, defenders of peace become vital guardians of Reality. In those periods, the veil between this world and others is especially thin, and the hearts of people can be easily manipulated by evil. People hoard food, hide their true intentions, and plot and curse in the dark. The defenders of Reality, thus, must be ever vigilant in the face of phantasms and malevolent entities seeking to rend the natural order, and as a corollary any evil action that deceives, manipulates, and conspires.

As an Embertide paladin, you expose the cruelty and ugliness of the world, dragging it out of its hiding places and holding it up to the light. Your oath is one of truth in the face of lies, confronting dissembling and betrayal, and upholding the importance of truth, however illusory it may seem.

entries.name: Tenets of the Embertide
entries: {@b Truth in Words} - Speak honestly and directly. Strive to never be dishonest in words unless revealing the truth would lead to the pain of the helpless.
{@b Truth in Actions} - Let your honesty guide others to truthfulness. Combat the ugly and the enemies of reality, and show their true colors.
{@b Reveal and Reflect Danger} - Endeavor to combat evil hidden behind disguises, and reveal it for its true face, be they mundane or supernatural.

subclassFeature.name: Oath Spells
entries: You gain oath spells at the levels listed.

entries.caption: Oath of the Embertide Spells
rows: 3rd
{@spell comprehend languages}, {@spell moonflare|EchoesOfRenaissance}
5th
{@spell detect thoughts}, {@spell adept ears|EchoesOfRenaissance}
9th
{@spell sense intent|EchoesOfRenaissance}, {@spell dispel magic}
13th
{@spell blight}, {@spell locate creature}
17th
{@spell wall of force}, {@spell hold monster}

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity
entries: At level 3 you gain the following Channel Divinity options:

entries.name: Expose the Grotesque
entries: You can use your Channel Divinity to discern the true nature of creatures you believe to be hiding in plain sight. As an action, you can choose a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). These creatures make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, any creatures targeted that are shapechangers immediately revert to their original form, take {@damage 1d10} radiant damage, and have disadvantage on attacks against you and your allies for 1 minute. Any creatures who are not shapechangers instead start growing painful spines and tentacles, revealing their ugliness for all to see, and take {@damage 1d10} psychic damage. Their speed is halved, and they have disadvantage on attacks for 1 minute. After 1 minute, if the non-shapechanging targets are not dead, they lose their new appendages..

entries.name: Bolster the Faithful
entries: You can use your Channel Divinity to protect your allies from the lies and manipulations of evildoers around you. Choose a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). For the next 10 minutes, you and the chosen creatures cannot have your minds read and have advantage on Wisdom checks and saving throws.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Unveiling
entries: Your aura castigates any who would seek to strike at you with hidden evil. When you or friendly creatures within 10 ft. of you are hit by a melee attack for the first time in combat, the attacker must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the attacker takes {@damage 1d8} psychic damage and is covered in painful boils and burns which deal an additional {@damage 1d6} acid damage at the start of each of their subsequent turns for 1 minute if they do not receive magical healing.

In addition, you can use your reaction whenever a creature is hit within your aura. This time, the attacker takes psychic damage equal to your Charisma modifier. You can use this feature in this way a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier and regain expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 ft.

subclassFeature.name: Withering Abolition
entries: You gain the ability to root out even greater forms of rot and deceit, exposing them for all to see. Any {@condition invisible} creatures who make a melee attack against you do not have advantage against you, as you can sense their presence just before they strike. Moreover, as a reaction you can make a melee attack against the attacker. On a hit, you can forego damage and impose a mutation on the creature. If it fails a Constitution saving throw, it is turned into a barbling mass of boils and tentacles. Each boil's popping lets out an impotent wheeze, and while in this form, the creature is {@condition incapacitated}. The creature can repeat the saving throw if it takes damage and at the start of each of its subsequent turns; on a success it reverts to its normal form but takes {@damage 1d10} psychic damage.

subclassFeature.name: Immolate the Vile
entries: You erupt in a glorious conflagration of holy light, extinguishing all artifice and subterfuge. As an action you can transform into a burning corona of holy light for 1 minute.

items: You gain resistance to all damage.
You can cast the {@spell sunbeam} spell without expending a spell slot or needing it on your spell list.

All shapechangers revert to their original form when they come within 30 ft. of you, and all {@condition invisible} creatures within 60 ft. of you have to make a Constitution saving throw or become visible and take {@damage 1d10} psychic damage.

You can choose a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier. They must make a Constitution saving throw or transform into a grotesque creature reflecting their worst traits. It is up to the GM what final form these creatures take. While in this form, they are {@condition incapacitated}. They can repeat the saving throw at the start of each of their turns, and on a success they revert to their original form, but they take {@damage 2d8} + your Charisma modifier in psychic damage when they do so.

subclassFeature.name: Tide Guardian
entries: You scan the horizon, noticing imperceptible shifts in the movements of the water as you watch the movements of enemy vessels. Suddenly, the faint scent of ambergris and sulfur hits your nostrils, and your eyes dart to the right. You slide down the rigging and alert your shipmates: deep below the surface of the waves, a monster stirs. You are ready for it.

Perhaps you were a member of the Ottoman navy or Barbary corsairs, or the Genoese or Venetian navies. Or maybe you hail from commercial origins, as a fisherperson or merchant, or underneath the waves. Or perhaps you came to the sea later and fell in love with the mesmerizing blue of the Adriatic. You have committed yourself to traveling the waves and protecting the peoples who make the sea their home. You revere the sea in all its temperaments and help guard against evil incursions above or beneath the waves.

entries.name: Expert Swimmer
entries: When you choose this Archetype, you gain a swimming speed of 40 feet if it is not higher already.

entries.name: Weapon Expert
entries: You have a pool of Guardian Points equal to 2 times your proficiency bonus. For the rest of the day, whenever you miss an attack roll, you can use any number of Guardian Points for the attack roll and potentially turn the miss into a hit. Your expended points return when you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Long Sight
entries: You double your proficiency bonus in Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks if you do not double it from another source, such as Expertise. If you do, choose another skill from Wisdom to double your proficiency bonus.

entries.name: Arcane Bloom
entries: You learn {@spell Barbarossa's underwater vitality|EchoesOfRenaissance} cantrip and one other druid cantrip of your choice. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability modifier for both cantrips.

subclassFeature.name: Tide Guardian Magic
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you learn an additional spell when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Tide Guardian Spells table. The spell counts as a ranger spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of ranger spells you know.

entries.caption: Tide Guardian Spells
rows: 3rd
{@spell swim|EchoesOfRenaissance}, {@spell Barbarossa's tidal heave|EchoesOfRenaissance}
5th
{@spell Barbarossa's cold dispersion|EchoesOfRenaissance}, {@spell mirror image}
9th
{@spell call lightning}, {@spell glass explosion|EchoesOfRenaissance}
13th
{@spell control water}, {@spell ice storm}
17th
{@spell cone of cold}, {@spell conjure elemental} (air or water)

subclassFeature.name: Speaker of the Waves
entries: Your tie to the seas grows even stronger, and your ability to conjure its fury and passion intensify.

entries.name: Improved Swim
entries: Your swimming speed increases by 10 ft. You can also use a bonus action to {@action Dash} or {@action Disengage} when underwater or on water surface.

entries.name: Expert Dive
entries: You can cast {@spell water breathing} without expending a spell slot. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Wave Skipping
entries: You can cast {@spell water walk} targeting yourself once per day. The spell is added to your spell list and doesn't count against the number of spells you know.

entries.name: Marine Friends
entries: You can cast the {@spell speak with animals} spell without expending a spell slot. It counts as a ranger spell for you, and you do not need it on your spell list. You can cast it without expending a spell slot a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier and expended uses are restored when you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Increased Aim
entries: Once per day, after seeing the roll but before the GM lets you know the result of the attack roll, you can add +10 to the result if the attack was made with a weapon you are proficient with.

subclassFeature.name: Whelm and Woe
entries: You tap into the infinite power of the ocean depths.

entries.name: Enhance Expert Dive
entries: You can now cast {@spell Barbarossa's floating materials|EchoesOfRenaissance} once per day without expending a spell slot. You also have advantage on any check related to pulling or pushing a creature into water, though the creature can be no more than one size larger than you.

entries.name: Drowning Attack
entries: When you hit with your Increased Aim feature, you can now attempt to capture the target in a 15 ft. watery sphere if it is no more than one size larger than you. After you deal damage with the weapon, the creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be trapped in an orb of water. The creature is considered out of breath and has a number of rounds equal to its Constitution modifier before it drowns if it cannot breathe underwater. At the start of each of the creature's turns, it takes {@damage 1d8} bludgeoning damage and {@damage 1d8} cold damage, and then it can make a Strength saving throw to get out of the sphere. The sphere pushes other creatures away from it, and you must use your concentration to keep the creature trapped in the sphere.

subclassFeature.name: Vengeance of the Seas
entries: You have become the paragon of the sea's cataclysmic power. You can cast {@spell earthquake} once without expending a spell slot and regain the ability to do so after 7 days.
Your drowning attack becomes more powerful. It now deals {@damage 1d10} bludgeoning damage and {@damage 1d10} cold damage.
Your swimming speed increases by 10 more feet.

subclassFeature.name: Carnifex
entries: A pale, stern figure with dark clothes walks slowly through the field of dead bodies. The curved blades are covered with blood, fresh from the lives just taken. The figure walks slowly, looking for signs of pain and suffering. The eyes deepen with sadness for lost lives, but they do not betray their feelings to any who might be watching. They hide their emotions behind a sense of duty, but these are not the eyes of a killer: the bandages from their fingers to elbows cover only the hardships of the road; their hood hides their seasoned hair and well-earned scars.

Souls do not disappear into the void. As a dweller on the edges where life withers and gloom is always painted with red, you know this better than most. You know the pain of suffering souls and those who die terrible deaths. Maybe you served a lord as their executioner; maybe you were a doctor who treated the heavily wounded; you may have served as a battlefield healer, or as a soothsayer in the woods. You are familiar with the passing of lives, and it is your duty to seek out the suffering ones, you are able to communicate with them better than most.

subclassFeature.name: Soul Whisperer
entries: At 3rd level, your connection with the ones that passed away manifests itself in your magic. You learn the {@spell grave whispers|EchoesOfRenaissance} and {@spell spare the dying} cantrips and can cast them at will, using your Wisdom as your spellcasting ability modifier. You can cast the {@spell speak with dead} spell once, without expending a spell slot. You can't do so until you finish a long rest. When you cast this spell, the spell's 10-day restriction becomes 30 days for you and you can ask 2 more questions.

After you cast the {@spell speak with dead} spell in this way, you gain an awareness and know if the creature has been killed or not. Each time you gain a subclass level, you gain another use of casting the {@spell speak with dead} spell this way before taking a long rest.
In addition, when you reach certain Ranger levels, you learn the following spells. They are considered Ranger spells for you, and they do not count against the Ranger spells you know

entries.caption: Carnifex Spells
rows: 3rd
{@spell fragments of death|EchoesOfRenaissance}
5th
{@spell Michelangelo's buried memories|EchoesOfRenaissance}
9th
{@spell sense spirit|EchoesOfRenaissance}
13th
{@spell Ficino's unity of the soul|EchoesOfRenaissance}
17th
{@spell hallow}

subclassFeature.name: Mercy Kill
entries: Your skills are honed in the borders of death, and you naturally enchant your attacks. When you hit a creature with a weapon, you can deal an extra {@damage 1d4} force damage to the target, which can take this extra damage only once per turn. If the creature is an undead, it takes an additional {@damage 2d4} damage.
When you kill a creature, you can choose to cast the {@spell gentle repose} spell on it immediately without using a spell slot.

subclassFeature.name: Necrotic Deny
entries: Your ability to withstand death's pure negative energy has increased with time. When you or a creature within 30 ft. of you takes necrotic damage, you can use your reaction to grant it resistance to the necrotic damage until the start of your next turn.
In addition, when you hit an undead creature with an attack for the first time, it must make a Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition frightened} of you for 1 minute or until it takes damage.

subclassFeature.name: Proper Burial
entries: The {@spell gentle repose} spell's duration is one year when you cast it or cause it to happen like you can as explained in the Mercy Kill ability.

subclassFeature.name: Necrotic Vengeance
entries: You walk easily between life and death, and you can unleash your raw power of death upon your enemies. When an ally you can see within 60 ft. of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to expend a spell slot and cause the attacker to take the same amount of damage as necrotic damage. If the damage exceeds your Ranger level + Wisdom modifier, you must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or fail this ability. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all uses of it when you take a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Sense the Grim
entries: You can concentrate your inner abilities that are dwelling in the fringes of death and life on a creature that you touch. You must make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. On a success, you know if the creature's life is going to end in the next year or not. If it's less than one year, you know it, but you don't know exactly how long. This effect takes into consideration a natural lifespan, so it does not grant divine knowledge, nor does it work like fortune-telling.

subclassFeature.name: Touch of Life
entries: You can cast the {@spell unmake the undeath|EchoesOfRenaissance} spell once, without expending a spell slot. You can't do so again until you finish a long rest. When you cast this spell, the material cost is halved for you.

subclassFeature.name: Echo Thief
entries: As magic has grown in the world, so too have its various practitioners: some study assiduously, some are born with innate magic, some draw upon nature or the divine. You, however, are of an order altogether new and unique, drawing upon the Weave of magic indirectly. You utilize the remnants of magic already cast, something unseen by most, but you have adopted a special attunement for discovering arcane echoes.

subclassFeature.name: Versatile Arcana
entries: You have learned enough about magic to have an elementary grasp of some of its precepts. Choose 2 cantrips from the Wizard spell list. You can cast these cantrips at will. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these cantrips.
In addition, you can cast {@spell detect magic} and {@spell identify} spells as rituals.

subclassFeature.name: Echo of the Weave
entries: By the time you are 3rd level in this class, you have learned to identify spells and the echoes they leave behind. When a spell is cast, it leaves behind an echo you can see or feel until the start of the caster's next turn; you can absorb that arcane energy and use it to your benefit. Check out the Echo Table below for certain levels and the echoes of spells you can absorb. If a spell fits the criteria, you can absorb the echo of a spell that is cast since the end of your last turn using your bonus action. The absorption lasts until the start of your next turn. You can't feel or see the spell if the origin is under total cover, meaning you can't absorb it even if its distance matches, and you can have only one echo absorbed at a given time. Any effects on creatures due to an Echo's effects are negated if you gain a new Echo or the Echo's duration has elapsed.
The absorption's duration increases by 1 minute each time you gain a new Subclass Feature (at levels 9, 13, 17).
The distance of a spell addresses the origin of a spell, not the point it reaches or effects.

entries.caption: Echo Table
rows: Cantrips, 1
30 ft.
45 ft.
60 ft.
90 ft.

entries: When you absorb a spell, you can improve your abilities to do one of the following while the echo remains absorbed by you:

entries.name: Magical Sneak Attack
entries: You can forgo {@damage 1d6} from your Sneak Attack dice to make your damage force damage, instead of the normal damage type of your weapon.

entries.name: Elemental Sneak Attack
entries: If you absorb a damaging spell that deals one of the damage types (acid, cold, fire, or lightning), you can change one of your Sneak Attack dice with the elemental type. For example, if you absorb a {@spell fire bolt} with your bonus action, you can change one of the {@dice 1d6|1d6s} from your Sneak Attack pool to fire damage.

entries.name: Mirror the Spell
entries: You can cast the spell you absorbed with your bonus action. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and regain expended uses when you finish a long rest. The spell uses your spellcasting ability and if it requires concentration, you must concentrate on it. If the spell requires costly components, you must provide them as well, otherwise you can't ignore material components if there is no cost. If the spell was cast on a higher level than normal, it's counted as the lowest possible level.

entries.name: Enhance Magical Defenses
entries: You can use your reaction when you make a saving throw against a spell. The spell's echo lets you add {@dice 1d6} to the saving throw if you fail.

entries.name: Improved Cunning Action
entries: The next Cunning Action you take lets you choose two options from the list of available options, but you can't choose the same two options. You can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest. After 9th level, you can use this ability without needing to rest each time you take a Cunning Action.

subclassFeature.name: Edge of the Arcane
entries: By the time you reach level 9 in this class, your understanding of the Weave has increased greatly. You have advantage on saving throws against spells or other magical effects.

In addition, when you hit a creature with an attack roll with a successful Sneak Attack, you can forgo using your Sneak Attack damage dice; if you do so, you can force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it can't cast spells or activate magical objects. Additionally, if it was concentrating on a spell, it loses concentration. This effect remains for 1 minute on the creature. At the end of each of its turns, it can repeat the saving throw to be free from the effect. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and regain expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Additionally, the absorption's duration increases by 1 minute.

subclassFeature.name: Resonating Awe
entries: At 13th level, your expertise in harvesting the echo of magic has blossomed to even greater heights. When you absorb an echo of a spell, you have these two options:

items.name: Perfect Strike:
entries: You don't need to have advantage against a target to make a Sneak Attack while you have this spell echo. You can't use Sneak Attack if you have disadvantage on the roll.

items.name: Precise Strike:
entries: You can instantly expend the echo to grant yourself a bonus on one attack roll you make this turn equal to the spell's level (+1 bonus if it's a cantrip).
You can use these features a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and regain expended uses when you finish a long rest.
Additionally, the absorption's duration increases by an additional minute, and you can absorb an echo with a free action instead of a bonus action.

subclassFeature.name: Perfect Echo
entries: When you absorb a spell and cast it, you can use the spell attack bonus or spell save DC of the original caster if it's higher than your spellcasting ability.
In addition, while you have a spell absorbed, you have access to two new reactions: Echo Blast and Echo Shift.

entries.name: Echo Blast
entries: Each creature within 5 ft. of you must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Spell save DC or take {@damage 4d8} force damage, or half as much on a success.

entries.name: Echo Step
entries: You can teleport to a location within 5 ft. of the origin of the last spell you absorbed echo from. Additionally, the absorption's duration increases by an additional minute.

subclassFeature.name: Malandanti
entries: The curse is in your blood. Hex is etched to your name and now is an inseparable part of it. The poison is in your soul, but it does not kill you: instead, it enhances you in devilish and formidable ways. Your journeys in the night are a part of your existence, and you walk through the night like it belongs to you.
Or you belong to it.

Malandanti are seen as the “Evil Walkers,” and during your past, their magic has gotten into you. Either you were training under a malandante witch; you or an ancestor was a victim of their rituals; or maybe you opposed them in some way, and their blood spilled on you changed you forever. In the end, you have their power.

entries.caption: Malandanti Hex Effects
rows: Some tree branches, leaves, and similar plants grow on parts of your body.
Your veins appear dark green or other dark colors.
One of your arms looks like a rotten tree branch.
You give off a scent of dead flowers after you cast a spell.
Some people are absolutely convinced that you have no pupils in your eyes.
Sometimes, when you really are irritated by someone, something very small but very annoying happens to them.

subclassFeature.name: Walker in the Night
entries: You are a creature of the night. You can see normally in darkness up to 120 ft. even if the darkness is magical and you can't be {@condition blinded}.

In addition, if there is a light source in front of you, you can use your action to put them all out if they are within 60 ft. of you and if you can see them. If the light source is magical, you can spend a sorcery point to dispel it if it's cast as a 2nd level or lower level spell. For each level above the 2nd level, you must spend an additional sorcery point to dispel the magical light.

When you use this ability, you can cast the {@spell darkvision} spell as a bonus action. If you cast it this way, its range is 30 ft. for you, but its duration is 10 minutes instead of 8 hours. For extended sorcery points, you can target one more creature for each sorcery point after the first one.

subclassFeature.name: Ill Words
entries: Your words carry the power of curses. When you cast a spell of 1st-level or higher with a verbal component, you can slightly alter the words and fill them with ill words, banes, hexes, or curses of your choice from the list below if you spend a sorcery point. The spell must include an attack roll or a saving throw for an enemy target. If you are successful (you hit or the enemy fails the saving throw), you can apply the condition on the creature. If it's an area of effect, you can choose a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier who are affected by the spell. You can't affect the same creatures again until you finish a long rest. When you have sorcery points, you can spend one sorcery point to affect a creature again (no action required to spend it).

entries.name: Wail
entries: The target screams as loud as it can, the creatures within 5 ft. of them take {@damage 1d4} psychic damage. The damage dice and the area of effect grows larger when you reach certain sorcerer levels: 5th level ({@damage 2d4}, 10 ft.), 9th level ({@damage 3d4}, 15 ft.), 13th level ({@damage 4d4}, 20 ft.), 15th level ({@damage 5d4}, 30 ft.).

entries.name: Nightmare
entries: The target cannot benefit from its next long rest due to heavy nightmares.

entries.name: Deform
entries: The target's appearance changes in a baleful way. For example, you can place a scar on the target's body, turn the target's nails yellow and twisted, or give the target bad breath.

entries.name: Veil
entries: The target hits with disadvantage until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Fell Portent
entries: The target falls {@condition prone}. When you reach 5th level, the target can't move until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Loss
entries: The target loses the possession of a nonmagical object it had before and can't find it until it finishes a long rest or the GM decides otherwise.

In addition, when you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Cursed Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells as your known spells, but they do not count against the spells you know. They are Sorcerer spells for you.

entries.caption: Cursed Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell bane}, {@spell whispering death|EchoesOfRenaissance}
3rd
{@spell darkvision}, {@spell deadly embrace|EchoesOfRenaissance}
5th
{@spell bestow curse}, {@spell speak with dead}
7th
{@spell blight}, {@spell cursed link|EchoesOfRenaissance}
9th
{@spell disrupt one's weave|EchoesOfRenaissance}, {@spell geas}

subclassFeature.name: Cursed Aura
entries: At 6th level, your connection with the hex in your blood grows stronger. You have a strong aura that activates momentarily when you spend a sorcery point. Creatures of your choice within 15 feet of you decrease {@dice 1d4} from their next attack roll or saving throw until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: The Veil
entries: At 14th level, you reach an unimaginable might with your hexes. When you expend a sorcery point, you are immune to necrotic and poison damage until the end of your next turn, and if you are hit by either of the damage types while you are immune to them, you gain the damage as healing and restore the dealt amount as hit points.

subclassFeature.name: Word of Night
entries: You learn the {@spell absolute fear|EchoesOfRenaissance} spell, and it does not count against the sorcerer spells you know. You can spend ten sorcery points to cast the {@spell absolute fear|EchoesOfRenaissance} spell without expending a spell slot. You can't cast it again on the same creature.

subclassFeature.name: Dramaturgy
entries: Your innate power comes from the spirits of artists who have come before you: spirits of the stage, of forgotten street performers, of musicians and dancers and painters. The powers imbued in you allow for bursts of explosive creativity, a mastery over light and shadow, and a keen eye for reading people. Your powers are not limited to urban environments, however: wherever creatures may have gathered to be inspired by a performance, whether it be glade or glacier, you can call upon the gathered spirits.

subclassFeature.name: Spirit Spells
entries: You learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Spirit Spells table. Each of these spells counts as a sorcerer spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of sorcerer spells you know.

entries.caption: Spirit Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell illusory taunt|EchoesOfRenaissance}, {@spell marvelous performance|EchoesOfRenaissance}
3rd
{@spell amplify feelings|EchoesOfRenaissance}, {@spell somber orb|EchoesOfRenaissance}, {@spell voice change|EchoesOfRenaissance}
5th
{@spell majestic performance|EchoesOfRenaissance}, {@spell sense spirit|EchoesOfRenaissance}
7th
{@spell magical outburst|EchoesOfRenaissance}, {@spell Ficino's unity of the soul|EchoesOfRenaissance}
9th
{@spell dream}, {@spell Rary's Telepathic Bond||Telepathic Bond}

subclassFeature.name: Explosive Epiphany
entries: Starting at level 1, as a bonus action you can summon a spirit of the stage to aid you. This spirit can take any humanoid form you wish, though it is ethereal and barely visible. The spirit cannot attack, but it can take other actions as normal.

The spirit lasts for a number of minutes equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1). When its time is up or if you end it early as a bonus action, you can have it explode as a “final bow,” dealing {@damage 1d6} radiant damage to any creatures within 5 feet.

entries.name: Summon Inspiration
entries: Starting at level 6, you can now summon {@dice 1d4} spirits. In addition, the “final bow” damage of the spirits increases to {@damage 2d6} radiant damage.

entries.name: Awe-inspiring Performance
entries: You can choose to awe a number of humanoid creatures within 30 ft. equal to the number of sorcery points you wish to spend. These targets make Wisdom saving throws. On a failure, they are under the effect of the {@spell charm person} spell for a number of minutes equal to your Charisma modifier.

entries.name: Chiaroscuro
entries: You have mastered the contrast between light and shadow, knowing when to grab the spotlight and when to hide in the dark.

items: When you are in dim light or darkness, you can cast {@spell invisibility} without expending a spell slot. You can do this a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier. If you cross into a well lit area during that time, you can continue the invisibility if you spend 2 sorcery points. You regain all uses of this ability after a long rest.

When you are in bright light, you can cast the {@spell fly} spell a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier. If you cross into dim light or darkness, you can continue to fly if you spend 2 sorcery points. You regain all uses of this ability after a long rest.

entries.name: In the Spotlight
entries: If you are under normal or bright light, you can draw attention to yourself in order to give your allies advantage. Choose a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier. Those creatures must make Wisdom saving throws. On a failed save, the creatures are dazzled by your presence and the shimmering halo of spirits around you. They are friendly towards you unless they are immune to being {@condition charmed} or you attack them. Additionally, your allies have advantage on their attacks against these targets. The charm ends after the target takes damage.

subclassFeature.name: Closing Ceremony
entries: Your summoned spirits now deal {@damage 4d6} radiant damage to creatures within a 10-foot-radius sphere when they take their final bows, but this damage does not affect you or your allies.

subclassFeature.name: Plague Doctor
entries: Your patron is a powerful being of death and disease. The motives of such entities are diverse, with some delighting in every pustule and boil which signals the growth of their power, while some may even provide remedies to contain and shape their deleterious creations, much like a sculptor shapes a masterpiece. Some see disease as a necessary aspect of life and lord over both healing and sickness in equal measure. Patrons of this sort might include Sekhmet, the Egyptian goddess of the hot desert sun, plague, chaos, war, and healing; Loviatar, the Finnish goddess of death and disease; the Nosoi of Greek myth or the Morbi of Roman mythology; Asclepius, Greek god of medicine; Apollo, Greek and Roman god of plague (amongst many other things); Babalú-Ayé, West African spirit of the earth and smallpox; Namtar, Sumerian demon of disease; the Wen Shen in Chinese mythology; Gozu Tenno in Japanese mythology; Pesta of Norwegian folklore; or powerful hags, djinns, demons, or other deities.
