entries.name: Personas
entries: These personas can be used to enrich the festival environment, or they can spark the imagination for possible quests.

entries.caption: Festival Personas
rows: {@b The Overzealous Bard} – Singing loudly and somewhat off-key, attracting (or repelling) a small crowd.
{@b The Juggling Merchant} – Selling trinkets while impressively juggling them to draw attention.
{@b The Star-Crossed Lovers} – A couple secretly meeting in the chaos of the festival.
{@b The Unlucky Gambler} – Complaining loudly about losing everything at a rigged game booth.
{@b The Masked Reveler} – Dressed extravagantly and speaking cryptically, refusing to reveal their face.
{@b The Pickpocket Apprentice} – A nervous child trying (and failing) to lift someone's coin purse.
{@b The Firebreather} – Putting on a daring show, surrounded by an adoring crowd.
{@b The Exotic Pet Owner} – Parading a brightly feathered bird or strange animal through the streets.
{@b The Town Crier} – Enthusiastically proclaiming the next big event or piece of juicy news.
{@b The Harried Parent} – Frantically searching for their mischievous child lost in the crowd.
{@b The Mysterious Fortune Teller} – Reading palms or cards from a dimly lit booth.
{@b The Wandering Minstrel} – Playing a soft tune in the corner, unbothered by the commotion.
{@b The Cheerful Blacksmith} – Displaying small, decorative metalworks, chatting with everyone passing by.
{@b The Barefoot Dancer} – Twirling gracefully in the square, their joyful movements infectious.
{@b The Puppeteer} – Performing a comical or dramatic tale with intricate marionettes.
{@b The Drunken Reveler} – Stumbling through the crowd, overly friendly, and hilariously trying to join every conversation.
{@b The Wide-Eyed Tourist} – Marveling at everything with an air of naive wonder.
{@b The Festival Guard} – Standing stoically but secretly enjoying the entertainment around them.
{@b The Spicy Food Vendor} – Daring everyone to try their "inferno stew" with a cheeky grin.
{@b The Grumpy Elder} – Complaining about the noise and reminiscing about "better festivals" in their youth.

entries.name: The Regatta
entries: The annual gondola race, the Regatta, is entertainment for spectators but serious competition for the participants. The prize is the illustrious red pennant, a large bag of coins, and bragging rights until the next big regatta.

The race starts near the Sant'Elena church, east of the Doge's Palace in the Castello district; heads up the Grand Canal past the Rialto Bridge until the canal's terminus near the Church of Corpus Domini, before turning back and finishing in front of Ca' Foscari, a palazzo at the widest bend of the Grand Canal. In front of Ca' Foscari is a floating barge called a machina, on top of which is a rack with the pennants (red for first place, light blue for second, green for third, and yellow for fourth, with a picture of a pig on it) and monetary awards. The rowers must reach the machina and grab the red pennant to be declared the winner. There the doge and distinguished guests look on approvingly from one of the upper balconies of the Ca' Foscari, and sometimes shower the crowd with well wishes.
While the competition is more civil than the gladiator fights of old, guards do not get in the way of participants trying to prevent their opponents from winning unless it gets bloody.

In the following passage, you can simulate the gondola race by rolling on some contest rolls and tables. The race is separated into four parts: "the First Leg", "Rialto Bridge", "the Second Leg", and "the Home Stretch." indicating the events that occur consecutively throughout. An adventurer proficient with water vehicles adds their proficiency bonus on all the rolls regarding the navigation of the gondola. While adventurers are free to take individual actions as they want during the race, rolls for the gondola regarding navigation, tables, and saving throws are rolled by one adventurer with their own bonus. This adventurer doesn't have to be the same all the time and can be changed between rolls.

With slight adjustments, this racing module can be used in other settings with different racing scenarios, such as boat racing in the Bosphorus of Istanbul, horse races in the steppes of the Silk Road, or the fierce chariot races taking part in Ancient Greece.

entries.name: The Start of the Race
entries: At the start of the race, initiative is rolled to determine the launch order of the teams. For the adventurers, only roll for the highest initiative bonus. After the order of the ships is determined, they are considered to be sailing.

entries.name: Passing Opponents with Contest Rolls
entries: When adventurers want to pass another team's gondola they must succeed in a Strength check contested by their challenger gondola's Strength. Adventurers who are actively rowing the gondola add up their Strength modifiers and combine it with the gondola's contest roll. These contest rolls can be made once per race section by both the adventurers and the opponents. In the second half of the race, the closest opponent challenges back with a Constitution contest in which adventurers must respond with their Constitution ability. In a situation where adventurers have no other opponents to pass in front, gaining one place can be interpreted as opening the gap behind, equal to one gondola length.

entries.name: Usage of Magic Among the Crowd
entries: The Regatta is a famous event in the city, with many people lining the Grand Canal to watch how it unfolds. Any use of conspicuous magic would be witnessed by the whole crowd and among them highly ranked people such as the Council of Ten or the Doge himself. If the adventurers want to use magic furtively, you can have them make a Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check contested by an observer's Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check.

entries.name: Opponents
entries: Every year dozens of teams enter the Regatta but not all of them compete for absolute victory. Among many teams that race to either try themselves, display their custom gondolas, or impress a certain audience, there are some who would like to race for the pure glory of it. These fierce competitors usually distinguish themselves from others by either painting their gondolas or carrying a flag of a specific color.

entries.name: The Golden Team: The Castellani
entries: With the prow of their black gondola painted with gold, shining among other contenders, the reigning champion team is being led by the arrogant Corvetto Leone (CN human male, patron of the arts). Alongside him, four paddlers row towards the finish line under his command.

After their victory in the previous year's championship, an unpleasant rumor spread through the streets that the Golden Team owed their championship to unknown witchcraft. The team, originating from the neighborhoods of Castello, has its gondola improved by the skilled workers of the San Trovaso boat workshop. Their long continuing feud with The Nicolotti's also affects their race in the Regatta; the passion for winning and beating their rivals never abates.

entries.name: The Golden Team's Gondola
entries: When rolling for the Golden Team, apply the following bonuses: +3 for Strength, +5 for Dexterity (and Initiative), and +0 for Constitution. If the competition escalates into combat, the gondola's HP is considered 50, and its Armor Class is 12.

entries.name: The Purple Team: The Nicolotti
entries: Wounded by the previous year's defeat, the purple team wants nothing more than to defeat their rivals, the Golden Team, and show people that their previous win was a fraud. Fueled by revenge, their leader Ambrogio Vignon (CN human male, patrono delle navi, naval officer) might prioritize the Golden Team's downfall over his own team's glory.

entries.name: Purple Team's Gondola
entries: When rolling for the Purple Team, apply the following bonuses: +1 for Strength, +2 for Dexterity (and Initiative), and +1 for Constitution. If the competition escalates into combat, the gondola's HP is considered 50, and its Armor Class is 11.

entries.name: Orange Team
entries: It is said that the orange team chose their color after seeing tulips during their journey through the Ottoman Empire. This team of young adventurers (various non-evil alignments, gondoliers, journeymen) are fierce competitors, but their main goal isn't to win. They want to showcase their skills to potential patrons who would support their later expeditions.

entries.name: Orange Team's Gondola
entries: When rolling for the Orange Team, apply the following bonuses: -1 for Strength, +2 for Dexterity (and Initiative), and -1 for Constitution. If the competition escalates into combat, the gondola's HP is considered 40, and its Armor Class is 8.

entries.name: Green Team
entries: Having struggled to succeed at the Regatta in previous years, the Green Team (various non-evil alignments, commoners of Venice) is more determined than ever to showcase their true talent to Venice. Although they haven't secured a win yet, their results have steadily improved, bringing them closer to the top. While victory is their ultimate goal, they wouldn't be opposed to an offer that guarantees them a future victory, either through interference or the elimination of other teams.

entries.name: Green Team's Gondola
entries: When rolling for the Green Team, apply the following bonuses: +0 for Strength, +0 for Dexterity (and Initiative), and +0 for Constitution. If the competition escalates into combat, the gondola's HP is considered 35, and its Armor Class is 10.

entries.name: Creating Your Own Teams
entries: If your story demands more teams with various NPCs, you can always add more. Giving unique motivations to teams, enriches the roleplaying experience and provides different outcomes for each race. When altering the stats of the gondolas keep in mind that Dexterity allows teams to launch fast, Strength allows them to get past opponents, and Constitution allows them to keep rowing after a long time thereby affecting the final part of the race and the result.

entries.caption: First Leg Encounters
rows: A strong headwind arises, pushing against the gondola. Adventurers must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw to power through it, or lose one place.

A costermonger gondola carrying fruits suddenly swerves into the race path. Adventurers must succeed on a {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check to spot it early or a {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check to avoid collision, or lose two places.

An opponent team behind grapples the adventurers' gondola by throwing a rope. They slow the gondola down while quickly pulling up alongside. A successful {@dc 12} Dexterity saving throw removes the rope but opponents catch up to speed unless the saving throw result is more than 16. If the saving throw is unsuccessful, the gondola drops back one place in the order.
A merchant boat loaded with spices suddenly pulls out from a side canal. The adventurers must navigate around it with a successful {@dc 13} Wisdom saving throw or lose one place.

A narrow opening between two gondolas creates a perfect opportunity to gain some time. A successful {@dc 14} Dexterity check allows them to take the risky maneuver and gain two places. If the check fails, they lose two places due to a minor collision.
A sudden crosscurrent tests the rowers' synchronized rhythm. A successful {@dc 13} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check overcomes the drag and keeps the craft on track, gaining one place.

A sudden burst of mist falls down on the city, making the visibility awful. A successful {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check allows the adventurers to use it as an advantage, gaining one place inside the fog.
A floating debris cluster threatens to damage the oars. A successful {@dc 12} Dexterity check lets the crew quickly pull the oars up and avoid the hazard without losing momentum.
The canal narrows with the company of racing and moored gondolas, creating a bottleneck. Succeeding on a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw allows adventurers to slip through and gain one place.

A boat suddenly gets out among the moored gondolas along the canal and rams into one of the opponents making them lose places. As you pass that boat you notice a familiar face rowing it who doesn't seem surprised by the accident.

entries.name: Rialto Bridge
entries: You can roll on, or choose from, this table for each time they pass the bridge (once heading up the Grand Canal, and once heading back into the Home Stretch).

entries.caption: Rialto Bridge Encounters
rows: The bridge approaches too quickly. Adventurers must succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw or ram into the pillar of the bridge, losing two places while recovering.

A rope stretches among the support pillars under the bridge. The rope can be noticed early by adventurers with at least 12 passive Perception or a successful {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check. If the rope is unnoticed, they lose two places while maneuvering under it.
A porter on the bridge drops a heavy barrel full of spices down to the gondola. The impact causes disruption and the gondola loses one place in the order but takes no damage.

A commoner jumps down from the bridge and lands in the gondola attempting to push the adventurers into the water. The gondola slows down and loses one place in the order if he is not taken care of quickly.

Rival gondoliers try to force the adventurers' gondola into the bridge's supports. A successful {@dc 14} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) or Intelligence (Water Vehicles) check avoids the collision. Failure results in losing one place, however success results in gaining one.
The adventurers can use the bridge supports to push the gondola forward. A successful {@dc 13} Strength check results in gaining one place.
A stranger (commoner) throws a rope from the bridge offering help. If accepted, the gondola speeds up, allowing the adventurers to gain one place.

The adventurers reach alongside the opponents in the front while approaching the bridge. Since there isn't enough space in between the support pillars, the opponents ram into them while trying to squeeze alongside, allowing the adventurers to gain one place.
A successful {@dc 14} Wisdom check reveals that the canal's bend makes the fastest route along the inside. Using the gap on the furthest right allows adventurers to gain two places.
A hooded figure among the crowd seems to mumble some words and move their hands stealthily. The gondola catches a current and speeds up, gaining two places.

entries.name: Second Leg of the Race and the Home Stretch
entries: Roll twice on this Table–once for the Second Leg and once for the Home Stretch after passing the Rialto Bridge (the second time).

entries.caption: Second Leg & Home Stretch Encounters
rows: An abrupt gust of wind pushes the gondola towards one side of the canal, making adventurers lose two places. After the blow, an opponent in the rival gondola appears to be moving their hands suspiciously.
An opponent gondolier tries to sideswipe the adventurers' boat. A successful {@dc 12} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check fends them off or on a failed roll, the team loses one place.
A sudden downpour starts to fill the gondola. If at least one adventurer doesn't start emptying the water, the gondola slows down dropping one place in the order.

An opponent throws a wine bottle at the adventurers to slow them down. A successful {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw allows one to grab the bottle mid-air or on a failed save adventurers lose one place with the impact.
A broken bricola within the canal causes the gondola to scrape the bottom. Make a successful {@dc 12} Wisdom saving throw to navigate out of it quickly, or lose two places.

A wealthy patron from the spectators throws a heavy coin pouch into the water as a donation to the racers. A successful {@dc 14} Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check allows it to be reached before the pouch sinks deeper. The pouch contains 100 gold pieces.
A strange shift in gravity lifts the gondola slightly higher. While the sound rising from underwater is unsettling, the gondola gains speed, resulting in gaining one place.

A flock of birds lift off from the water as gondolas close by. The chaos reduces visibility, giving the adventurers a chance. A successful {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check allows the adventurers to capitalize on the distraction and gain one place.
The closest opponent drops one of their paddles into the water, slowing down to almost half their speed.

As the finish line approaches, spectators start to cheer the color of the adventurers' gondola. The uplifting spirit fills the Grand Canal giving the adventurers enough moral boost to row stronger and gain two places.

variantrule.name: Professions

entries.name: Core of the System
entries: The Profession System is designed to enhance the backgrounds and current occupations of player characters besides their "adventuring classes." Adventuring classes define players' core abilities and their general features from combat encounters to social situations. The Profession System is aimed at giving players opportunities to enrich their downtimes, backgrounds, non-combat activities, explorations, daily goals and occupations and their characters out of adventure days.

Characters can take up the path of a Profession between Levels 1-3 and have access to Apprentice levels of the professions if they meet the prerequisite for the intended profession. It is recommended that players should take at least two weeks of downtime to begin a Profession. It is not advised for characters to have more than one profession, as the system is not designed for multi-professions, and it could end up for characters to have unfair advantages. However, at the GM's discretion, players may take suitable perks from other professions if needed. If a character wants to start a profession at later levels, GM may let them start with more Profession Experience (PEX) depending on the earlier experiences of the adventurer. For example, if the character acts as an advisor to an important underground boss, they may start from the Journeyman rank.

PEX is the main way of progressing through the Ranks and gaining new abilities. Most of the Professions explain how to gain PEX. For example, the very first Profession designed by us–the Bounty Hunter in {@i The City of Crescent}–gains PEX through collecting bounties, and it is scaled with the Challenge Ratings of said bounties.

To improve ranks, a character must spend their PEX for the current rank's abilities (usually at least two of them), and also reach the designated PEX for the next rank and expend the experience as well. It should be noted that the rank system does not work like 5th edition class leveling; you must spend your PEX in order to rank up.

There are four ranks for each profession: Apprentice, Journeyman, Expert, and Master. Apprentice is the starting level, and there is no PEX needed to enter that profession, but investments should be made beforehand or the backstory of the character must fit the profession. Each profession has a prerequisite for it, but if a character's backstory fits, the GM may allow for the profession to be chosen.
For Journeyman rank, you must spend at least a total 100 PEX on abilities in the Apprentice rank and spend 300 PEX to reach the rank.
For Expert rank, you must spend at least a total of 200 PEX on abilities in the Journeyman rank and spend 1,000 PEX to reach the rank.
For Master rank, you must spend at least a total 400 PEX on abilities in the Expert rank and spend 5,000 PEX to reach the maximum rank.
When you spend enough PEX to reach the next rank, you can also purchase other abilities as well before advancing. In addition, you can purchase earlier abilities from lower ranks.
See {@charoption Mendicant|EchoesOfRenaissance} and {@charoption Condottiero|EchoesOfRenaissance}

spellcasting.name: Fiendish Spellcasting
headerEntries: The aamon can cast these spells without needing material components. Charisma is its spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 14}, spell attack bonus {@hit 6}):

trait.name: Shapechanger
entries: The aamon can use its action to polymorph into a Small or Medium humanoid, or back into its true form. Other than its size and speed, its statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

trait.name: A Glimpse into the Flames of the Future (1/Week)
entries: The aamon can spend a day resting in a dark place to see a vision of the future. The vision is usually distorted, twisted, evil in every way, and in most cases impossible to actually occur. The GM has the details about it, and the aamon usually tries to fulfill the vision it has seen.

trait.name: Truest Strike
entries: The aamon can cast the {@spell true strike} cantrip at will. When it casts the cantrip, the spell stays active for {@dice 1d4 + 1} rounds rather than 1 round.

trait.name: Summon Fiendish Help (1/Day)
entries: The aamon can summon {@dice 1d4 + 1} {@creature imp||imps} to serve it or to spy for it. The imps usually return to wherever they came from after 8 hours.

bonus.name: Dark Visions {@recharge 5}
entries: The aamon can mark a creature it has seen in its visions for 1 minute. The marked creature receives momentarily flashes belonging to the vision each time it takes damage and must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or fall under the effects of the {@spell crown of madness} spell. The aamon concentrates on the spell. If a creature succeeds on the saving throw or has been affected by the spell, it can't be affected or marked again until 10 minutes have passed.

action.name: Long Claws
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +6} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}15 ({@damage 3d6 + 4}) acid damage plus 4 ({@damage 1d6}) psychic damage.

monster.name: Ales Leo
languages: five of the GM's choice, two of which must be Italian and Ancient Latin

spellcasting.name: Sapiens Leo
headerEntries: Parts of its body appear more alive and its facial expressions are more conspicuous. It can innately cast these spells ({@hit +6} to hit, spell save {@dc 15}, uses Charisma as spellcasting ability):

spellcasting.name: The Guardian of the City (3/Day)
headerEntries: In the city of Venice, Ales Leo can cast {@spell remove curse}, {@spell counterspell}, or {@spell dispel magic}, using Charisma as its spellcasting ability.

trait.name: The Wise and the Brave
entries: Ales Leo has two forms: Sapiens Leo or Fortis Leo. Sapiens Leo represents times of peace, prosperity, knowledge, and advancement in science. In this form, the lion wields a tome. Fortis Leo represents times of war when the lion is shown with a sword and having courage, spirit and determination to defend the city. It can use its action to change forms between Sapiens Leo and Fortis Leo.

trait.name: Fortis Leo
entries: Parts of its body that represent a construct capture more attention. While in this form, it is considered a construct and it takes 5 fewer points of damage each time it is hit.

trait.name: Flyby
entries: Ales Leo does not provoke an opportunity attack when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Ales Leo makes two Divine Claw attacks. It can replace one of the attacks with Strong Breath or Arcane Ray.

action.name: Divine Claw
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +8} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}14 ({@damage 2d8 + 5}) bludgeoning damage plus 5 ({@damage 1d8}) radiant damage. If Ales Leo moves at least 20 feet straight toward the target immediately before the hit, the target takes an extra 13 ({@damage 3d8}) bludgeoning damage, and the target must succeed on a {@dc 18} Strength saving throw or be knocked {@condition prone} if it is a creature.

action.name: Strong Breath
entries: Ales Leo hurls a powerful magical breath in a 40-foot cone. The creatures inside must succeed on a {@dc 18} Strength saving throw or take 18 ({@damage 4d8}) bludgeoning damage and be pushed 20 ft. away and knocked {@condition prone}. On a successful save, they only take half damage and are not knocked back.

action.name: Arcane Ray
entries: {@atk rs} {@hit +6} to hit, range 60 ft., one target. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d10}) poison damage plus 6 ({@damage 1d10}) radiant damage. The target must succeed on a {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target is {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute.

monster.name: Angós
languages: understands all but can only speak Vulgar Latin and Greek

trait.name: Settlement Bound
entries: Angós is bound to a city (determined by the GM) and can't leave its borders.

trait.name: Sturdy Oarsman
entries: As long as Angós is on a waterborne vessel, it can't roll below its Strength score in Strength ({@skill Athletics}) contests made to push or pull.

trait.name: Undead Nature
entries: Angós does not require food, water, breath, or sleep. In addition, it can complete a long rest while piloting the boat.

trait.name: Unholy Vipers
entries: Whenever Angós is hit, the target that hit it must succeed on a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw or take 2 ({@damage 1d4}) poison damage plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) necrotic damage, or half on a successful save. In addition, if the target is a creature, the creature's hit point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the necrotic damage taken. This reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. The target dies if its hit point maximum is reduced to 0.

trait.name: Venomous Bargain
entries: If represented with a belonging, Angós can locate the creature that the item belongs to immediately. In order for this feature to work, the target must sacrifice a portion of hit dice of theirs and make a payment equal to a hundred times the sacrificed hit dice. For example, if a creature is asked to sacrifice 3 hit dice (i.e. 3d8) the payment is 300 gd. Other bargains can be struck with Angós, such as traveling to a place by water (inside the city), delivering a very delicate message or a package, striking a creature, or similar. The cost is up to the GM.

trait.name: Ethereal Transportation
entries: Angós, while on its boat, can travel through the city it is bound to and can reach a destination in a duration that takes 10 minutes at most due to its magical and mysterious nature. While traveling, only the creatures that it allows can see it and its boat. While using this feature, it can't collide with other ships or affect the physical world.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Angós makes two attacks with its Stygian Oar.

action.name: Stygian Oar
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +5} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d6 + 3}) bludgeoning damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) necrotic damage.

spellcasting.name: Innate Spellcasting
headerEntries: The rainbow fairy can innately cast the following spells without needing any material components. Charisma is its spellcasting ability for these spells (spell save {@dc 13}, spell attack bonus {@hit +5}):

action.name: Fairy Dust
entries: The rainbow fairy sprinkles fairy dust on a point of its choosing within 60 ft. Any creature within 20 ft. of it must succeed on a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw or take 7 ({@damage 2d6}) radiant damage or half as much on a successful save.

action.name: Magical Ward (3/Day)
entries: The fairy can grant up to three creatures that it can see within 60 ft. of it Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects for {@dice 1d4 + 1} rounds.

trait.name: Object Integrity
entries: Due to its extensive knowledge of craftsmanship, the arsenalotto deals double damage to objects and constructs if it deals bludgeoning damage.

trait.name: Innate Fixer
entries: The arsenalotto can cast {@spell mending} as a ritual.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The arsenalotto makes two melee attacks or two ranged attacks.

action.name: Light Hammer
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Dart
entries: {@atk rw} {@hit +4} to hit, range 20/60., one target. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) piercing damage.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The artisan casts one of the following spells, using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}):

trait.name: Tool Expertise
entries: The artisan has Advantage on ability checks related to its tool proficiencies.

action.name: Shortsword
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +4} to hit, reach 5ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) piercing damage.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The astronomer casts one of the following spells, using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}):

action.name: Celestial Movements
entries: The astronomer can use its action to predict the weather and celestial movements (such as an eclipse, a passing comet, or a blood moon).

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atk mw,rw} {@hit +3} to hit, reach 5ft., or range 20/60 ft., one target. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d4 + 1}) piercing damage.

spellcasting.name: Innate Spellcasting
headerEntries: The avogadore casts these spells without any material components. Its spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save {@dc 13}, {@hit +4} to hit spell attacks):

action.name: Greatsword
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) slashing damage.

action.name: Power of the Law {@recharge 5}
entries: The avogadore can innately cast the {@spell command} spell without any components (except for verbal to deliver the command word). The spell save DC is equal to 13 (spellcasting ability is Charisma).

spellcasting.name: Innate Spellcasting
headerEntries: The Borda can cast these spells innately, without needing material components. Charisma is its spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 14}, spell attack bonus {@hit +5}):

trait.name: Born in a Swamp
entries: The Borda's movement is not affected by difficult terrain made of mud, swamp or similar areas.

bonus.name: Magical Rope
entries: The Borda can manifest a magical rope with its bonus action and use it as a {@spell thorn whip} cantrip. The Borda can't manifest the rope if it is {@condition incapacitated}.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) piercing damage, plus 4 ({@damage 1d6}) acid damage.

action.name: Rope Attack
entries: {@atk rw} {@hit +5} to hit, range 40/80 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d6 + 3}) piercing damage. A creature that is hit is {@condition restrained} by the Borda. The creature can try to escape by using its action with a contested Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check. While a creature is {@condition restrained}, it takes 7 ({@damage 2d6}) piercing damage at the start of each of its turns and the Borda can pull the creature 10 ft. closer every turn as a free action.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The capitano casts one of the following spells, using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}, {@hit +4} to hit):

trait.name: Good Aim
entries: The capitano adds +2 bonus to ranged attacks.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The captain makes two attacks in any combination.

action.name: Rapier
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) piercing damage.

action.name: Pistol
entries: {@atk rw} {@hit +7} to hit, range 30/80 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) piercing damage.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The galley captain casts one of the following spells, using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}, {@hit +4} to hit):

bonus.name: Seafaring Commander {@recharge 4}
entries: The galley captain can use its bonus actions to command an ally within 60 ft. that can hear the galley captain: it can move half of its speed or make a weapon attack.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The captain makes two attacks in any combination.

action.name: Rapier
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) piercing damage.

action.name: Pistol
entries: {@atk rw} {@hit +5} to hit, range 30/80 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) piercing damage.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The plaguebeast can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Grappler
entries: It has Advantage on Strength ({@skill Athletics}) checks regarding grapple. A creature grappled by the plaguebeast takes 5 ({@damage 2d4}) poison damage at the start of its turns.

trait.name: Opportunist
entries: The plaguebeast has Advantage on Initiative rolls.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +6} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}15 ({@damage 2d10 + 4}) piercing damage plus 11 ({@damage 3d6}) poison damage.

action.name: Squeeze
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +6} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) bludgeoning damage plus 3 ({@damage 1d6}) poison damage. The creature is {@condition grappled} by the plaguebeast if it's smaller than Large. It can only have one creature grappled in this way at a time.

spellcasting.name: Innate Spellcasting
headerEntries: The fated one cast the following spells innately, without needing material components. Charisma is its spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}, spell attack bonus {@hit +4}):

action.name: Starry Strike
entries: {@atk rs} {@hit +4} to hit, range 60 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d8}) radiant damage.

action.name: Impending Fate {@recharge 6}
entries: The fated one can target a creature within 60 ft. of it. The creature must succeed on a {@dc 12} Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target is vulnerable to a damage type from the list: radiant, necrotic, or psychic damage for 1 minute or until it takes damage from that source. On a successful save, it takes 4 ({@damage 1d6}) radiant damage.

monster.name: Hidden One
languages: understands two languages of the GM's choice but can't speak

spellcasting.name: Innate Spellcasting
headerEntries: The hidden one can cast the following spells innately, without needing material components. Charisma is its spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 13}, spell attack bonus {@hit +4}):

trait.name: Radiant Ward
entries: The hidden one can cast {@spell blade ward} as a touch.

bonus.name: Radiant Bond (1/Day)
entries: The hidden one can cast {@spell warding bond} spells to a creature it can touch with a bonus action, without any material components. When it casts the spell, it gains 11 ({@damage 3d6}) temporary hit points.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The hidden one can attack twice with its Bestial Attack.

action.name: Bestial Attack
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) radiant damage.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The novice condottiero makes two longsword attacks.

action.name: Longsword
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +6} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d8 + 4}) slashing damage or 9 ({@damage 1d10 + 4}) slashing damage if used with two hands.

action.name: Heavy Crossbow

reaction.name: Precise Swordsman {@recharge 5}

action.name: Multiattack

reaction.name: Riposte {@recharge 5}
entries: When a creature misses an attack against the expert condottiero, it can use its reaction to attack the creature who missed. This attack deals additional damage ({@damage 1d4}).

trait.name: Iron Lungs

action.name: Handaxe
entries: {@atk mw,rw} {@hit +3} to hit, reach 5 ft., or range 20/60 ft., one target. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d6 + 1}) slashing damage.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The bassarid can cast the following spells, using Charisma as its spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}, spell attack bonus {@hit +4}):

trait.name: Pleasure or Pain (1/Day)
entries: The bassarid can use a minute to change a liquid from one to another. While doing so it has two options: turning a liquid into wine or turning it into a poison. If it's a wine, it tastes delicious and could make people addicted to it on repeated consumption. If it's poison, it can only be detected with a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}), Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}), or Herbalism Kit check. The poison deals {@damage 2d4} poison damage to the drinker and forces them to make a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it is {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute.

trait.name: Gear
entries: The bassarid carries two ritual daggers, one {@item potion of healing}, two vials of {@item basic poison|PHB|poison}, one Disguise Kit, and it wears hide armor.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The bassarid makes two attacks with its ritual dagger.

action.name: Ritual Dagger
entries: {@atk mw,rw} reach 5 ft., or range 20/60 ft., one target. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) piercing damage plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) poison damage. If it's a critical hit, the creature is {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The gerarae can cast the following spells, using Charisma as its spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 16}, spell attack bonus {@hit +8}):

trait.name: Pleasure or Pain (3/Day)
entries: The gerarae can use a minute to change a liquid from one to another. While doing so it has two options: turning a liquid into wine or turning it into a poison. If it's a wine, it tastes delicious and could make people addicted to it on repeated consumption. If it's poison, it can only be detected with a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}), Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}), or Herbalism Kit check. The poison deals {@damage 2d4} poison damage to the drinker and forces them to make a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it is {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute.

trait.name: Ritual Master
entries: The gerarae can cast these spells as rituals (Charisma is its spellcasting ability): {@spell alarm}, {@spell find familiar}, {@spell purify food and drink}, {@spell animal messenger}. With the GM's discretion, the gerarae could learn more ritual spells.

trait.name: Gear
entries: The gerarae carries four ritual daggers, three {@item potion of healing}, four vials of {@item basic poison|PHB|poison}, and one Disguise Kit.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The maenad makes three attacks with its ritual dagger. It can replace one of the attacks with a spell.

action.name: Ritual Dagger
entries: {@atk mw,rw} {@hit +6} to hit, reach 5 ft., or range 20/60 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d4 + 3}) piercing damage plus 7 ({@damage 3d4}) poison damage. If it's a critical hit, the creature is {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The maenad can cast the following spells, using Charisma as its spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}, spell attack bonus {@hit +4}):

trait.name: Gear
entries: The maenad carries a ritual blade, three {@item potion of healing}, four vials of {@item basic poison|PHB|poison}, and one Disguise Kit.

bonus.name: Rampage (1/Day)
entries: The maenad can enter a battle frenzy called Rampage as a bonus action. The Rampage lasts for a minute. During this minute, the maenad has Advantage on attack rolls and deals an additional damage equal to {@damage 1d6} (same damage type as the weapon they are wielding). The condition ends early if the maenad is {@condition incapacitated}.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The maenad makes two attacks with its ritual blade.

action.name: Ritual Blade
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}9 ({@damage 1d10 + 3}) slashing damage. If it's a critical hit, the creature is {@condition stunned} until the start of its next turn.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The dapifer casts one of the following spells, using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 16}, spell attack bonus {@hit +8}):

trait.name: Enchanting Aura (15-foot radius)
entries: Each creature that starts its turn in the dapifer's aura or enters it for the first time must make a {@dc 16} Wisdom saving throw or fall under the effects of the {@spell suggestion} spell. A creature that succeeds on the saving throw is immune to the effect for 24 hours.

trait.name: Shapechanger
entries: The dapifer can use its action to polymorph into a Small or Medium humanoid, or back into its true form. Other than its size and speed, its statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

trait.name: Fiendish Charm
entries: The dapifer can innately cast {@spell charm person} spell ({@dc 16}), but the target does not understand it was cast by the dark dapifer after the spell duration is over.

trait.name: Spell Master {@recharge 5}
entries: The dapifer can cast a spell or a cantrip using a bonus action.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dapifer makes two life drain attacks.

action.name: Life Drain
entries: {@atk ms,rs} {@hit +8} to hit, reach 5 ft., or range 60 ft. one target. {@h}14 ({@damage 4d6}) necrotic damage. The dapifer restores hit points equal to the highest roll of d6 roll. On a critical hit, the dapifer may forgo the healing effect and grant the target Disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes against the dapifer.

trait.name: Diagnose
entries: If the dottore can spend 1 minute examining a patient, it has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) checks to determine a poison or disease.

trait.name: Antidote (5)
entries: The dottore carries an item called an antidote on it. The antidote, when consumed with a bonus action, neutralizes any poison affecting a creature, removes the {@condition Poisoned} condition, and gives Advantage on saving throws against diseases to the creature until it finishes a long rest. The dottore can produce an antidote by spending one week and 50 gd.

trait.name: Healer
entries: The dottore carries a {@item healer's kit|phb}. When it uses it on a creature, the creature can roll one of its hit dice and regain hit points equal to the total plus 3.

trait.name: Other Gear
entries: The dottore carries these items in addition to the ones mentioned above: a vial of {@item Basic Poison (vial)|PHB|poison}, a vial of {@item acid (vial)|PHB|acid}, Herbalism Kit, a book about medicine, and surgical equipment, such as a knife, bandages, and alcohol to clean the wound.

action.name: Poisoned Touch
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}2 ({@damage 1d4}) poison damage. The creature must succeed on a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition Poisoned} for 1 minute. It can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns to be free from the effect.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The lone one can cast the following spells, using Intelligence as its spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 13}, spell attack bonus {@hit +5}):

action.name: Arcane Impact
entries: {@atk ms,rs} {@hit +5} to hit, reach 5 ft., or range 60 ft. one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 2d6}) psychic damage.

trait.name: Blinding Strike (2/Day)
entries: The radiant one can cast the {@spell blinding smite} spell.

trait.name: Blinding Eruption (1/Day)
entries: The radiant one can erupt into light and choose any enemies within 15 ft. of it. Each chosen creature must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or become {@condition blinded} for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, the target can make a Constitution saving throw. On a success, the spell ends.

action.name: Greatsword
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +5} to hit, reach 5 ft., Hit: 10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) slashing damage plus 4 ({@damage 1d6}) radiant damage.

action.name: Radiant Retribution
entries: {@atk rs} range 30 ft., one target. {@h}10 ({@damage 3d6}) radiant damage.

spellcasting.name: Innate Spellcasting
headerEntries: The caladrius can cast the following spells innately, using Wisdom as its spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}, spell attack bonus {@hit +4}):

trait.name: Holy Protection
entries: The caladrius is always under the effects of the {@spell sanctuary} ({@dc 12}) and the {@spell detect poison and disease} spell. If it attacks, the {@spell sanctuary} spell is restored at the start of its next turn.

trait.name: Bright Melody (1/Day)
entries: The caladrius can sing a beautiful song to mend the hearts that it can hear within 30 ft for 1 minute. After a full minute, the creatures gain the benefits of a short rest.

trait.name: Innocent Life
entries: A creature that damages the caladrius takes double the damage it dealt as radiant damage.

action.name: Healing Touch {@recharge 5}
entries: The caladrius can touch a creature with a non-evil alignment and restore 7 ({@damage 2d6}) hit points to it. If it has a non-magical sickness, it is also cured.

action.name: Holy Beak
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}3 piercing damage plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) radiant damage.

spellcasting.name: Innate Spellcasting
headerEntries: The merciful one can cast these spells innately, without material components. Wisdom is its spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 14}):

trait.name: Permanent Sanctuary
entries: The merciful one is always under the effects of the {@spell sanctuary} spell ({@dc 14}). If it is broken due to spell's effects or some other way, it is renewed after 10 minutes.

action.name: Mercy (1/Day)
entries: The hidden one can use its action to touch a creature and cast {@spell lesser restoration} or {@spell greater restoration} on it without needing material components.

action.name: Calming Touch
entries: The merciful one touches a creature and marks it. If the creature attacks a creature until the end of its next turn, it must succeed on a {@dc 14} Wisdom saving throw or take 18 ({@damage 4d8}) radiant damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.

spellcasting.name: Waterborne Spellcasting
headerEntries: The adept gondolier can innately cast the following spells while on its waterborne vehicle or within 30 feet of water, using an oar or a similar item related to its vehicle as its spellcasting focus. Charisma is its spellcasting modifier (spell save {@dc 15}, spell attack bonus {@hit +7}):

trait.name: Vehicle Mastery
entries: The adept gondolier has Advantage on any check related to its gondola.

trait.name: Iron Lungs
entries: The adept gondolier can hold its breath for double the normal amount.

trait.name: Gear
entries: An adept gondolier usually carries a magic necklace that can cast {@spell goodberry} once a day and a magical weapon called oar of the sturdy. In addition, it may carry three {@item potion of healing|PHB|potions of healing} and 20 +1 ammunition for its hand crossbow.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The adept gondolier can make three oar attacks. It can replace one of the attacks with a hand crossbow.

action.name: Oar of the Sturdy
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +7} to hit, ranged 20/60 ft., or reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) bludgeoning damage or 8 ({@damage 1d10 + 3}) bludgeoning damage if used with two hands. This attack is counted as magical.

action.name: Hand Crossbow
entries: {@atk rw} {@hit +4} to hit, range 30/120 ft., {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) piercing damage.

trait.name: Vehicle Mastery
entries: The gondolier has Advantage on any check related to its gondola.

trait.name: Iron Lungs
entries: The gondolier can hold its breath for double the normal amount.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The gondolier can make two oar attacks.

action.name: Oar
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d8 + 2}) bludgeoning damage or 7 ({@damage 1d10 + 2}) bludgeoning damage if used with two hands.

spellcasting.name: Waterborne Spellcasting

trait.name: Vehicle Mastery
entries: The journeyman gondolier has Advantage on any check related to its gondola.

trait.name: Iron Lungs
entries: The journeyman gondolier can hold its breath for double the normal amount.

trait.name: Gear
entries: A journeyman gondolier usually carries a magic necklace that can cast {@spell goodberry} once a day and a magical weapon called oar of the sturdy. In addition, it may carry two {@item potion of healing|PHB|potions of healing} and 10 +1 ammunition for its hand crossbow.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The journeyman gondolier can make two oar attacks. It can replace one of the attacks with a hand crossbow.

action.name: Oar of the Sturdy
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d8 + 2}) bludgeoning damage or 7 ({@damage 1d10 + 2}) bludgeoning damage if used with two hands. This attack is counted as magical.

action.name: Hand Crossbow
entries: {@atk rw} {@hit +4} to hit, range 30/120 ft., {@h}5 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) piercing damage.

trait.name: Brutal Damage
entries: When the hinthial rolls an 18 or 19 on an attack roll, it deals an extra 10 necrotic damage. If it's a critical hit, the damage becomes 20 necrotic damage.

trait.name: Gear
entries: It uses a magical net to trap its foes. The net appears back in its hand if it misses or if the enemy is freed from the net. Its kopis is also considered a magical weapon while it is being wielded by the hinthial.

trait.name: Magical Sense
entries: The hinthial can sense magic items and objects that date to the time of Etruscan and early Roman civilization while within 120 ft. of them.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The hinthial makes three attacks with its kopis. It can replace one of the attacks with the magical net.

action.name: Kopis
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +7} to hit reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d6 + 4}) slashing damage. When a creature is hit by a hinthial wielding a kopis, it falls {@condition prone}.

action.name: Magical Net
entries: {@atk mw,rw} {@hit +7} to hit, reach 5 ft. or ranged 15 ft. one target. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d6}) poison damage. On a hit, the creature is {@condition restrained} by the net if it is smaller than Huge. The DC to escape the net is 15.

trait.name: Brutal Leap
entries: The fallen demon has Advantage on the next attack roll against if moves at least 15 ft. before attacking on that turn.

trait.name: Shapechanger
entries: The fallen demon can use its action to polymorph into a Small or Medium humanoid, or back into its true form. Other than its size and speed, its statistics are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The fallen demon can attack twice with its fiendish claws.

action.name: Fiendish Claws
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +6} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) piercing damage plus 4 ({@damage 1d6}) fire damage.

spellcasting.name: Innate Spellcasting
headerEntries: Il Mazaròl casts one of the following spells, requiring no material components and using Charisma as the spellcasting ability ({@hit +7} to hit, spell save {@dc 15}):

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: Il Mazaròl has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Il Mazaròl makes one Bite attack and one Claw attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +7} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d6 + 4}) piercing damage plus 18 ({@damage 4d8}) force damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +7} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d6 + 4}) slashing damage plus 9 ({@damage 2d8}) force damage.

reaction.name: Corrupt Souls
entries: When Il Mazaròl strikes down a creature and kills it, it can use a reaction to make it fall to 1 hit point instead of dying. The creature must succeed on a {@dc 15} Charisma saving throw or be {@condition charmed} by Il Mazaròl for {@dice 1d6} days. If it fails the saving throw by 5 or more, its alignment changes to what Il Mazaròl deems appropriate. This change is permanent unless a {@spell remove curse} or {@spell greater restoration} spell is cast.

spellcasting.name: Innate Spellcasting
headerEntries: The crimson fiend can cast the following spells, using Charisma as its spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 16}, spell attack bonus {@hit +4}):

bonus.name: Fiery Form
entries: As a bonus action, the crimson fiend can turn a form of pure elemental fire until the start of its next turn. While in this form, it is immune to all damage except cold damage but can't attack any creature. It gains a flying speed of 20 ft. and gains immunity against {@condition prone}, {@condition restrained}, {@condition paralyzed} conditions. If it ends its turn in a creature's space, it takes 6 ({@damage 1d10}) force damage while the creature takes 2 ({@damage 1d4}) fire damage. While in this form, it can squeeze through in openings as narrow as 1-inch, such as a keyhole or similar.

action.name: Flame Fist
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) bludgeoning damage plus 4 ({@damage 1d6}) fire damage.

action.name: Eruption
entries: Il Rosso targets a point within 60 ft. of it. Flame erupts from the point and creatures within 10 ft. of that point must succeed on a {@dc 12} Dexterity saving throw or start burning for 1 minute. A burning creature takes 4 ({@damage 1d6}) fire damage at the start of each of its turns for the duration. Only water from a spell can put out the flames. On a successful save, a creature takes only 2 ({@damage 1d4}) fire damage.

trait.name: Amphibious
entries: The ladropaura can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Acidic Skin
entries: A creature that hits the ladropaura from 10 ft. or closer must succeed on a {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw or take 7 ({@damage 2d6}) acid damage. On a success, it takes half damage.

trait.name: Breathtake
entries: If underwater, whenever the ladropaura scores a critical hit against a creature, the creature loses all air in its lungs and starts to suffocate if it can't breathe underwater.

trait.name: Shapechange
entries: The ladropaura can change its shape using its action. It can change its size to smaller sizes than it already is, and all of its statistics remain the same. It can alter its appearance however it likes, though it usually chooses to change into gaseous form or the form of an elf.

trait.name: Magical Surge
entries: When a spell targets the ladropaura or a spell is cast within 15 ft. of it, ladropaura gains 1 charge to its Magical Surge. It can spend a charge to use Magical Drain as an action, or it can use its reaction to spend a charge to grant itself a saving throw bonus (+7). It can have a maximum of 5 charges.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The ladropaura makes one attack with its spikes and two attacks with its claws. One of the attacks can be replaced with Magical Drain.

action.name: Spikes
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +9} to hit, reach 10 ft. or one target. {@h}16 ({@damage 3d6 + 5}) bludgeoning damage plus 5 ({@damage 1d8}) acid damage. The creature is {@condition grappled} by the ladropaura if it's smaller than Large.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +9} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}12 ({@damage 2d6 + 5}) slashing damage plus 11 ({@damage 3d6}) acid damage. The target must succeed on a {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition stunned} until the end of its next turn.

action.name: Magical Drain
entries: The ladropaura drains magic in an area in a 15-foot-radius from itself. Each creature within the area must make a {@dc 14} Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they can't cast spells and take 11 ({@damage 3d6}) damage at the start of each of their turns while they are in the area. On a successful save, they only take half the damage in the first instance.

trait.name: Poisonous Strikes
entries: The weapons held by the hollow skin are coated with poison. Its attacks deal extra poison damage included in the actions.

trait.name: Hide Presence
entries: The hollow skin's creature type appears like whatever it wants to be when targeted by a feature, spell, or magical effect that would affect it, for example a paladin's Divine Sense ability or the {@spell detect evil and good} spell.

trait.name: Mark for Destruction (1/Day)
entries: The hollow skin chooses a damage type and touches a creature to force it to make a {@dc 12} Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the next time it is hit with the damage type of the hollow skin's choice, it is counted as vulnerable to the damage type. If the target has immunity to the chosen damage type, this feature does not work. On a successful save, the next time it is hit with the damage type of the hollow skin's choice, it takes an extra 7 ({@damage 2d6}) necrotic damage and the mark ends. While the mark continues, the hollow skin knows where the target is for 1 hour, unless it is on another plane of existence.

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atk mw,rw} {@hit +3} to hit, reach 5 ft., or range 20/60 ft., one target. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d4 + 1}) piercing damage plus 4 ({@damage 1d6}) poison damage.

monster.name: Living Mask
languages: can't speak but understands any two languages

action.name: Attach {@recharge 5}
entries: The living mask can use its action to attach to a creature's face within 10 ft. of it. If the creature has a Charisma score of 13 or lower, the living mask starts to eat its face and the creature is {@condition grappled} (escape {@dc 15}) by the living mask. While {@condition grappled}, the creature takes 7 ({@damage 2d6}) necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns. When a creature dies in this way, the living mask takes complete control of their body. While a creature is {@condition grappled} by the living mask, it is {@condition silenced}. If the creature's Charisma score is 14 or higher, it must make a {@dc 15} Charisma saving throw or is {@condition grappled} by the living mask.

action.name: Sleep Gas {@recharge 5}
entries: The living mask creates an invisible and scentless gas that covers an area within 10 ft. of it. The creatures that enter the area for the first time or those that start their turn there must succeed on a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw or fall asleep. The area stays gassed for 1 minute.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The merchant casts one of the following spells, using Charisma as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}, spell attack bonus {@hit +4}):

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atk mw,rw} {@hit +2} to hit, range (20/60) or reach 5ft., one target. {@h}2 ({@damage 1d4}) piercing damage.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The hex-bender can cast these spells. Charisma is its spellcasting ability modifier (spell save {@dc 17}, spell attack bonus {@hit +9}):

spellcasting.name: Hex Magic
headerEntries: If a creature with a soul is marked by a Hex of the Walker ability within 15 ft. of the Hex-bender, it gains access to these spells using the same numbers in Spellcasting ability.

trait.name: Spirit Shroud
entries: The witch of the night can sense creatures that died within the last 24 hours by performing a 10-minute ritual.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The hex-bender makes three Mal-intent attacks.

action.name: Mal-intent
entries: {@atk ms,rs} {@hit +9} to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft., one target. {@h}12 ({@damage 2d6 + 5}) poison damage plus 4 ({@damage 1d6}) necrotic damage. If the d20 on the attack roll is 17 or higher, the creature falls under the effects of "Hex of the Walker" ability from Malandante, Hex-bender stat block.

action.name: Hex of the Walker
entries: A creature within 60 ft. of the Hex-bender that it can see must succeed on a {@dc 17} Wisdom saving throw or be marked by the ability for 1 minute and take 9 ({@damage 2d8}) necrotic damage. At the start of each of its turns the marked creature takes 27 ({@damage 6d8}) necrotic damage. If a creature dies while marked by the Hex of the Walker ability, Hex-bender can cast a spell from its Hex Magic ability or turn the creature to a hexed spirit.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The malandante disciple can cast these spells. Charisma is its spellcasting ability modifier (spell save {@dc 13}, spell attack bonus {@hit +5}):

trait.name: Spirit Shroud
entries: The malandante disciple can sense creatures that died within the last 24 hours by performing a 10-minute ritual.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The malandante disciple makes two Malintent attacks.

action.name: Mal Intent
entries: {@atk ms,rs} {@hit +5} to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft., one target. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) poison damage plus 4 ({@damage 1d6}) necrotic damage. On a critical hit, the creature falls under the effects of the Hex of the Walker ability from the malandante, hex-bender stat block.

trait.name: Spectral Form
entries: The hexed spirit can move through solid objects and creatures. If it ends its turn there, it takes 6 ({@damage 1d10}) force damage.

trait.name: Hex Aura
entries: Creatures within 5 ft. of a hexed spirit have Disadvantage on saving throws.

action.name: Spectral Sweep

reaction.name: Nullify Damage
entries: As a reaction, the hexed spirit transfers 13 ({@damage 3d8}) hit points from a malandante within 30 ft when it is hit. The malandante takes this as necrotic damage and must use its reaction. The hexed spirit can't attack if it uses this reaction.

Using Hex Magic deals the witch of the night 18 ({@damage 4d8}) force damage.

If the d20 on the attack roll is 17 or higher, the creature falls under the effects of the Hex of the Walker ability from the malandante, hex-bender stat block.

action.name: Hex Strike
entries: {@atk rs} {@hit +7} to hit, 60 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d6 + 4}) necrotic damage. The witch of the night can concentrate on this ability to mark the creature. The creature is affected by Hex Strike for 1 minute or until the witch of the night's concentration on this ability is broken. While affected, the creature takes 4 necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns.

While affected, the creature takes 4 necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns.

monster.name: Marionette
languages: can't speak but understands any three languages

trait.name: Mind Control
entries: When a creature attempts to control the marionette, it must make a {@dc 14} Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it is controlled by the marionette instead. The marionette can control the creature's actions and speech, and the creature can't take actions of its own control. While controlling the creature like this, the marionette can't take actions on its own. For this mind control to end, the creature must stop interacting with the strings of the marionette.

trait.name: Evil Incarnate
entries: While the marionette controls a creature, one of the creature's attacks deals psychic damage equal to 7 ({@damage 2d6}).

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The marionette makes two attacks with its Mind Burst. While controlling the creature, the marionette can replace one of the creature's attacks with a Mind Burst.

action.name: Mind Burst
entries: {@atk ms,rs} {@hit +6} to hit, range 60 ft., one target. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) psychic damage.

trait.name: Alert
entries: The oltremarino has Advantage on Initiative checks.

trait.name: Tactical Advantage
entries: When there is an ally within the oltremarino or the enemy it's attacking, it has Advantage on the attack roll.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The oltremarino makes two spear attacks.

action.name: Spear
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d6 + 3}) slashing damage, or 8 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) slashing damage if used with two hands.

spellcasting.name: Innate Spellcasting
headerEntries: The ombra can innately cast the following spells. Intelligence is its spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 13}, spell attack bonus {@hit +4}):

trait.name: Gear
entries: The ombra carries a {@item shortsword +1} and a {@item light crossbow +1}. Additionally, it usually has access to the following items and consumables, and it can use as a bonus action to use any of them:

items: 2 {@item potion of hill giant strength|dmg|potions of hill giant strength}

action.name: Shortsword +1
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +6} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d6 + 4}) slashing damage plus 11 ({@damage 3d6}) slashing damage if it does not have Disadvantage on the attack roll.

action.name: Light Crossbow +1
entries: {@atk rw} {@hit +6} to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d6 + 4}) piercing damage plus 11 ({@damage 3d6}) piercing damage if it does not have Disadvantage on the attack roll.

monster.name: Initiate
group: The Order Of The Scepter & Serpent

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting

entries: When the initiate uses a {@item Healer's Kit|phb} on a creature, the creature can spend one of its hit dice and roll it. Then it regains hit points equal to the result plus its Constitution modifier or the initiate's Wisdom modifier (whichever is higher).

trait.name: Gear
entries: Usually the initiate carries the following gear: {@item Healer's Kit|phb} (10 uses), two flasks of {@item holy water (flask)|PHB|holy water}, and an Herbalism Kit.

action.name: Healer's Wrath

action.name: Healer's Wrath
entries: {@atk ms,rs} {@hit +4} to hit, reach 5 ft., or range 60 ft., one target. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d6 + 2}) necrotic damage.

entries: When the hygeia uses a {@item healer's kit|phb} on a creature, the creature can spend one of its hit dice and roll it. Then it regains as much as hit points + its Constitution modifier or the initiate's Wisdom modifier (whichever is higher).

trait.name: Gear
entries: Usually the initiate carries these gear on it: {@item Healer's kit|phb} (10 uses), two flasks of {@item holy water (flask)|PHB|holy water}, an Herbalism Kit, and three {@item potion of healing|PHB|potions of healing}.

action.name: Healer's Wrath
entries: {@atk ms,rs} {@hit +4} to hit, reach 5 ft., or range 60 ft., two targets. {@h}9 ({@damage 1d8 + 4}) necrotic damage.

reaction.name: Ottoman Slap {@recharge 5}

On a success, the target takes only half damage and is not {@condition stunned}.

reaction.name: Fierce Sailor {@recharge 6}

Only those who entered the service of the state can attune to this magic item.

trait.name: Hard to Impress

action.name: Rapier
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +3} to hit reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d8 + 1}) piercing damage.

spellcasting.name: Traditions of an Old House

Charisma is their spellcasting ability (spell save DC is 13, spell attack bonus is {@hit +5}).

action.name: Rapier
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d8 + 2}) piercing damage.

reaction.name: Old Roots Die Hard

action.name: Longsword
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 2}) slashing damage or 8 ({@damage 1d10 + 2}) slashing damage if used with two hands.

reaction.name: Elegant Duelist (3/Day)
entries: When patrizio of the new house misses an attack roll, it can use its reaction to reroll the attack roll.

This effect is triggered when a creature enters the aura for the first time or starts its turn there.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The patrizio, ducal house makes two greatsword attacks.

action.name: Greatsword
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}9 ({@damage 2d6 + 2}) slashing damage.

trait.name: Good Ears
entries: The naval officer has Advantage on checks to determine lies.

bonus.name: Commander (5/Day)
entries: The naval officer targets an ally that can hear it within 60 ft. The ally gains {@dice 1d4} temporary hit points. It can sacrifice those points to add them to its next attack roll before making it.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The naval officer makes two attacks in any combination.

action.name: Pistol
entries: {@atk rw} {@hit +3} to hit, range 30/80 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d8 + 1}) piercing damage.

action.name: Rapier
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) piercing damage.

entries: {@atk mw,rw} {@hit +5} to hit, reach 5 ft., or range 20/60 ft., one target. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) piercing damage plus 5 ({@damage 2d4}) poison damage.

trait.name: Atone the Sins (3/Short Rest)
entries: The acolyte priest can spend at least 1 minute while listening to confessions and charge for a penance (it can be monetary or an action, such as spending a day cleaning a church, or similar). If the penance is completed, the creature's alignment can't be shifted for seven days and has +1 bonus on all ability checks and saving throws.

trait.name: Religious Ward
entries: All creatures have Disadvantage on attack rolls against the acolyte priest unless the priest attacked them, harmed them, or affected them with a negative spell within 24 hours.

action.name: Humble Approach
entries: The acolyte priest forces a creature within 30 ft. of it to make a Wisdom saving throw. If the acolyte priest's Religious Ward is active against that creature, the creature has Disadvantage on this save. On a failed save, the creature subtracts {@dice 1d8 + 2} from all damage rolls for one minute. It can repeat the saving throw at the end of its turns. If it attacks or harms a creature during the minute, it takes 13 ({@damage 3d8}) damage. If the Religious Ward is broken, this effect ends early as well.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting

trait.name: Atone the Sins (3/Short Rest)
entries: The clergyman priest can spend at least 1 minute while listening to confessions and charge for a penance (it can be monetary or an action, such as spending a day cleaning a church, or similar). If the penance is completed, the creature's alignment can't be shifted for seven days and has +1 bonus on all ability checks and saving throws.

trait.name: Religious Ward
entries: All creatures have Disadvantage on attack rolls against the clergyman unless the priest attacked them, harmed them, or affected them with a negative spell within 24 hours.

action.name: Humble Sanctum

On a failed save, the creature subtracts {@dice 1d8 + 2} from all damage rolls for one minute. It can repeat the saving throw at the end of its turns. If it attacks or harms a creature during the minute, it takes 13 ({@damage 3d8}) damage. If the Religious Ward is broken, this effect ends early as well.

entries: The ragna can breathe air and water.

trait.name: Unseen Shadow
entries: The ragna must make a {@dc 14} Wisdom saving throw when it makes an attack while it is {@condition invisible}. On a success, it remains {@condition invisible}. On a failed save, it can't use the Veil in the Night ability until the start of its next turn.

bonus.name: Veil in the Night
entries: The ragna can turn {@condition invisible} until the start of its next turn, if it is under dim light or darkness.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The ragna makes two attacks with its deadly claws. It can replace one of the attacks with Deadly Leap.

action.name: Deadly Claws
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +7} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) piercing damage plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) necrotic damage. If a creature dies because of this attack, it will rise as a Drowned One at next dawn, unless its turn to undead is prevented.

action.name: Deadly Charge {@recharge 5}
entries: The ragna lunges towards a creature within 50 ft. of it. The creatures in the path must succeed on a {@dc 14} Dexterity saving throw or take 4 ({@damage 1d6}) piercing damage plus 4 ({@damage 1d6}) necrotic damage or half as much on a successful save. The target creature must succeed on the same saving throw. On a failed save, it is {@condition restrained} by the ragna. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns to be free from the effect.

monster.name: Drowned One
languages: understand all languages it spoke in life but can't speak

trait.name: Cursed Fungi
entries: When the drowned one hits a creature, it must make a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target is {@condition poisoned} for 1 minute and can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns to be free from the effect. On a successful save, a creature is immune to this effect for 24 hours. While a creature is cursed like this, it takes {@damage 1d6} necrotic damage at the start of each of its turns if it can't breathe. In addition, when a creature hits the drowned one, it takes 2 ({@damage 1d4}) poison damage.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) bludgeoning damage plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) poison damage.

action.name: Deadly Fume (1/Day)

Creatures that start their turn there or when they enter it for the first time must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw or fall {@condition unconscious}. An affected creature stays {@condition unconscious} for 10 minutes or until it takes damage.

trait.name: Obsession
entries: The red hand senses if it is within 120 ft. of whatever it is obsessed with. In addition, the red hand has Advantage on attack rolls against the creature if that creature carries that object. If the red hand does not satisfy its need with the object in the last week, it has Disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws.

trait.name: Golden Sense
entries: The red hand senses any precious gem, coin, or similar item within 120 ft. of it.

action.name: Crimson Touch
entries: {@atk ms} {@hit +4} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}9 ({@damage 2d8}) necrotic damage.

entries: The royal artist is immune to the {@condition charmed} condition.

action.name: Faithful's Gaze
entries: {@atk ms,rs} {@hit +6} to hit, reach 5 ft., or range 60 ft., two targets. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d10}) psychic damage.

action.name: Javelin (+1)

trait.name: Acrobatic Movement
entries: The street acrobat adds double its Dexterity modifier to its Armor Class when it is not wearing armor or shields and its speed is more than 5 feet.

trait.name: Throwing Master
entries: The street acrobat adds +1 bonus to ranged attacks made with weapons with the Thrown property. When it hits with a ranged attack roll using a weapon that has the Thrown property, it gains a +2 bonus to the damage roll (included in the actions).

trait.name: Throwable Gear
entries: The street acrobat usually has these kinds of throwable weapons and consumables at its disposal:

items: 3 flasks of {@item alchemist's fire (flask)|PHB|alchemist's fire}, range 30 ft., {@dc 13}
2 pouches of {@item ball bearings (bag of 1,000)|PHB|ball bearings}, range 30 ft. {@dc 13}
2 bags of {@item caltrops (bag of 20)|PHB|caltrops}, range 30 ft., {@dc 13}

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The street acrobat can throw three weapons or make two melee attacks. If it chooses to throw, it can replace one of the attacks with one of the items in its Throwable Gear above.

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atk mw,rw} {@hit +6} to hit, ranged 20/60 ft., or reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}5 ({@damage 1d4 + 3}) piercing damage or 7 ({@damage 1d4 + 5}) piercing damage if thrown.

action.name: Dart
entries: {@atk rw} {@hit +6} to hit, ranged 20/60 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d4 + 5}) piercing damage.

trait.name: Allure of Dance
entries: While not wearing any armor or holding a shield, the street dancer adds its Charisma modifier to its armor class. Its speed must not be 0 for it to be able to benefit it.

trait.name: Dance Like There's No Tomorrow
entries: The street dancer adds its Charisma modifier to Fast Strike attack and damage rolls (included below), provided that it is not wearing armor or holding a shield.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The street dancer makes two attacks with its Fast Strike.

action.name: Fast Strike
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +6} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}9 ({@damage 1d8 + 4}) bludgeoning damage.

spellcasting.name: Innate Spellcasting
headerEntries: The street actor can innately cast the following spells, using Charisma as its spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}, spell attack bonus {@hit +4}):

trait.name: Mimicry
entries: The street actor can copy a speech, an accent, a sound or similar audible data and copy it exactly.

action.name: Vicious Words
entries: {@atk ms,rs} {@hit +4} to hit, reach 5 ft., range 60 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 2d6}) psychic damage.

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atk mw,rw} {@hit +4} to hit, ranged 20/60 ft., or reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) piercing damage.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The temperatore can cast these spells using Intelligence as its spellcasting ability modifier ({@hit +4} to hit, {@dc 12})

trait.name: Mechanical Mind
entries: The temperatore has Advantage on Wisdom and Intelligence checks concerning constructs and machines.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The temperatore makes two attacks.

action.name: Psionic Strike
entries: {@atk ms,rs} {@hit +6} to hit, one target, reach 5 ft., or range 60 ft. {@h}12 ({@damage 2d8 + 3}) psychic damage.

action.name: Clockwork Hammer
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +4} to hit, one target, reach 5 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) bludgeoning damage. The target must succeed on a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw or be {@condition stunned} until the start of its next turn.

action.name: The Machine's Heart {@recharge 6}
entries: The temperatore can take control of a construct by spending an action. The construct must succeed on a {@dc 13} Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, the construct is under the clock watcher's control for 10 minutes.

trait.name: Instinct
entries: The vendor has Advantage on Initiative checks and can't be surprised.

trait.name: Tradesman Qualities
entries: The vendor can duplicate the effects of one of the following spells once per day: {@spell alarm}, {@spell merchant's ward|EchoesOfRenaissance}, {@spell purify food and drink}. Wisdom is its spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}).

action.name: Dagger
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +4} to hit, range (20/60) or reach 5ft., one target. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) piercing damage.

monster.name: Strix
languages: Can't speak but understands three languages

trait.name: Flyby
entries: The strix does not provoke an Opportunity Attack when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

trait.name: Ill Aura of Misfortune (15 feet)
entries: The strix has a magical aura. While in this aura, the characters are affected by the {@spell bane} spell whenever they take damage.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The strix makes two attacks with its Baneful Claws. Alternatively, it can use Blood Hunt twice.

action.name: Baneful Claws
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +7} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}15 ({@damage 3d6 + 4}) slashing damage plus 3 ({@damage 1d6}) psychic damage.

action.name: Blood Hunt
entries: {@atk ms} {@hit +7} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 2d6}) necrotic damage.

reaction.name: Ill Aura of Misfortune
entries: If the strix scores a critical hit against a creature, it can use its reaction to change it to a {@spell bestow curse} spell instead.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The master glassblower casts one of the following spells, using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}, {@hit +4} to hit with spell attacks):

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The master glassblower makes two melee attacks with its glass dagger, or makes one melee attack and then throws the dagger. If it throws the glass dagger, at the start of its turn, it conjures another one with the {@spell shards of glass|EchoesOfRenaissance} cantrip.

action.name: Glass Dagger
entries: {@atk mw,rw} {@hit +4} to hit, ranged 20/40 ft., or reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) slashing damage. On a hit, the target must succeed on a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw or its movement speed is reduced by half.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
