headerEntries: The glassblower apprentice casts one of the following spells, using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}, {@hit +4} to hit with spell attacks):

action.name: Glass Dagger
entries: {@atk mw,rw} {@hit +4} to hit, ranged 20/40 ft., or reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) slashing damage. On a hit, the target must succeed on a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw or its movement speed is reduced by half.

trait.name: Immutable Form
entries: The golem is immune to any spell or effect that would alter its form.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The golem has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Magic Weapons
entries: The golem's weapon attacks are magical.

bonus.name: Total Reflection {@recharge 4}
entries: The golem can use a bonus action to cast {@spell invisibility} on itself.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The glass golem makes two attacks in any combination using its Shattered Glass or Blinding Reflection.

action.name: Shattered Glass
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +9} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}23 ({@damage 4d8 + 5}) slashing damage.

action.name: Blinding Reflection
entries: {@atk rs} {@hit +9} to hit, range 120 ft. {@h}4 ({@damage 1d8}) radiant damage. The creature is {@condition blinded} until the end of its next turn.

reaction.name: Severe Critical
entries: When the golem scores a critical hit against a creature, it can use its reaction to cast the {@spell disrupt one's weave|EchoesOfRenaissance} and {@spell invisibility}. ({@dc 16}).

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The veteran of Venice makes three longsword attacks.

action.name: Longsword
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit +8} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}10 ({@damage 1d8 + 5}) slashing damage or 11 ({@damage 1d10 + 5}) slashing damage if used with two hands.

action.name: Heavy Crossbow
entries: {@atk rw} {@hit +6} to hit, range 100/400 ft., one target. {@h}9 ({@damage 1d10 + 3}) piercing damage.

reaction.name: Quick Charge
entries: The veteran of Venice can use its reaction to move half of its speed when a creature within 30 ft. of it moves. This movement does not trigger Opportunity Attacks.

spellcasting.name: Innate Spellcasting
headerEntries: The vivo can cast the following spells innately, without needing material components. Charisma is its spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}):

trait.name: Alter Shape
entries: The vivo can cast the {@spell enlarge/reduce} spell on itself at will but can't become a larger size than Medium.

trait.name: Conjure Object
entries: The vivo can cast {@spell Al-Jazari's practical summons|EchoesOfRenaissance} spell once a day, as an action.

action.name: Fae Gaze
entries: The vivo forces a creature it can see within 60 ft. of it to make a {@dc 12} Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes 7 ({@damage 2d4 + 2}) psychic damage and its next attack roll is made with Disadvantage.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: The rabbi can cast these spells without any material components. Wisdom is its spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 13}):

trait.name: Berakhah (3/Day)
entries: The rabbi can spend at least 1 minute studying or in silent prayer before uttering a berakhah, or blessing. The rabbi chooses up to five creatures within 30 ft.; those creatures are under the effect of the {@spell bless} spell. The creatures must be able to hear the rabbi in order to benefit from the blessing.

trait.name: Religious Ward
entries: All creatures have Disadvantage on attack rolls against the rabbi unless the rabbi attacked them, harmed them, or affected them with a negative spell within 24 hours.

trait.name: Amulet of the Faith (1/Day)
entries: Once per long rest, the rabbi can spend 1 hour to create an amulet, written on a piece of parchment, cloth, or similar material. The writings include one of the sacred names of God, names of angels, as well as blessings and specific words of aid or assistance. This amulet can then be carried by a creature and offer one of the following boons, depending on what specific assistance the amulet includes:

items: Advantage on saving throws when the target of a fiend's spells or effects.
Advantage on saving throws when the target of an undead's spells or effects.
Advantage on saving throws when the target of a curse from any source.
Speaking the final word on the amulet aloud casts {@spell pass without trace}.

entries: The amulet works once; the writing then fades, and the material it was written on crumbles to dust.

action.name: Humble Sanctum
entries: The rabbi forces a creature within 30 ft. of it to make a Wisdom saving throw. If the rabbi's Religious Ward is active against that creature, the creature has Disadvantage on this save. On a failed save, the creature subtracts {@dice 1d8 + 2} from all damage rolls for one minute. It can repeat the saving throw at the end of its turns. If it attacks or harms a creature during the minute, it takes 13 ({@damage 3d8}) damage. If the Religious Ward is broken, this effect ends early as well.

monsterFluff.name: Aamon
entries: A creature with enormous eyes and monster-like features, with long legs and reptilian skin, reeking of sulfur and cinnamon, stands dreadful at the edge of the shadows. Found peeking at the stars at the fringes of civilization or forgotten roofs and with faces that know the dawn and doom of the world, the aamon is a fiend with precognitive abilities. It feeds on the souls of prophets, seers, and augurs, mostly the false ones, preparing a doom that it has foreseen: a terrible and a dark one. With its shapechanging abilities, it easily plots its schemes.

entries.name: Terrible Goals
entries: Each aamon sees a terrible future that it wishes to fulfill and works towards it. Usually it hunts down anyone who could stop it. Alternatively, it befriends the potential obstacles to its prophecy, and analyzes their threat potential. Sometimes the death of a certain creature could make the prophecy an absolute failure. An aamon carefully pulls the strings it built around its visions and does everything in its power to ensure it. Usually, the visions it has are far from realistic or doable, and the aamon feels so devoted to the case that it strays away from fulfilling it right away so it can bask in the vision. The aamon is also powerless against natural causes and is unable to destroy entire cities or civilizations, though that won't stop it from trying if that is the vision it has seen.

entries.name: Possible Lair
entries: Some of the aamon make a lair for themselves, usually in simple and quotidian locations–perhaps a shop, an abandoned temple, or a local tavern's basement. At first glance, it's a normal place with daily objects and littered with papers, but the papers contain foul, twisted versions of religious texts, but twisted versions, which can be realized when one spends enough time reading them. On random pages, an aamon has notes of its horrible vision, and in some corners there are imps, the ones that an aamon summons from time to time as servants or agents.

monsterFluff.name: Ales Leo
entries: In times of dire tides, when survivors of war fled to the lagoon in search of a shelter against the dark, a legend kept their spirits alight and their hopes safe: a winged lion with the sharpest claws. No one knew its legend until one night, they discovered that it was the companion of a dying druid, aged with wisdom and kindness, who had instructed the lion to help those in need.

The lion would keep them safe in wars and carry the torch of enlightenment in times of peace. The druid taught the lion everything he knew, and so did the survivors of the dark tides. Since that time, Ales Leo has become the symbol of protection of Venice. The city has long forgotten the old druid and has subsumed the image of the lion into the cult of St. Mark, adopted patron saint of the city.

In fact, many in the city have forgotten that the lion is more than just a myth. Nevertheless, Ales Leo has remained to defend the Lagoon and its inhabitants. While it battled evil, its wounds and losses were healed and modified by scientists and craftsmen, making its warrior form more powerful than ever.

monsterFluff.name: Angós
entries: Whispers in the night tell the story of a sibilance and calm disturbance of the waves in the canals. A dark figure on a gondola covered with scales and trailed by snakes approaches those who tossed coins into the water and say the right words. He accepts bargains of many kinds, from fast travel arrangements to plaguing one's dreams, and finds shortcuts better than any resident of Venice.

Some say he was the first one that drowned in the waters when the city was founded; some tell a story of betrayal that Angós committed and was cursed in return. In either case, the arcanists of Venice believe that it once was an abhuman with potent magic powers that it carries even after its death.

entries.name: Shining After Rainy Days
entries: The rainbow fairies are creatures that are seen as glimpses of hope, especially on islands, along coastlines, and between tides. They are believed to appear after rainbows, as their name suggests, and they bring joy lost after a rain. They bring tiny but nutritious berries to travelers and often help those in distress find their way.

entries.name: Colorful Personalities
entries: The rainbow fairies are loud, friendly, and come in very different personalities, depending on the color they choose to wear. They accompany adventurers, travel distant seas, explore dangerous areas, get married, and delight in song and wine, depending on the light that shines on them when they wake up.

entries.name: Magical Protection
entries: They can grant magical protection to their allies for a brief period of time, as they are used to the perils of adventuring and other threats on the magical side of the world. It is said in legends that the rainbow fairies are born within the magic of rainbows, so they are able to protect others as well.

monsterFluff.name: Arsenalotto
entries: The fleet of Venice and the seafaring abilities of Venetians are famed across the Mediterranean world. They owe this reputation to the quality of their ships and the skills of the workers in the famous Arsenale. These have enabled the Venetians to take on not only their Italian rivals, the formidable Genoese, but also the mighty Ottoman Empire. The shipwrights are sturdy and agile people, masters of ship-building and craft, and are sworn to secrecy about the nature of their construction process.

monsterFluff.name: Artisan of Venice
entries: The artisans can be found in most corners of the city. They are one of the pillars that carry the Republic, as they cover the most important jobs in the city and make it breathe. Many of these artisans are respected in their areas and highly sought after for their craft.

monsterFluff.name: Astronomer
entries: Humanity has always sought the answers in the sky, and the calling has always been there. Those who gaze upon the stars have also narrowed a gate to the arcane and combined their curiosity for the world with a gaze beyond the veil. Astronomers are stargazers, scientists, and notable people from society with access to limited magical knowledge.

monsterFluff.name: Avogadore de Comun
entries: In Venice, state attorneys protected the rights of noble families and represented an important part of the laws that made the Republic of Venice the stable force it was famed for being. They investigate reported crimes, attend important cases, and overall defend the law.

entries.name: Born Forsaken
entries: These fey are born from the wails, tears, and blood of those who are forsaken. Enchanted swamp areas usually cover the tracks, bones, and memories of long gone spirits, and some manifest themselves as Borda, the ones that long for companionship and true friendship. Some of the Borda use this longing as a way of getting in touch with the ones in the swamp and use their magical ropes to help them. However, some are condemned to their loneliness and seek revenge on those who dared to cross their swamp; they kidnap them and forcibly bring them to their lair, forcing them to be a companion.

entries.name: Hide and Seek
entries: Borda rarely show themselves and tend to interact with people by leaving interesting objects or tracks that could be noticed or valued in a swamp. A deserted campsite, a silk rope, a backpack full of supplies, or a chest might look promising for treasure hunters. Some Borda use these to lure their prey, while some put them on a task to prove their worth.

entries.name: The Blindfold
entries: Borda's eyes are fiendish and grotesque, appearing rotten and dangerous, even to their own kind. Their sight is not limited to their eyes, so they put on a blindfold and unleash their power only when it is necessary.

entries.name: A Coven of Borda
entries: When at least three Borda form a coven, they gain powers, and their eyes' power grows even stronger.

monsterFluff.name: Capitano delle Navi
entries: The captains were the most important piece that operated that giant machine called the Venetian fleet. Captains lead their sailors into expeditions, naval battles, and more.

monsterFluff.name: Sopracomito
entries: The galley captains control the flagships of the navy, and their expertise in navigation and good leadership skills make them perfect for the job.

monsterFluff.name: Canali Plaguebeast
entries: This monster was said to have arrived in Venice during the first spread of the Black Death. Either it was born of the suffering of the masses, grew out of the pestilence leaching into the earth and water, or was simply attracted to surplus human carrion. It grew large and fat, and when the plague faded, it waited patiently for the next one. It has since spawned more of its kind, most of which are dormant and wait for the next epidemic. However, some younger plaguebeasts slink out and search for food, searching for easy meals and vulnerable prey–those who stray too close to the canals and don't pay attention, such as drunk revelers during Carnevale.

The plague beasts resemble putrid eels with rows of needle-like teeth. They are aquatic but can move on land for brief periods of time. They are scavengers and opportunists, unless they go too long between meals; when that happens, they are comfortable becoming ambush predators.

entries.name: Pure Energy
entries: The celestiali are a type of ethereal creature that usually comes from the realm of undead, the spirits stuck in the material realms for too long. However, instead of terrorizing innocents as horrifying undead, these souls found their way to the pure magic of the world and became the manifestations of innocence and deeds that are considered good.

entries.name: No Memories
entries: Although they remember almost nothing about their past lives, the celestiali usually have a singular goal they want to follow: like protect a certain church, escorting pilgrims to reach a holy place, guiding seafarers to safety, punishing pirates who kidnap people from coasts. Some are rather furious and vengeful, while some can be charming, peaceful and even defenseless.

entries.name: Cycle of Nature
entries: Some of the celestiali are transformed into more beastly shapes rather than humanoid forms, they can appear as a guiding deer in the forest, a loyal dog for a person in pain, and many other variable conditions, shapes and interesting aspects, sometimes even as a plant.

items.name: Fated One
entries: The fated ones usually look like humanoids and sense when the death of a creature is close.

items.name: Hidden One
entries: Hidden ones resemble a beast of their choosing, usually elk, antelope, or a similar animal of good omens and rarely take the form of predators. They usually exist to protect or guide ones in need, lost creatures, distressed travelers, or similar people.

monsterFluff.name: Condottieri
entries: The condottieri were mercenaries of great renown, but they were not mere sellswords: they were often leaders of mercenary armies and courageous people who changed the course of wars in the Italian peninsula and in the battles concerning the fate of Europe. The term originally meant "contractor," due to the fact that the condottieri offered their services according to a contract.

monsterFluff.name: Commoner of Venice
entries: The people living in Venice are a mixture of those descending from the original inhabitants, many of whom were transplants from other parts of the peninsula during the crumbling of the Western Roman Empire. Others are immigrants from other parts of the world, such as Eastern Rome, who have made their new home in the Lagoon. No matter their origin, they share a reputation for being resolute, proud, and ambitious.

entries.name: Hedonistic Cultists
entries: The ones that follow Bacchus focus on where they find pleasure and how to keep it. Their hedonistic view of the world forces a livelihood of lies and secrecy upon them. They enjoy their moments in closed quarters, safe havens –away from the eyes of the world.

entries.name: Magical Rituals
entries: Magical words uttered in the dark follow their footsteps and sounds of pleasure. Their expertise in indoor magic make the cultists of Bacchus a tremendous force to be reckoned with, and dangerous if they are faced as their enemies.

entries.name: Hierarchy
entries: The highest rank in the order belonged to women and they were called Maenad. They lead the rituals, command the low ranking cultists and decide the fate of the order. The Gerarae presides over the rituals and stands in for Paculla. The Bassarid are the lowest rank in the hierarchy and represent a regular but actually powerful cultist of Bacchus.

monsterFluff.name: Dark Dapifer
entries: There are many denizens of the darker corners of the realms that hunger insatiably for flesh and souls, and the dark dapifer is one such being that arose to fit a niche: serve those hungry ones the souls and flesh they crave. Their true forms are often sinewy, dark, and iridescent, akin to walking bitumen, though they typically appear as elegant and beautiful humanoids in order to attract followers and corrupt their souls. Some dapifers have strayed from their original calling and have instead begun gathering souls to empower themselves.

monsterFluff.name: Dottore
entries: Diagnosing disease and carrying out the work of a physician is a task few people can properly handle in the 16th century. Educated under experienced physicians and carrying out their work by combining ancient knowledge and existing science, doctors are a vital part of any society; in the Venice region, where many of them trained at the famed University of Padua, they are particularly adept at treating wounds.

items.name: Lone One
entries: The celestials who live in the dark corners of the world and away from prying eyes are sometimes called l'ombra, the shadow but not because of their alignment or deeds. They prefer solitude and peace rather than actively engaging with humans and other species. They seclude themselves in a suitable place where they probably won't be bothered, and then they protect that place, grow a garden of plants, adopt pets, or do other similar activities in a place they call home. Their main struggle is to recall what happened to them in their lives, as they are aware that they once lived as humanoids. They can never shake the feeling of forgetting something, and leaving important things behind. Most of them engage in divination magic because of that, rather than focusing on their possible innate spellcasting abilities

items.name: Radiant One
entries: Radiant ones usually seek retribution upon evil doers to the best of their abilities. They usually pose as law enforcement, soldiers, vigilantes, city guards, hunters, crusaders or similar humanoids to effectively fight against those which they consider evil.

monsterFluff.name: Caladrius
entries: These birds are said to visit the ones with an illness and carry good fortune to them. Arcane researchers report that, they are snow-white birds, or majestic owls that inspire the beholders their bright beauty.

items.name: Angelo Misericordioso
entries: The merciful ones usually act as healers, soothsayers, or similarly helpful roles while drawing as little attention to themselves as possible.

monsterFluff.name: Gondoliers
entries: The canals of Venice are world famous and filled with gondolas rowed by these sturdy and seasoned people. Gondoliers are experts in guiding their gondolas and listening to the city of Venice. However, some of them carry mysteries more than they let on: hiding under their innocuous looks are a cunning nature and an ability to gaze beyond the veil.

entries.name: Buried within History
entries: When the Romans took over the Italian peninsula, the remains of Etruscan civilization were buried deep or were embraced by the Romans. However, some vengeful spirits remain; the brave warriors of old, valiant sailors of the coasts and they are all but forgotten.

entries.name: Lost Glory
entries: These warriors of old seek glory, loathe their successors and desire to kill whoever stands in their way. They seek their lost glory among the catacombs, buried places, canals, and deep forests within the Italian peninsula, and if they are ever spotted near Venice, they sometimes walk through the canals and lagoons with magical nets, sifting through the silt and sediment for lost treasures from their past to help in their fruitless vengeance.

monsterFluff.name: Il Caduto
entries: Monstrous and Dreadful. They are driven mostly by their hatred and an urge to kill. They plot their movements beforehand and attempt to strike at the hearts of their enemies with their overwhelming power. They look normal most times but when they reveal their true shape, it is usually the last sight that any mortal witnesses.

monsterFluff.name: Il Mazaròl
entries: Only those with a soul stinking with sin and corruption can meet with Il Mazaròl, and few can survive to tell the tale. Risen as a fiend from the corpses of false witnesses, corrupted merchants, and the sinners that stayed silent in dire times, Il Mazaròl is a grotesque being with elegance, manners, and horns that pierce its own eyes. Cursed with blindness, it sees by feeling the weight of consciences around it–smelling souls heavy with guilt and sin. How Il Mazaròl pierced the veil and found itself in our world is a mystery, but many suspect that it must be drawn to this world by the will of an expert conjurer who knows what he or she is doing.

entries.name: Breathing Fire
entries: They are what remain of sacrificed souls who were thrown into the fires of endless torment and who clawed their way out through sheer hatred. They look for revenge and retribution, and if they cannot find it they take out their malic on whatever may fall in their path. Appearing as a skeleton or zombie with cracks in their body filled with red hot flame or white fire traces, they are a sight not easily forgotten. They can control fire, and are immune to it as most fiends are.

entries.name: Servants of Evil
entries: They are usually conjured by cultists as a means to terrorize their enemies, inflict fear upon them, or as a punishment for a fellow cultist, an adversary, or a rival to condemn their soul for eternity. It is also possible for humanoids filled with hatred and fury to rise as Il Rosso after they suffer a deadly injury during a fire.

monsterFluff.name: Ladropaura
entries: This entity is the growing manifestation of ancient angers, growing fat off the pestilence, corruption, and excess of the Venetian Lagoon. Its age is unknown, but it is said to be one of the great ancient beasts of old. It can take many forms, but its original is that of a gargantuan serpent with tusks and thorns along its rubbery, acidic body. Its eyes are vacant and reflect the stars above. It has long arms to grasp and push it through the shallower waters of the lagoon, though it is comfortable in deeper waters as well. It has a giant toothy maw on its undercarriage which it reserves for larger and more magical meals, though it often subsists on smaller fare that it eats through its front baleen-filled mouth. When it takes other forms, which it can only do temporarily, it appears as a cloud of swamp gas, or a gaunt elf with grey, mottled skin. When in its natural monstrous form, its spikes can resemble bricolle, the wooden poles in the lagoon used for navigation and as pier columns. Sometimes the monster lies in shallow water and feeds off the thoughts, dreams, and evils of the city.

entries.name: Unnoticed
entries: These fiends are almost-human. Their flesh, body, eyes, mind, and everything is the same as a human. They are in their own body, no fiend possessed them, but they cease to be humans anymore. They lost their souls, gave up on their breath, or some other vile deed transformed what they are into mere fiends.

entries.name: Silently Dangerous
entries: They are not worse than a human with evil intentions, but they hide what they truly are and await their time for malice. Even adept spellcasters cannot easily identify these fiends. Thus, they can be anywhere, hiding in plain sight–smiling at your face or shaking your hand.

entries.name: Mark for Greater Evil
entries: Their most dangerous threat is to leave a mark for a bigger and more dangerous hunter. They silently and subtly mark a creature they desire, and the marked ones usually become the targets of more dangerous devils, evildoers, and deceivers.

entries.name: Silent Danger
entries: These abominations have tremendous patience, maybe exceeding so-called immortal species or spirits that witness the ends of civilizations. They feed off flesh and take over brains, synergizing with the body as long as it can endure. There is no way to tell them apart from ordinary masks. They are not like the mimics of wizards found in dungeons. They do not negotiate, they do not speak. They only wait for the right moment to strike. They can wait for eternities in tombs, in excavation sights, in sunken ships, or even everyday locations where no one would suspect a mask to be the cause of so many recent deaths.

entries.name: Face Off
entries: They destroy their target's face and consciousness. They take complete control and commit horrible acts. Without any indication of emotion, without a shred of empathy, living masks use their husks for terrible ends.

entries.name: Obscure Intentions
entries: Each living mask has different intentions. They commit unspeakable acts, yet their end goal is often inscrutable. Some plot great massacres, while some try to reach interesting artifacts. Some kidnap people, and some even try to have children; while a humanoid is adorned with these masks, even the Devil does not know what it plans.

entries.name: Evil Walkers
entries: They are witches that walk in the night with ill intent. They aim to disturb sleeping souls, bind spirits to their cause, and unleash horror upon the world. Each circle or coven formed by the malandanti carries its own purpose, whether it be to seek power beyond imagination or revenge against those who wronged them.

entries.name: Spreading Rot
entries: The malandanti create rot to harm the crops, rain death on their enemies, or to cripple trade of a specific good. Their rot is sinister and deadly, for they do not reveal their true nature immediately.

entries.name: Soul Hex
entries: Souls trapped in the afterlife or on their way to be at peace can be interrupted by the malandanti. A soul trapped by their hexes fuels their more powerful and deadlier spells and enables them to further their terrible goals.

monsterFluff.name: Marionette
entries: Beware! Never trust a puppet with strings of silk; don't look at their eyes! Never stay alone with them! Never let them touch your hands, and under any circumstances, DO NOT ATTEMPT to use them!
Dangerous! These creatures haunt you, hunt you, destroy you, and eventually capture your soul! If you try to control them, they will control you instead!

Possession! These horrible creatures are not demons or devils, but they are surely as deadly as a devil with fiery horns. They slowly come to life with evil intent, or they are brought to life by some evil plot, no one knows, but they are cunning, patient, and hellbent on mayhem. A marionette deserted in an alley, under a bed, or behind a counter can be used for entertainment if one is agile with such crafts. However, some of them control their masters and their strings are their own.

entries.name: The Heart Beats!
entries: If one were foolish enough to peel away the layers of clothing on the marionette, one would see a gaunt ribcage covering their torso and a heart seemingly made of stone or marble inside it. When the puppet possesses someone, its heart starts to twist and twist, in a macabre approximation of life.

monsterFluff.name: Oltremarino
entries: The life of the Doge is under their protection. These special infantry from the Dalmatian territories–hence their alternate name, schiavoni (meaning 'slavs')–are the crack troops of the Venetian army, and the trusted guards of the Doge's Palace.

monsterFluff.name: Ombra
entries: A shadow looms over the Adriatic sea, following the orders by the Doge's Palazzo–unseen, dangerous and deadly. Gathering information for the Most Serene Republic and ensuring its safety, the ombra could be anyone on the street, in a shop, in a crowd, in a church, or on a ship. It is usually advised that one should even be suspicious of their own shadow.

monsterFluff.name: The Order Of The Scepter & Serpent
entries: Rumored to have been founded in the city of Pergamon in Anatolia, the Order is devoted to Asclepius, ancient Greek god of medicine. The symbol of their organization is the asklepian, a rod with a serpent entwined around it, and members of the order are committed to the curing of diseases, tending to the sick, and researching new methods of healing. It is part clerical and part scientific order, and many of the first pharmacies of Europe are secret meeting places of this beneficent order. In the generations since its founding, the Order has developed a resentment and rivalry with the Cult of Bacchus, which it sees as a main vector for many of the maladies of the day due to its hedonistic behavior.

_copy.name: The Order Of The Scepter & Serpent
The Order Of The Scepter & Serpent
The Order Of The Scepter & Serpent

monsterFluff.name: Occultista
entries: Some dark corners of the city are occupied by practitioners of dark arts and followers of dark shadows. They are mostly silent, but they wait with patience and care and pursue dark ambitions shaped by desire and ill-intents.

monsterFluff.name: Ottomans In Venice
entries: The Ottoman Empire has shaken Europe to its foundations since the Battle of Varna and the conquest of Constantinople. Now, it is about to become the greatest power in the world, shaping it according to its desires. They are striving to control the Mediterranean Sea and have become arguably the strongest adversary of Venice. However, the commerce between the two powerful states continues even while hostilities mount. The city of Venice, or its overseas dominions, can host many people from the Ottoman Empire. The privateers are pirates who have pledged their loyalty to the Ottoman sultan and worked towards the goal of making the Mediterranean an Ottoman sea. The levends are the brave sailors of the Ottoman navy and are as fierce as the janissaries are on land. Ottoman officials sometimes visit Venice to establish ties between the two states, and some Ottoman civilians are here for trade or other various reasons.

monsterFluff.name: Patron of the Arts
entries: Many artists are in need of a patron who could support them. These patrons can be nobles, wealthy merchants, curious privateers, or old successful artists with considerable wealth. They care about the arts and want to support artists for various reasons: to show their interest, as a matter of status among their society, to show off to fellow patrons, or other reasons.

entries.name: Venetian Nobility
entries: Nobles of Venice are proud, rich, and powerful. They govern the city and control the political and economic flows within it, including the councils, the navy and military, mercantile enterprises, and even which Doge will be elected. All the noble families of import are recorded in the Golden Book (Libro d'Oro), and the even more important families are also recorded in the Silver Book (Libro d'Argento), which distinguished the supposed original families of Venice. These noble houses can broadly be divided into Old Houses (Case vecchie), New Houses (Case nuovo), and Ducal House (Case ducali, those families of either Old or New which have had a member elevated to the position of doge). Though it is mandatory for nobility to wear the customary toga and beret related to their station in the government, it is sometimes necessary for members of these houses to don armor and take up arms.

monsterFluff.name: Patrono Delle Navi
entries: The officers of the navy are involved in all sorts of aspects of naval military life, including dealing with deserters, issuing orders of trials, and making the sailors obey the long arm of the law.

monsterFluff.name: Plague Doctor
entries: The plague has killed more than wars have. This has led many people to arm themselves against this disease, to stop it before spreading too much, and to stop it from re-appearing. Trained in the arts of diagnosing the Black Death, plague doctors travel the blighted lands. Some are there to help those in need, while some traverse the fringes of death and shadow, embracing the destructive nature of the plague

monsterFluff.name: Priests Of Venice
entries: In Venice, priests are considered the spiritual leaders of their parishes, guiding the commoners, sailors, officers, and more with their faith and wisdom. They offer their services to people by praying with them, giving them blessings, and offering advice to the community, as well as leading services at the many churches in the city. Known for their kindness and dedication, priests often help the poor, resolve conflicts, and bring comfort to those in need.
When fog settles in, and you hear the creaking of ships and twisting of metal posts, it is best to stay indoors, preferably far away from the windows.

entries.name: Drowned
entries: Ragni are said to be what has become of evil people who drown within sight of a town. They become monsters which stalk the waters at night and when visibility is bad, hoping to catch someone unawares. Perhaps they simply want companionship again, or perhaps they are truly monstrous, no one knows.

entries.name: Dreadful Appearance
entries: They are large creatures with long, spindly, spider-like legs which creak at the joints, resembling the sound of warping wood and metal hinges in the wind. They appear slow and ponderous but can strike with speed and reach when they are near their target. The legs of ragni connect to a sallow abdomen covered in sea-soaked rags. Their bodies are bloated, misshapen, grotesque approximations of the human form–mockeries of what they once were. Their heads do not appear to have eyes but instead have four barbles that grope and feel around a gaping, dripping maw.

entries.name: Servants of Ragni
entries: Evil aberrations called ragna create drowned ones from the corpses touched by their hateful spirit. They rise at a ragna's control and haunt swamps, marshes, and coastal towns. They serve their masters with all their power. When a ragna dies, the drowned ones gain a glimpse of consciousness and regret for what they have done in their mindless service. Some seek retribution against other ragna, while some seek serenity in the loneliness of the world. If a drowned one is free from a ragna control, its Intelligence and Charisma scores become what they were when they were alive.

entries.name: Fungi
entries: Drowned ones carry marine fungi on their skin, and it is deadly to unprepared adventurers. It is deadly to touch and carries poisonous fumes to be unleashed on the living and potentially neutralize them for their vile masters.

entries.name: Driven by Greed
entries: Mammon is a word for money in Aramaic and often used to describe wealth and the greed behind it. It is also a word used to describe one of the lords of the Hells. Some ancient curses, hexes, ill-words, and pacts cause the rise of these servants of Mammon, and any foolish enough to wish for wealth in this way quickly find that they have spelled their own doom.

entries.name: Insatiable Glutton
entries: Red hands have a distinct, insatiable desire for an object, usually gold, and they never have enough. They always desire it with a burning passion and plot to have it no matter what. They lie, persuade, coerce, and conduct disturbing plans to get their hands on what they crave.

entries.name: Different Shapes
entries: Red hands are usually with actual crimsonhued hands, as if their hands were soaked into a pool of blood. When a red hand takes a life or commits evil deeds, the blood color gets darker. Other than their terrifying hands, they usually resemble humans or other humanoids, such as tieflings.

entries.name: Golden Sense
entries: Red hands usually sense any kind of precious material around them and are drawn to it by their nature. They haunt merchants, nobles, seafarers, and any wanderer that attracts their attention.

monsterFluff.name: Royal Artist
entries: Some artists are so talented or well connected that they have the support of a noble house, covering their expenses and protecting them in times of need. Some of these artists share a keen interest in arcane arts and sometimes they are hired to help the house, train their children, protect their interests and investigate mysterious events on their behalf.

monsterFluff.name: Sanctae Romane Ecclesiae
entries: In the esteemed hierarchy of the Sanctae Romanae Ecclesiae, cardinals occupy an exalted position as spiritual leaders, scholars, and advisors to the Pope. Their theological expertise, their guidance in spiritual matters, and wise advice for the Pope are the pillars of the Roman Church. Cardinals often mediate critical decisions and diplomatic matters on behalf of the Holy See, and they are entrusted with safeguarding the doctrines of Christianity and guiding the faithful.

monsterFluff.name: Savio del Consiglio
entries: These magistrates are an important part of the city, as they wield important power and serve as augurs for ill days, dire sunsets, and vicious storms. They are tasked with assisting the city's administration, but some of them have gravitated towards protecting the city to a greater extent. These sages have unlocked arcane vitality and use their power to assist and empower La Serenìssima.

monsterFluff.name: Savio del Ogliari
entries: Some sages of the city dedicate themselves to the maritime efforts of the Republic and put their hard work into the naval administration, helping with operational efficiency, carrying out punishments, and setting an example for future generations.

monsterFluff.name: Seafarer
entries: Some commoners in La Serenìssima answered the call of the sea and dedicated their lives to working in sailing vessels. They are sturdy, curious, and wellknown in the Mediterranean world for their resolve and abilities. Some are merchants, some are adventurers, and some fill the ranks of ships to fight for their Republic.

monsterFluff.name: Signore della Notte
entries: The lords of the night are the grim backbone of the administration of Venice, the menacing law enforcers of the city. They operate at night, eliminating any threat to the city's smooth operation with their expertise in their jobs.

monsterFluff.name: State Inquisitor
entries: Some crimes require specialists who are willing to go beyond some norms and even limits of morality to solve crimes in Venice. The state inquisitors are mysterious figures tasked with uncovering conspiracies and rooting out corruption. They operate independently, answer only to the highest authorities, and wield almost limitless power to interrogate, investigate, and prosecute those who threaten the city's order. With their sharp intellect and resolve, they guard the benefits of the Republic from the shadows.

monsterFluff.name: Street Acrobat
entries: Life as a traveling entertainer can be hard; they perform from town to town or street to street and rely on the kindness (and coinage) of strangers. Even if they don't seem like warriors, their keen reflexes and physical prowess developed from years of performing makes them dangerous in combat, provided they can stay out of arm's reach of their foe.

monsterFluff.name: Street Dancer
entries: Music is an inseparable part of the city, and dancers are right at its core. Capturing the music with their bodies, the festivities of Carnevale and other occasions are better with the existence of the dancers.

monsterFluff.name: Street Actor
entries: The times of Carnevale host many talents in the streets. The actors are one good example. These entertainers of the crowds are proven talents and captivate the hearts of people with their amazing mimicry, humorous performances on stages, and their alluring mannerisms.

monsterFluff.name: Temperatore
entries: The clock-keepers in Venice keep the city running. Some play the part of a humble clock-maker, while others assume roles as members of the city's watch while keeping lanterns lit at night and crafting constructs to help defend the city.

monsterFluff.name: Vendor
entries: Vendors are the heartbeat of Venice's bustling markets, selling goods that range from everyday essentials to rare and exotic items. With their persuasive charm and sharp wits, vendors' shouts inviting people to purchase their wares can be heard echoing along the canals and streets. Whether trading spices, fabrics, or trinkets, vendors bring color and life to the city's streets, making them an essential part of Venetian commerce.

entries.name: Ominous Presence
entries: The strix, although a large vulture, is usually interpreted by sailors as a sign of bad luck and ill omen throughout their voyage. It looms over ships, haunts coasts and sometimes found over shipwrecks staring to the very hearts of anyone who stumbles upon them.

entries.name: Bloody Beak
entries: Those who are unfortunate enough to get close to a strix notices the crimson color on its beak. It's not natural because it's blood. No one dared to check what kind of blood it is, or whose blood it is.

monsterFluff.name: Vetrai, Glassblowers of Venice
entries: Special glass types that are manufactured in Venice are almost as important as silk, and those who work in this treasured trade guard its secrets with their lives. Glassblowers have special conditions compared to other citizens of the city. They can't leave the island of Murano without permission, but at the same time they are held in high regard in society and afforded more opportunities for social advancement than an average non-patrician Venetian. Additionally, some glassblowers furtively and carefully work on melding their glass arts with arcane secrets.

entries.name: Blinding Light
entries: The finest creations of the glassblower masters of Murano found their breath with magic that captures and reflects light. These golems are the finest works within the storied creations of Murano, known only by a few who dwell in the matters of the arcane. These marvelous golems capture light and unleash a blinding radiance to disable enemies and protect secrets.

entries.name: Translucent
entries: They are hard to detect and very agile, unlike other golem creations. They can absorb light and vanish into thin air, becoming invisible even in broad daylight and at the corner of everyone's eyes.

entries.name: Cutting Edge
entries: Their edge is so sharp that even the hardest skin or heaviest armor can't escape their blows. They cut so deep that even a creature's connection to the weave can be severely damaged.

monsterFluff.name: Veteran of Venice
entries: In Venetian society, war heroes, seasoned sailors, long-term successful officers, and others who proudly served the Republic are held in high esteem, and their contributions are celebrated widely. These veterans are experts in times of war and usually spend their days honoring the Republic and protecting it in dangerous circumstances.

entries.name: Trickster
entries: The vivo usually excels at creating illusions and temporarily creating actual materials on a whim. They live in glades, coastal areas, and mostly away from human eyes. However, their extremely curious nature occasionally makes them visit human settlements and maybe even dwell in cities.

entries.name: Different Sizes
entries: The vivo are usually Small, but they can turn themselves into Medium or Tiny sized as well, to help them hide better. They sometimes join seafaring adventures disguised as humans or tiny creatures to avoid the eyes and help the crew or make their lives miserable.

table.name: Barbarian Legendary Inspirations Deck
rows: The next time you Rage, your Rage can end only if you fall {@condition unconscious} or you end it voluntarily.
You can cast spells and concentrate on them while Raging until you finish a long rest.
You can Rage one additional time until you finish a long rest.
During the next three turns, when you use your Reckless Attack, the creatures you hit don't gain Advantage against you as a result of Reckless Attack mechanics.
The next time you score a critical hit, your Rage Damage Bonus and Strength modifier are doubled as well.
During your next Rage, add your Rage Damage to your AC as well.
The next time you enter Rage, you gain an additional resistance. Choose one from: force, psychic, thunder, cold, or poison.
On your turn, you can use a bonus action to regain hit points equal to your hit die ({@dice 1d12}) + Constitution modifier.
You have {@sense blindsight} within 30 feet for 10 minutes. For the benefit, you must not be Raging.
For the next minute, when you roll a critical hit, enemies that have less than half of their hit point maximum are {@condition frightened}.
The next time a condition is applied to you, you can end it by entering Rage as a Reaction.
You add your proficiency bonus to the next three Initiative rolls.
For the next minute, you add your Rage Damage to any Strength check you make.
The next time you are raging, you are immune to one of the following damage types: bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing.

The next time you are raging, you are immune to one of the following conditions: {@condition blinded}, {@condition charmed}, {@condition deafened}, {@condition frightened}, {@condition paralyzed}, {@condition poisoned}, {@condition prone}, {@condition restrained}, or {@condition stunned}.

When you take the Attack action in the next three turns, you can use a bonus action to make an Unarmed Strike. The attack deals an additional {@damage 1d4} poison damage. The poison damage increases at certain barbarian levels: 5th ({@damage 2d4}), 11th ({@damage 3d4}), 16th ({@damage 4d4}).

The next time you are Raging, when you score a critical hit, you apply a condition to the creature until the end of your next turn: {@condition prone}, {@condition stunned}, {@condition blinded}, or {@condition deafened}. It can be used each time you score a critical hit against a creature for the duration of that Rage.
For one hour, you double your proficiency bonus on skills that you are proficient with.
For the next minute, you add your Charisma modifier to your Armor Class (for Unarmored Defense only).
The next time you are Raging, you have a flying speed equal to your walking speed.

table.name: Bard Legendary Inspirations Deck
rows: For your next turn, you can cast {@spell blade ward} as a bonus action.

Choose up to five humanoids who can hear you. They become friendly towards you for 5 minutes and do not become hostile at the end of this effect's duration. This card can only be played after you have given a performance (speech, music, storytelling, etc.) that relates to your Bard College tradition, or whatever is permissible by your GM.

The next time you cast {@spell vicious mockery} or {@spell bane}, the damage die is increased to d6 instead of d4. When you spend this card, you can cast one immediately (as an action) without expending a spell.
You can give three allies of your choice the benefits of the {@spell heroism} spell without expending a spell slot.
The target of your fiery insults is under the effects of the {@spell vicious mockery} spell and takes {@damage 1d6} fire damage. You can target two humanoids at the same time with this effect.
You can cast {@spell thunderwave} as a bonus action. In addition, those who fail the saving throw are {@condition stunned} until the start of their next turn.
You can cast the {@spell create food and water} spell without expending a spell slot and even if the spell is not one of your known spells.
During the next short rest, you can increase the die your allies roll for Song of Rest – for instance {@dice 1d8} instead of {@dice 1d6}.

Choose three creatures who can hear you. Each target makes a Wisdom saving throw; on a failure, the target takes {@damage 3d6} psychic damage and has to use its reaction to make a melee attack against a creature that is within reach of the target. If there are no creatures within range, the target takes another {@damage 1d6} psychic damage. On a successful save, the target takes half damage and does not make an attack.
You can cast the {@spell clairvoyance} spell once without expending a spell slot and without needing the spell on your spell list (it does not get added to your known spells).
You can cast the {@spell slow} spell once without expending a spell slot.
You can cast the {@spell hypnotic pattern} spell once without expending a spell slot.
You regain one use of Bardic Inspiration.
You can cast {@spell shatter} as a bonus action without expending a spell slot once.

Choose four creatures who can hear you. These creatures must make a Wisdom saving throw or fall asleep. If they cannot be put to sleep by magic, they become {@condition stunned} until the end of their next turn.
The next time you hit with a weapon, you can cause that target to be under the effect of either the {@spell vicious mockery} or the {@spell Tasha's hideous laughter|PHB|hideous laughter} spell.
You can cast {@spell speak with plants} once without the need for material components.
You regain a spell slot of the highest level available to you (maximum 5th level). In addition, you can cast {@spell suggestion} as a bonus action.
For one hour, you double your proficiency bonus on skills that you are proficient with.
For one hour, you have resistance to psychic, cold, thunder, and poison damage.

table.name: Cleric Legendary Inspirations Deck
rows: When you cast the {@spell sacred flame} cantrip on your next turn, you deal an additional {@damage 1d8} radiant damage.
You can cast the {@spell guiding bolt} spell as a bonus action and without expending a spell slot once.
You can cast the {@spell moonbeam} spell as a bonus action.
You can cast {@spell mirror image} on yourself as a bonus action without expending a spell slot. If {@spell mirror image} is not on your spell list, you can still cast it this time.
You can cast the {@spell daylight} spell once without expending a spell slot.
The next time you cast {@spell bless} or {@spell guidance}, the die is increased to d6 instead of d4.
You can give three allies of your choice the benefits of the {@spell heroism} spell without expending a spell slot.

You can briefly project a copy of yourself to an area within 5 ft. of an ally and no more than 30 ft. away from you. Your copy can administer one touch spell to an ally of your choice before disappearing.
By sharing a personal story related to your faith (duration: minimum one minute), you can grant up to three allies the benefits of the {@spell enhance ability} spell without expending a spell slot.
You gain a flying speed of 60 ft. for five minutes.
You can cast {@spell spirit guardians} without expending a spell slot, and you gain 15 temporary hit points.
You regain a spell slot of your choice (maximum 5th level).

Creatures of your choice in a 20 ft. radius must make a Charisma saving throw; on a failure, they find their will to fight flagging. For the next minute, they have Disadvantage on attack rolls against you or your allies, and if they do hit, they take {@damage 2d6} psychic damage.

Dark tendrils of energy shoot out from you. Make a spell attack roll against up to 3 targets within 30 feet of you. On a hit, each tendril deals {@damage 3d6} necrotic damage, and the target is {@condition grappled}.

Choose four creatures within 15 ft. of you. You may choose to target these creatures with the {@spell beacon of hope} or {@spell bestow curse} spells. You can divide as you wish – for instance, two allies get {@spell beacon of hope} and two enemies get {@spell bestow curse}. You can do this only once and do not need a spell slot to do so.

You can attempt to magically restrain up to 3 creatures within 60 ft. of you. The creatures must make Wisdom saving throws. On a failure, they are {@condition restrained} and take {@damage 4d10} radiant damage. They cannot get out of the restraints through magical means, such as {@spell teleport} or {@spell misty step}. The only way to release the bonds is to break your concentration.
You gain one more use of your Channel Divinity ability before your next rest.
You gain one more use of Divine Intervention to use in the next seven days.
For one hour, you double your proficiency bonus on skills that you are proficient with.
You can cast the {@spell sending} spell without expending a spell slot or needing it on your spell list.

table.name: Druid Legendary Inspirations Deck
rows: For the rest of the day, you are under the effects of the {@spell speak with animals} spell.
Until the end of your next long rest, you are under the effects of the {@spell jump} and {@spell longstrider} spells.
For one hour, you sense any beast, monstrosity, or fey within one mile. By spending an action, you can limit the range up to 120 ft.
When you cast a spell or a cantrip that deals damage, three creatures within 60 ft. of you (you can choose yourself as one) restore {@dice 1d10} hit points.
While in your next Wild Shape, your Armor Class increases by 2.
You can cast the {@spell enlarge/reduce} spell twice without expending a spell slot.
When you enter your next Wild Shape form, you can immediately cast a spell as a reaction.
The next spell you cast does not expend a spell slot (maximum 5th level).
While in your next Wild Shape form, you can cast spells and ignore components for the first minute, unless the components have monetary value.
The next time you use your Wild Shape, you can turn into a monstrosity (max CR 2).
For the next hour, you are under the effects of the {@spell speak with plants} spell.
The next time you use your Wild Shape you can turn into a fiend (max CR 1).
For the next hour, you are under the effects of the {@spell see invisibility} spell and notice any shapechangers that you can see.
For the next 10 minutes, you can walk on water and similar liquid surfaces.
While in your next Wild Shape, your attacks deal an extra {@damage 1d4} necrotic damage. The damage increases in certain druid levels: {@damage 2d4} (5th), {@damage 3d4} (11th), {@damage 4d4} (16th).

While in your next Wild Shape, whenever you take damage that would drop your beast form to 0 HP, you can use your reaction to stay in beast form by expending spell slots and regaining {@dice 1d6} hit points for each spell slot you expend.
You can cast the {@spell call lightning} spell without expending a spell slot.
For the next minute you have resistance to a damage type of your choice.
A fey of your GM's choice comes to your aid (whether it be a combat or non-combat encounter).
You regain a use of your Wild Shape.

table.name: Fighter Legendary Inspirations Deck
rows: You gain the usage of another Fighting Style for the next ten minutes.
The next time you use your Second Wind, you roll another {@dice d10} and remove one level of exhaustion, if any.
For the next minute, you can treat a melee weapon without the Heavy property as if it has Light property.
The next time that you fail on a Dexterity saving throw against a trap or a magical effect that you can see, you can choose to succeed instead.
For the next minute, when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, instead of dealing damage, you can grapple or shove the creature 5 ft. away from you.
Non-magical difficult terrain does not cost you an extra movement for two rounds.
You can use {@action Dash} as a bonus action for the next minute.
Add your proficiency bonus to your damage rolls for the next three rounds.
Attack twice when an Opportunity Attack is available.
Any attack within 5 feet of you allows you to Attack once using your Reaction.
You can take the {@action Dodge} action as a bonus action on your turns for the next {@dice 1d6} rounds.
For three rounds, your movements do not trigger an Opportunity Attack.
For the next minute, your Armor Class increases by 2.
Until the end of your next long rest, you are proficient with all saving throws.
For the next minute, you have {@sense blindsight} with a range of 15 feet.

Until the end of your next long rest, whenever you use your Action Surge, enemies that can see you must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition frightened} by you until the end of your next turn.
You can use your bonus action to use the {@action Help} action for an ally that you can see within 30 ft. of you that can see or hear you.
For the next three rounds, all attack rolls have Disadvantage against you.
You are under the effects of the {@spell jump} spell for 1 hour.
You gain another usage of Action Surge until the end of your next long rest.

table.name: Monk Legendary Inspirations Deck
rows: You regain {@dice 1d4} ki points.
For the next three rounds, you add your proficiency bonus to your Armor Class.
You can take the {@action Dash} action as a bonus action.
For the next minute, you have Advantage on all saving throws.
For the next minute your Martial Arts die counts as if it is one category higher (for example, if you are Level 7, it is normally d6. With this ability, it counts as d8). It cannot exceed d12.
For the day, when you score a critical hit, you regain a ki point.
You can take the {@action Dodge} action as a bonus action.
For the next three rounds, ranged attacks have Disadvantage against you.
For one hour, you don't take fall damage and are immune to the {@condition prone} condition.
For the next 10 minutes, your jump distance is tripled and difficult terrain does not cost you extra movement.
For the next minute, you have resistance to non-magical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.
For the next minute, your unarmed strikes deal extra radiant or necrotic damage (your choice when you use this feature) equal to your Wisdom modifier.

The next time you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, instead of dealing damage, you can apply one of the conditions on the target if it's a creature: {@condition blinded}, {@condition deafened}, {@condition prone} or {@condition stunned}.
For your next ranged attack, you can apply a ki feature on a hit.
The {@spell invisibility} spell is cast on you.
The {@spell see invisibility} spell is cast on you.
You can cast the {@spell misty step} spell three times without expending a spell slot until you finish a long rest.
You can spend your ki points to heal yourself. For each point spent right after this feature, you restore {@dice 1d6} hit points.
You can use your ki points to touch a downed creature. For each point spent right after this feature, it regains {@dice 1d4} hit points.
You regain all of your expended ki points.

table.name: Paladin Legendary Inspirations Deck
rows: You regain one use of Divine Sense.
Your Lay on Hands pool is replenished.
For one minute you can change your fighting style to another paladin option. You cannot change more than once, and after one minute, you revert to your original style.
You regain the use of your Channel Divinity.
You regain a spell slot of the highest level available to you (maximum 5th level).
You can cast the {@spell fireball} spell without expending a spell slot. You can cast this spell even if it is not on your spell list.
For the next minute, any healing you do is increased by {@dice 1d8}.
When you hit with an attack, you can then do an unarmed strike attack as a bonus action. This unarmed strike deals an extra {@damage 1d6} radiant in addition to your unarmed damage.
For the next 3 rounds, you have Advantage on Concentration checks.

You conjure three ancestral spirits to fight alongside you or give you and your allies aid. The spirits can make one melee or ranged attack each; they use your attack bonus. On a hit, they each deal {@damage 2d6} radiant damage. Alternatively, each of the spirits can touch one willing creature and give {@dice 2d6} healing. After their actions, the spirits disappear.
You can cast {@spell protection from evil and good} as a bonus action and it can affect three allies within 15 ft. of you.
For the next minute, you have Advantage on all Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) checks. In addition, the next time you hit, you can cast {@spell dispel evil and good} as a bonus action.

You can attempt to magically restrain up to 3 creatures within 60 ft. of you. The creatures must make Wisdom saving throws. On a failure, they are {@condition restrained} and take {@damage 4d10} radiant damage. They cannot get out of the restraints through magical means, such as {@spell teleport} or {@spell misty step}. The only way to release the bonds is to break your concentration.
The next time you hit with an attack, you can cast {@spell shatter} as a bonus action without expending a spell slot. You don't have to have the spell on your paladin list to do this.
You can cast {@spell death ward} on up to 4 creatures of your choice.

The next time you hit with a weapon, you can cause that target to be under the effect of either the {@spell vicious mockery} or the {@spell Tasha's hideous laughter|PHB|hideous laughter} spell. You do not need to have the spell on your spell list.
The next time you cast {@spell bless} or {@spell divine favor}, the die is increased to d6 instead of d4.
Three allies of your choice gain the benefits of the {@spell heroism} spell without expending a spell slot.
Until the next long rest, you have Advantage on Charisma checks when in an urban center that is not hostile to you.
When you hit with a melee attack, two allies of your choice can make attacks as reactions.

table.name: Ranger Legendary Inspirations Deck
rows: You are under the effects of the {@spell animal friendship} spell for the rest of the day.
For the rest of the day, you are under the effects of the {@spell speak with animals} spell.
You regain an expended spell slot of your choice (maximum 5th level).
For the next hour, you can't roll below 15 on the d20 for on your {@skill Stealth} checks.
Until you finish a long rest, you can cast the {@spell invisibility} spell three times without expending a spell slot.

The next time you hit a creature, you force it to succeed on a Constitution saving throw or become vulnerable against a damage type of your choice: bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing until the end of your next turn.
The next time you damage a creature with a weapon attack or a spell, you or an ally within 30 ft. of you regains hit points equal to {@dice 2d8}.
For the next 24 hours, you can cast two druid cantrips of your choice at will.
For the next hour, you can sense the presence of aberration, celestial, fey, fiend, and undead creatures within 60 ft. of you.
For the next 24 hours, you can cast the {@spell find familiar} spell without expending a spell slot and material components.
You gain the usage of another Fighting Style for the next 10 minutes.
You can cast the {@spell detect magic} spell without expending a spell slot.
For your next three Attack actions, you can impose a condition when you hit a creature: halve its speed, {@condition prone} or {@condition stunned} until the end of your next turn.
Until you finish a long rest, you can cast the {@spell pass without trace} spell without expending a spell slot three times.
You have {@sense blindsight} within 30 feet for one hour.
For the next 10 minutes, you learn resistances, vulnerabilities, and immunities of creatures that you can see.
For your next three Attack actions, you can pin your enemies down to their spots if you hit them. Their movement becomes 0 until the end of your next turn.
For one minute, you add your Wisdom modifier to your attack rolls or damage rolls (You must declare which one before dice results are announced).
For your next hit, you double your Dexterity modifier for the damage.
For the next three rounds, you can make another attack when you take the Attack action.

table.name: Rogue Legendary Inspirations Deck
rows: Until the end of your next turn, you can use the Sneak Attack feature even if you don't meet its requirements.
For the next 10 minutes, you understand lies when you hear them.
For the next 10 minutes, you can't roll below 15 on skill checks which you are proficient with.
For the next 1 minute, any Wisdom or Intelligence check made against you has Disadvantage.
The {@spell invisibility} spell is cast on you.
Until you finish a long rest, you can cast two wizard cantrips of your choice. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for those cantrips.
The next time you use your Cunning Action, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Dexterity modifier.
Until you finish a long rest, you have proficiency in a saving throw of your choice.
You can cast the {@spell detect thoughts} spell three times without expending a spell slot. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability modifier.
For the next three rounds, you can use two bonus actions instead of one.
Until you finish a long rest, you can cast the {@spell thunderwave} spell three times. It does not need to be on your spell list, and you do not need to expend spell slots.
You can cast the {@spell shield} spell three times without expending a spell slot.
Once until you finish a long rest, you can give yourself +10 bonus on an attack roll before the GM declares if it's a hit or not.
For the next minute, you can cast the {@spell knock} spell at will.
The next time you use your Cunning Action, the attacks against you have Disadvantage until the end of your next turn.
For one minute, if you roll 18 or higher on an attack roll, it is counted as a critical hit for you.
For one minute, when you have Advantage on an attack roll, you can reroll one of the dice once.
For the next ten minutes, you understand every language you hear.
For the next minute, no attack can have an Advantage against you.
When you roll for your Sneak Attack, you add an additional d6 to the damage total for 1 minute.

table.name: Sorcerer Legendary Inspirations Deck
rows: For the next 10 minutes, you can use a Metamagic Option that you don't already have.
For the next minute, whenever you use your Font of Magic feature, you regain a sorcery point.
Your spell save DC is increased by 2 for the next minute.
For the next minute, you have Advantage on Constitution saving throws.
You regain {@dice 3d6} hit points.
You can cast {@spell fireball} once without expending a spell slot in the next minute.
You are immune to fall damage until you finish a long rest.
Each creature within 30 ft. you must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be {@condition blinded} for 1 minute. Failed creatures can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of their turns.
The next time you cast a spell, the target has Disadvantage on its saving throw.
For the next 10 minutes, you have resistance to a damage type of your choice.
You can cast the {@spell fly} spell once, targeting yourself, without expending a spell slot.
For the next minute, if you are targeted by a spell, the caster must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or take necrotic damage equal to your Charisma modifier + sorcerer level.
The next time you spend Sorcery Points, you regain temporary HP equal to {@dice 1d6} for each Sorcery Points spent.

The next time you use your Font of Magic feature to create a spell slot, a spellcaster within 60 ft. of you also gains the spell slot and can use it to cast spells for 1 hour. The maximum level for the spell slot is Level 5.
The next time you use your Metamagic feature, you don't spend Sorcery Points.
The next time you use your Metamagic feature, you can affect the spell with another Metamagic that is known to you by spending the normal costs and following its rules.
For the next minute, you can add your Charisma modifier to the damage of your Sorcerer cantrips.
The next time you deal damage with a Sorcerer spell, you can reroll one of the damage dice but must use the new roll.
You replenish {@dice 1d4} Sorcery Points.
Your expended Sorcery Points are replenished.

table.name: Warlock Legendary Inspirations Deck
rows: For the next 10 minutes, you have another spell slot. Its level is equal to your warlock spell slots.
You choose a spell from your patron's spell list. You can cast that spell three times without expending a spell slot.
For two hours, you gain the benefits of a Pact Boon that you do not possess.

When you cast a spell that deals a type of damage from the following list, you can change that damage type to one of the other listed types: acid, cold, fire, lightning, poison, thunder. You can do so three times until you finish your next long rest.
For the next hour, you gain the benefits of an Eldritch Invocation that you do not know. You still must meet the prerequisites.
The {@spell darkness} spell is cast centered on you and you can see clearly in it.

Until you finish a long rest, you gain two 1st-level spell slots and one 2nd-level spell slots apart from your warlock spells. You can use them to cast appropriate spells. They can be replenished with a short rest, until they expire when you finish a long rest.
For your next four attacks, you deal an additional {@damage 1d6} force damage.
For the next minute, whenever you deal damage to a target, you gain {@dice 1d8} temporary hit points.
Until you finish a long rest, you can't be {@condition charmed} or {@condition frightened}.
For the next hour, you are under the effects of the {@spell detect evil and good} and the {@spell protection from evil and good} spells.
For the next hour, your mind cannot be read with magic and any spell that analyzes whether you are lying or not determines you are being truthful.
For the next minute, spells you cast cannot be affected by {@spell counterspell} or {@spell dispel magic}.
The next warlock spell you cast does not expend a spell slot. This feature does not work for Mystic Arcanum spells.
For the next warlock spell you cast with your Pact Magic spell slots, you are counted as if you are using a spell slot of one level higher.
When you roll a critical hit with a weapon or a warlock cantrip in the next minute, you add your proficiency bonus to the damage.
For the next minute, you reduce incoming damage by an amount equal to your Charisma modifier.
You can cast {@spell vampiric touch} once without expending a spell slot.
You can immediately detect illusions and invisible creatures within your sight and notice shapechangers until you finish a long rest.
You immediately gain the benefits of a short rest.

table.name: Wizard Legendary Inspirations Deck
rows: You can replace one of the spells you prepared with another one in your spellbook.
The next time you use your Arcane Recovery, you regain spell slots as if you were one level higher.
You choose a 1st level spell. Until you finish a long rest, you can cast it at will.
You change a cantrip you know with another cantrip from the wizard spell list.
You can cast a spell you know without expending a spell slot once.
When you finish your next long rest, you can prepare spells as if you are two levels higher for that day.
When you expend your last spell slot in the next hour, you gain temporary hit points equal to your level.
When you take damage or are {@condition blinded}, {@condition stunned}, or {@condition paralyzed}, you regain a spell slot of 1st or 2nd levels.
You can't roll below 10 on Intelligence checks for the next ten minutes.
For 1 minute, you have Advantage on Strength, Dexterity and Constitution saving throws.
When you cast a spell that requires concentration, that concentration can't be broken due to taking damage. This effect applies to only one spell.
For the next hour, you are under the effects of the {@spell detect magic} and {@spell see invisibility} spells.
For the next spell you cast, you don't need to provide material components.
When a spell is cast within 60 ft. of you, you can cast {@spell counterspell} without expending a spell slot. You can do this three times until you finish a long rest.
You can cast {@spell dispel magic} three times without expending a spell slot until you finish a long rest.
Choose a 2nd level spell from your spell book. You can cast it at will until you finish a long rest.
When you cast a spell that deals acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage, you can change the damage type with another damage type on the list.
Until you finish a long rest, you are proficient with light, medium, and heavy armor, as well as shields.
The next time you use the Arcane Recovery feature, the {@spell mage armor} spell is cast on you for 24 hours.
Until you finish a long rest, you have a copy of your highest spell slot (maximum 5th level).

Close relatives

Single parent

rows: You have no family
Close relatives

Your parent is working in a city far away and occasionally sends you letters.
Picked to be trained as a mercenary or soldier from birth

rows: None
1d4 - 1 (minimum one)
