Forte Sant'Andrea greatly expanded and updated the previous fortifications in lieu of the Italian Wars and the looming threats of the Ottoman ships, and though it is formidable, it is still a work in progress.

A company of {@creature oltremarino|EchoesOfRenaissance|oltremarino} guards and condottieri are stationed at the fort, as well as several arsenalotti overseeing the construction efforts. There is still one wall that is not fully completed, and there are only a few cannons. There has been talk of laying a defensive chain across the lagoon mouth like the one which guarded the Golden Horn in Constantinople, but that plan has not materialized yet.

entries.name: Sidequests
entries: These quests can take place within the adventure module {@i A Serenade for the Damned} or can be treated as standalone adventures.
Creature names followed by the symbol 🔔 are from the 5e SRD. Creature names followed by the symbol ⁜ are from previous Historica Arcanum releases.

entries.name: Lurking Dread

entries: {@b Recommended Level:} 2
{@b District Locations:} Santa Croce
{@b Quest Summary:} A narrow canal hidden from direct sunlight is known for its unlucky nature. Gondoliers have gone missing, and it is up to the adventurers to get to the bottom of the problem.
{@b Possible Rewards:} 50 gd, common magic item

Tucked deep within sestiere Santa Croce is a narrow canal that rarely sees direct sunlight. Gondoliers who use it know that the useful shortcut it provides must be weighed against grave dangers. The canal is believed to be haunted, and a few gondoliers and passengers have disappeared over the past few years. Many of the gondoliers refuse to believe the stories, but even locals living in nearby buildings have heard strange noises and drowned cries on certain evenings. The adventurers are tasked with getting to the bottom of what is going on, and eliminating or expelling the danger. If the adventurers are aware of Angós, the Disrupter of Waves and think to ask about it, the gondoliers will either not know who the adventurers are referring to, or they will say, "Angós would never kill gondoliers. This must be something else."

entries.name: Developments
entries: The adventurers need to stake out the canal, preferably during one of the darkest nights of the month. No fire light illuminates the canal normally, so if the adventurers do not have their own illumination or darkvision, the area will be heavily obscured. A {@creature canali plaguebeast|EchoesOfRenaissance} lurks in the waters, but it is an opportunistic hunter. It won't attack a full party unless it is defending itself: it will prefer to grab someone set apart from the group or someone who appears smaller and weaker. The canal is only 7 feet wide; the buildings on either side are over 30 feet tall, and the water is only 6 feet deep.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The gondoliers will offer a monetary reward for getting rid of the threat, either killing the beast or forcing it to leave (50 gd). You can also have the guild offer the adventurers a common magic item if it suits your game.

entries.name: What Do Shadows Think?

entries: {@b Recommended Level:} 2
{@b District Locations:} San Marco
{@b Quest Summary:} Gasparo the wine seller is spooked; he needs help quieting a haunting voice that is ruining his business.
{@b Possible Rewards:} {@item goblet of perspicacity|EchoesOfRenaissance}, {@item decanter of endless wine|EchoesOfRenaissance}

Gasparo, who sells wine under St. Mark's Bell Tower (Campanile) in the Piazza San Marco, is usually a cheery and garrulous man—quick with a smile and a story. He calls the cups of wine he sells ombra, after the shadow of the bell tower that he moves with throughout the day. However, lately he sits glumly in the sun across the piazza from the tower, watching the shadow intently. If asked about his change of mood and location, he will say "the shadow is cursed. It won't leave me alone!" If the adventurers convince Gasparo to tell them more, he will say that he started hearing a "chill voice from beyond the grave."

Gasparo is being haunted by the {@creature ghost} of a young noble woman who was killed by her lover. The ghost knows Gasparo is well-known for his good company, his stories of romance and lost love, and that he is known for not spreading lies. Thus, the ghost has been bothering Gasparo to tell the truth about her story so that her murderer will see justice. On a successful {@dc 13} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Intimidation}) check, the adventurers can convince Gasparo to head back to the bell tower's shadow, where the ghost immediately tries to reach out again. Alternatively, the adventurers could try to reach out to the chill voice themselves, and if they have a reputation of doing good in the city, the ghost can be convinced to speak with them. During the day, when the bell tower casts a shadow, she is able to communicate with the party; however, she is only visible at night and only makes herself visible to those she fully trusts.
The ghost will give the following information to the characters or to Gasparo:

items: Her name in life was Agatia di Selino. She was originally from Candia (Crete), but she and her mother moved to Venice recently. As each day passes, she loses more grip on her past life, so she is desperate to see her killer brought to justice.

She was working as a cleaner and assistant for the Dolfin family, and started a relationship with one of the family's scions, Giovanni Dolfin (LE, human male, early 20s, {@creature Old House Patrizio|EchoesOfRenaissance|patrizio, old house}). Their relationship was secret, but Giovanni promised her much. She knew that nobles are not allowed to marry outside of the noble families, but she had held out hope that true love would triumph.
Her natural talents in math led to her being asked to count stores and calculate costs to help the family's business.

She discovered discrepancies in the numbers and brought these to Giovanni's attention. He promised her that he would look into it. That night, he invited Agatia on a romantic gondola ride. He strangled her in the covered gondola and paid the gondolier to help him dispose of her body.

She doesn't expect Giovanni to be punished by the government for her disappearance, but she wants his reputation destroyed, as she now suspects he was responsible for the discrepancies in the family's accounts.

entries: The adventurers have several ways they could approach a solution to this quest. They could convince Gasparo to spread the story of Agatia and what Giovanni did to her, though it could lead to Gasparo being arrested for "spreading lies" if the party does not have concrete evidence to back up the stories. Evidence or no, the tale of Agatia's murder and the cold-blooded noble lover begins to spread quickly if Gasparo is convinced to spin the tale with a successful {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Intimidation}) check. Alternatively, the party can confront Giovanni directly and avenge Agatia, which would be the fastest solution but one which would lead to more problems for the party. Giovanni travels with {@dice 1d4} condottieri guards at all times. If they go this route, Giovanni will deny any wrongdoing unless he is about to be killed; then he will plead for his life and reveal where he hid her body. He will admit that he was afraid his indiscretions would be exposed, so he silenced her. He, along with another young noble named Bernardo Nani (LE, human male, early 20s, {@creature New House Patrizio|EchoesOfRenaissance|patrizio, new house}) are investing in the slavery trade, buying prisoners from Candia and selling them to Spain, among other locations.

If the party does not want to risk confronting a powerful noble, they could do their own investigations into the Dolfin family's business. If they sneak into the Palazzo Dolfin, they can potentially find the incriminating records in the warehouses on the ground floor (piano terra). A successful {@dc 16} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check will get the party past the 2 condottieri guards, and a successful {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check will give the party all the details they need to reveal that Giovanni and an outside partner have been funneling money away from the family for another venture. Alternatively, the party could pose as merchants wanting to do business with the Dolfins and talk their way in and out of the palazzo. A successful {@dc 14} Charisma ({@skill Deception}) check will get them into the palazzo for a meeting with the patriarch, Delfino Dolfin (LN, human male, late 50s, {@creature Old House Patrizio|EchoesOfRenaissance|patrizio, old house}).

entries.name: Developments
entries: The adventurers can collect enough information to land Giovanni in serious trouble, though mostly due to embezzlement rather than the murder or horrid trade he was involved in. He will be arrested for embezzlement and conspiracy, and he will be disowned by his family. Delfino Dolfin will pay reparations to Agatia's mother, who works as a washer woman at an osteria, and pay for a proper burial for Agatia's body, which, if the party doesn't find it, will be found after Giovanni confesses to everything in custody. Agatia will thank the party before departing the bell tower's shadow.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: For their help and dedication to uncovering the truth, Gasparo will award the adventurers with a {@item goblet of perspicacity|EchoesOfRenaissance} and a {@item decanter of endless wine|EchoesOfRenaissance}.

entries.name: The Merchant Who Loved Me

entries: {@b Recommended Level:} 3
{@b District Locations:} San Marco, Other Islands (Burano and Mazzorbo)

{@b Quest Summary:} A merchant of the Fondaco dei Tedeschi has gone missing, and both Venice and the Holy Roman Empire suspect him of espionage. Either side will pay handsomely for his apprehension, dead or alive.
{@b Possible Rewards:} 250 gd, one use of the {@spell bless} spell each, one common/uncommon magic item

Nikolaus Herel (LN, human male, early 20s, {@creature merchant of Venice|EchoesOfRenaissance}) is a merchant in the Fondaco dei Tedeschi, the headquarters for all Germanic merchants in Venice. The building sits right next to the Rialto Bridge on the Grand Canal. It has warehouses on its ground floor, along with a large courtyard, and upper floors house offices and living quarters of all official Germanic merchants in the city.

Spies of the Council of Ten suspect that Nikolaus was more than just a merchant, however; they believe he was supplying merchant guilds in the Holy Roman Empire with state secrets about lacemaking and other industries. They have records of his visits to the island of Burano, the lacemaking center of Venice, as he and some other merchants were working on exporting Burano lace (legally) to the Holy Roman Empire, but they could find no evidence of any wrongdoing. Now he has disappeared into thin air, apparently—no one in the Fondaco knows where he has gone. In fact, Nikolaus is only a spy in the sense that every merchant shares what they know will give their businesses an advantage, or if the Empire demands it. However, Nikolaus was not a particularly important asset—not until now, at least. His disappearance has alarmed Holy Roman emissaries in the Fondaco, who fear that he discovered very lucrative secrets and has absconded to France or somewhere else with his knowledge. The truth is that neither government is correct: Nikolaus fell head over heels in love, and will do anything for the object of his affection—even scuttle his own career and risk his life.

If the adventurers investigate, either on the Venetian government's or the Fondaco's behalf, they will be followed by the other side: there are spies everywhere in Venice, after all. If the adventurers are hired by the Fondaco, they are allowed to inspect Nikolaus's quarters; if they are working for the Council of Ten, they will have to talk their way, or sneak, into the Fondaco upper floors ({@dc 16}) and break into the room ({@dc 15} Strength [{@skill Athletics}] or thieves' tools). Inside the spartan bedchambers, a successful {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check reveals a loose panel in a wardrobe, behind which is a strip of lace cloth with a note written in what appears to be charcoal, {@i "please, you have kind eyes, good sir. Take me away from here."} The note appears to have been written by someone new to writing, or with a potential physical ailment, as the penmanship is clumsy.

Signs point to the island of Burano and the lacemaking houses. If the adventurers did not find the clue in the bedchambers or were unable to enter the room (if they are working for the Council of Ten, for instance), you can have one of the Council of Ten spies tell them that a young woman from Burano has also gone missing, having not shown up for work today. Burano lies to the northeast of Venice, in an area of the lagoon that was more prominent in earlier centuries when Venice had closer ties to Constantinople; the nearby islands of Torcello and Mazzorbo were especially prominent. When the adventurers pull up to the docks of Burano, they find a sleepy island with a small community of colorful houses, and soon thereafter the sounds of chatting women working at needlepoint can be heard coming from several of the houses lining the fondamente. If the adventurers are working for the Council of Ten, they can head straight for the house with the missing woman; if they are working for the Fondaco, they can procure a list of the houses the merchants visited, and from there discover that a young woman is missing from one of them.

If the adventurers question the workers—all very young women working for an older madam—they can make a {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check. On a success, they find that, although it is normal to be concerned for a missing person, the workers are overly nervous. If they are pressed, they will reveal the following:

items: The missing young woman's name is Bella. She never mentioned a family name.
She arrived recently, and she had no memory of her past.
Her embroidery skills are second to none. However, she never seemed happy.
The women will say that being around Bella made them cheerier, more satisfied with their work, and now that she's gone, everything seems even more laborious and tiresome.

entries: The workers have not seen Nikolaus since the German merchants visited in an official capacity a few days ago. If the adventurers get permission, they can search the living quarters where the women sleep, and search Bella's bunk. They find a piece of cloth, torn by a knife or other sharp object, and a piece of charcoal under her pillow. A {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana} or {@skill Investigation}) or Wisdom ({@skill Perception} or {@skill Survival}) check will pick up a trail leading behind the house and along the back canal; you can tailor the trail to your party. For instance, with a Survival or Perception check, it is the strong scent of wildflowers; with Arcana or Investigation, it is a faint trail of magic, almost like dust caught in the light.

This trail leads to the narrow channel between Burano and the island of Mazzorbo, an island mostly consisting of farmland. Have the adventurers make a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check; on a success, they can follow the trail to Chiesa di Santa Caterina (Church of St. Catherine); however, they also notice that they are being followed by a group of {@dice 1d4} {@creature ombra|EchoesOfRenaissance|ombra, royal spies}. Nikolaus and Bella are hiding in the church and preparing to leave for the mainland at night. They will not fight the party, but they will beg the adventurers to look the other way and let them go. Nikolaus fell in love with Bella at first sight, and Bella needed a ticket out of the lagoon. She doesn't remember her past, but she knows she is not safe here, and every day that passes fills her with more anxiety. A {@spell detect magic} spell will indicate that Bella herself gives off a magical aura; if she is pressed on the issue, she will eventually reveal that she is an {@creature lone one|EchoesOfRenaissance|angelo, lone one}, a type of celestial creature. If she is asked why she didn't escape on her own, she will say that she does not know why, but she saw a vision (with a divination spell) that she must leave with a "person with sandy hair and sad eyes" or she will be trapped forever. She has no destination in mind except to get away from the lagoon.

entries.name: Developments
entries: The adventurers can complete this quest in a number of ways: turning Nikolaus in to the Fondaco or the Council of Ten; turning both of the escapees in; letting them escape; or helping them get to the mainland.

items: If Nikolaus is brought back to the Fondaco dei Tedeschi, he will not be tried for treason, but he will be fired and forced to return to the Holy Roman Empire. On his way out of the city, he will try to escape and return to Bella, but he is shot with crossbow bolts after jumping into the lagoon and trying to swim away. Bella, meanwhile, sadly returns to her work unless one of the party members fits the physical description of "sandy hair and sad eyes"; if that is the case, she will beg them to help her escape. If they do not, she sadly returns to work, and two days later a {@creature hinthial|EchoesOfRenaissance|hinthial, etruscan shade} appears and kills her—its reasons for doing so are unknown. The party will be rewarded 250 gd.

If Nikolaus is turned in to the Council of Ten, they will interrogate him for days, ultimately finding that he did not steal any lacemaking secrets. Bella, meanwhile, sadly returns to her work unless one of the party members fits the physical description of "sandy hair and sad eyes"; if that is the case, she will beg them to help her escape. If they do not, she sadly returns to work, and while Nikolaus is still in a Pozzi prison cell in the Doge's Palace, a {@creature hinthial|EchoesOfRenaissance|hinthial, etruscan shade} appears and kills her. The party will be rewarded 250 gd.

If the adventurers let Nikolaus and Bella escape, they are eternally grateful. Nikolaus will give them 50 gd, and Bella will give them a blessing: each of the adventurers has 1 use of the {@spell bless} spell, which they can cast without needing spell slots or spellcasting ability. The ombra spies that were following the party, if they have not been shaken, will follow Nikolaus and Bella and apprehend them if the adventurers do not stop them.

If the adventurers offer to accompany Nikolaus and Bella to the mainland, Bella will be grateful but nervous, as it is not what she saw in her vision. They will have to take boats or traverse several marshy islands between Mazzorbo and the mainland. A {@creature hinthial|EchoesOfRenaissance|hinthial, etruscan shade} will attack them. It can walk on water, so the boats do not hinder it. If the hinthial is defeated, the adventurers can gain one common or uncommon magic item, which falls out of the hinthial's nets.

entries.name: In the Murk and Mire

entries: {@b Recommended Level:} 2–3
{@b District Locations:} San Marco, Castello, Other Islands

{@b Quest Summary:} A beloved engineer has not returned home, and his wife will reward the adventurers if they look into it. The quest leads to inquiring with the fishermen at Riva degli Schiavoni before it ends at the lair of some sea monsters at the mouth of the Adriatic.
{@b Possible Rewards:} {@item rapier +1|DMG|+1 rapier}, 250 gd and 120 sl

Bartolomea (NG, human female, late 30s, {@creature merchant of Venice|EchoesOfRenaissance}) runs the White Lion Tavern (Osteria di Leon Bianco) while her husband Massimo, an engineer, often travels to other parts of the Venetian territories for construction projects. He recently went to Zara (Zadar) and was expected to return a few days ago. If the adventurers frequent the White Lion, they will notice that Bartolomea is not her usual cheerful self, and if they offer to help her, she will point them to the fishermen and merchants at the Riva degli Schiavoni, the long waterfront promenade in sestiere Castello where many of the ships come into the city. "I have checked in with sailors there the past few days, but there has been no word of Massimo's ship. There have also been reports of strange sightings near the mouth of the lagoon. The sailors are spooked. Will you dig deeper for me and look for my husband? I'm no adventurer, and I can't afford to shut this place down for days. But I can compensate you for your time."

If the adventurers agree to help Bartolomea, she will point them towards Ivano di Traù, or Ivan of Trogir (LN, human male, early 40s, seafarer, {@creature commoner of Venice|EchoesOfRenaissance}), a fisherman who runs an unofficial guild of sailors who are schiavoni (originating from Dalmatia) but are not wealthy enough to join the more established social organizations in the city. Ivano is wary of talking to strangers, but a 10 sl bribe or successful {@dc 13} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Intimidation}) check will get him to reveal that the local sailors are scared because there are "sea monsters" attacking smaller vessels near the mouth of the lagoon, on the Adriatic Sea side. Ivano thinks these monsters might be the reason Massimo's ship never returned. No fisherman is willing to risk his ship on a journey out there without getting paid at least 10 gd; at the same time, the gondoliers do not travel that far. If the adventurers are serious about their intention to take care of the monster problem, Ivano will give them each a {@item potion of water breathing|DMG}.

Once the adventurers find their way out to the mouth of the lagoon and enter the Adriatic, the weather turns dark, and the sea turns choppy. Have the adventurers make a {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check to pilot the ship without getting dashed against the shore. The boat will be attacked by 2 {@creature merrow}, who focus their attention on trying to pull the characters into the water and drowning them. If the adventurers put up a good fight and manage to severely injure one or more of the merrow, the creatures will escape to their nearby lair. If the characters wish to find out what happened to Massimo, they will have to follow, which requires a {@dc 11} Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check in the stormy seas.

entries.name: Developments
entries: The merrow have made their lair in a pocket of karst limestone about 20 minutes north of the site of the attack and about 50 feet under the surface. Outside the entrance are strewn bits of ships with remains of sailors fastened to them, perhaps to ward off other denizens of the briny depths. Inside the lair is quite rudimentary, consisting of only one large chamber where the merrow sleep and keep their booty. There are {@dice 1d4} {@creature merrow} here in total.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: If the merrow are defeated, the party can take a total of 200 gd and 120 sl. They also find a {@item +1 rapier} among the treasure.

The remains of Massimo and the rest of the crew that traveled with him are here; the merrow have been feeding on them. Massimo can be identified by the ring on his finger and a note in his pocket that has a minor enchantment on it so that it cannot be waterlogged; the note reads:
Our love was a crossing where two lonely people met, in order to protect and guide each other. — B.

If the adventurers return to Bartolomea with the news of her husband's demise, she will reward them with 50 gd. It is all she can spare, but she will also always offer the party a place to stay with clean beds and hearty fare, free of charge.

Additionally, the remains of another tavernkeeper's husband fell victim to this group of merrow. Dionosio, husband of Winifred la Grassetta at All'estero (see City of Venice: Locations, sestiere Castello), went fishing with some friends about a year ago and never returned. His remains and those of his friends, skeletal at this point, are in the lair. Dionosio's ring and brooch, given to him by Winifred, can be recovered and returned to her.

entries.name: Missing Armor, Missing Armoire

entries: {@b Recommended Level:} 3
{@b District Locations:} San Marco, San Polo

{@b Quest Summary:} The Blacksmith's Guild and the Mercer's Guild are accusing each other of stealing prized creations. If the adventurers don't get to the bottom of this, it may escalate into a neighborhood battle.
{@b Possible Rewards:} 400 gd, +1 armor, +1 weapon, consumable common/uncommon items

In the heart of sestiere San Marco, between the Rialto Bridge and the Piazza San Marco, lie the bustling streets of Calle dei Fabbri and Mercerie, where many of the most important trades and shops are located. These streets, almost mini-districts of their own, are the domains of the Blacksmith's Guild (the Calle dei Fabbri area) and the Mercer's Guild (Mercerie way). Though they are not in direct competition with each other for business, the neighbors have a mutual feeling of superiority over the other and believe their profession is more vital to the city. More recently, rivalries are threatening to spill over into actual conflict.

Both guilds are missing valuable creations and blame each other for the disappearances. The Mercer's Guild is missing an ornate armoire filled with exotic silks—both the wardrobe and its contents are "priceless," says Prudentia di Filippi (LN, human female, late 40s, {@creature merchant of Venice|EchoesOfRenaissance}), the sharp and distrustful head of the guild. Meanwhile, the Blacksmiths, led by Fabrizio Buffon (LN, human male, late 40s, {@creature merchant of Venice|EchoesOfRenaissance}) are missing a prize suit of armor covered in gold filigree, which was going to be a gift that Venice would present to the King of England, Henry VIII. Each guild will pay handsomely for the return of its item, and each will pay extra if the party is able to find evidence that the opposing guild was responsible.

When the adventurers inspect the crime scenes and question members of the guild, they learn that each of the guilds, independently, had a new member join their ranks—the same person. Since the guilds do not share notes on their inner workings, and since the member's noble pedigree checked out, there were no suspicions raised. However, this "noble" is actually a master thief posing as a younger noble from the reputable Badoer family. The man, going by the name Marino Badoer, is actually an {@creature aamon|EchoesOfRenaissance}. The fiend has seen a vision of the future which requires several, disparate items of great value to be gathered for some inscrutable purpose. The aamon has also foreseen the interference of the party; it will switch up its disguise and pose as commoners and deliver cryptic messages to the party: "Armor of gold you wish to behold, lies with treasures which unfold" and "The silks and wood of precious places East, find new life amidst a movable feast." These riddles are not extremely helpful, but what is helpful is the material the clues are written on: pieces of sail. As the GM, feel free to drop these messages wherever it seems appropriate: in the rooms where the missing items were stolen from; on the streets nearby where the adventurers "just happen" to find them; or in the adventurers' pockets if their passive Perception skills are not too high. The goal here is that the aamon wants the party to find it so that its vision of the future moves another step closer to fruition.

entries.name: Developments
entries: If the adventurers head out to find the provenance of the sail pieces, you can have them make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check; on a success (you can grant Advantage if any of the adventurers have a background in Venice or in sailing), they can trace the particular coloring of the sail pieces to a local shop called Tre Tochi, specializing in sails for small fishing ships. In the attic of the shop, unbeknownst to its owner Zago, the aamon has made its lair. The floor and walls are plastered with sail pieces and pages from books, and in the center of the attic, the armor, the armoire (with silks still inside), and three other items (your choice from the common or uncommon magic items list) are arranged in a star pattern. The aamon welcomes the adventurers, saying "I expected you earlier" before attacking. It is unclear how the fiend got the heavy armor and wardrobe into the attic, but it doesn't reveal its tricks to the adventurers.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The armor and the armoire can be returned to the guilds, preventing any escalations in their feud—though both sides are disappointed to hear that the other guild wasn't responsible. The party is awarded 200 gd from each guild (400 gd total), and they can keep the magic items they found in the attic.

entries.name: Poison on the Vine

entries: {@b Recommended Level:} 4
{@b District Locations:} San Polo, Castello, Other Islands (Sant'Erasmo and Vignole)

{@b Quest Summary:} Wine barrels in one of the warehouses on the Riva del Vin have been poisoned, and the adventurers are tasked with dealing with it. However, things are not what they seem, and solving the case means involving a local, popular vendor, and a charismatic but troubled priest.
{@b Possible Rewards:} common/uncommon magical item

Riva del Vin is a promenade just south of the Rialto Bridge, along the San Polo side of the Grand Canal, and it is where many products, especially wine (giving the lane its name), are delivered. There are several warehouses along the stretch which store wine, but one of them has been experiencing trouble. The Porta Verde, named that because of its distinctive green doors, has been the victim of sabotage. Several of the wine barrels have been spoiled, or worse, poisoned. One of the nobles who owns the warehouse, Girolamo Priuli (LN human male, late 30s, {@creature New House Patrizio|EchoesOfRenaissance|patrizio, new house}) blames witchcraft, and his accusations have been pointed at Pelegrina Balbi (CG, female elf, {@creature vendor|EchoesOfRenaissance}) in the Rialto Markets. Pelegrina works in the Campo Erberia, the vegetable market area of the Rialto; she helps at all the stands and is well-loved by everyone despite the fact that she doesn't sell produce of her own; oddly, she only seems to be there to help others. Girolamo recently ran into her and took a liking to her, but she rebuffed his advances, as she is in love with a gondolier named Yaqob (CG, male elf, {@creature adept gondolier|EchoesOfRenaissance|gondolier, adept}). Like Pelegrina, Yaqob has been in the city a long time, but they have managed to avoid scrutiny (over the fact that they don't seemingly age, or their appearance) because they are so precious to their communities. Yaqob, too, is in love with Pelegrina, but the two have not declared this to each other.

Girolamo knows there is something extraordinary about Pelegrina, and the fact that she rejected his overtures makes him think that she must be a witch. He is planning on bringing his accusations to the State Inquisitors if the adventurers cannot find the culprit.

Meanwhile, many of the gourds and root vegetables at the Herberia start ripening too quickly and are rotting before they can be sold. Pelegrina suspects a curse, but she is not sure who would be the source. The fact that the vegetables are also being affected by negative magic seems to indicate that she is not the source of the wine warehouse's problem, and Girolamo is pointing his ire in the wrong direction.

If the adventurers are allowed to inspect the warehouse, they can find trace scents of cleaning agents—the type used to clean oil paint—in the poisoned barrels. There is also an opalescent glean to some of the spilled wine, which might indicate oil, or oil paint, mixed in. If the adventurers inspect the rotting vegetables, they can make a {@dc 14} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana} or {@skill Nature}) check; on a success, or by using {@spell detect magic}, the party realizes that there is, indeed, a curse on the food—and the food seems to have bits of marble inside it. There is evidence that someone pushed the pebbles into the vegetables, and then the rot spread.

entries.name: Developments
entries: The one responsible for the ruination of the wine and the vegetables is a priest named Cristofolo Miro Collari (LE, elf male, {@creature mage}), who is in charge of the Church and Monastery of St. Francesco in the Vineyard, in sestiere Castello. Like Pelegrina and Yaqob, Cristofolo is an elf who has been in the city awhile; unlike the other two, Cristofolo has grown accustomed to controlling his flock and getting them to do his bidding, and making people's lives miserable if they cross him. The connection between Cristofolo and the crimes is thin, as he had servants do his dirty work, and he is cautious not to garner too much unwanted attention. However, if the wronged parties are questioned, they may recall having tense conversations with Cristofolo in the past, and that might be a lead that the party can pursue.

The adventurers might take this investigation in a number of different directions, and we recommend giving them time to chase down leads they might find fruitful. Below are some clues that they can come across:

items: Both the wine and vegetable sabotage are related to magic using artistic supplies (paint, paint cleaners, marble used in sculptures).
Several artists' workshops have noticed their supplies of marble, oil paints, and thinners have been reduced, as if there were thefts. However, there has been no evidence of anyone stealing anything.

The vegetables come from the island of Sant'Erasmo, also known as the Garden of Venice, and the wine that was tampered with originated from Le Vignole, known for its vineyards making wine for the doge. Both are easily accessible islands. If the adventurers inspect there, they find evidence that the ground has been poisoned.

The Riva del Vin and the Herberia are in close proximity to each other. If the adventurers stake out the Rialto district, they will see {@dice 2d4} {@creature imp||imps} sabotage another wine warehouse and/or vegetable stands. If the adventurers are watching both areas, {@dice 1d4} imps arrive at each place. The imps literally pour oil paint and cleaning agents in the wine, and push poisoned marble pebbles into some of the produce. If the party lets the imps do their dirty work and then follows them, have them make a group {@dc 14} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check; on a success, the imps raid some art workshops and then make their way back to the St. Francesco church.

If Pelegrina is asked about anyone giving her trouble lately, she will mention Girolamo, a few condottieri, and Cristofolo, who demanded that the Herberia provide produce at a discount for his upcoming fête. Pelegrina says that she saw him using {@spell charm person} spells on some of the vendors and stopped him. He then accosted Pelegrina later, but Yaqob intervened.

Girolamo will admit to pestering Pelegrina, but only because she is "ravishing, and I thought I might have a chance." A successful {@dc 13} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Intimidation}) check will convince Girolamo that Pelegrina is not a witch. Girolamo can also recall running afoul with monks from St. Francesco, who asked for a donation of wine for an upcoming fête. Girolamo admits that he was a bit rude with the monks and dismissed them.

If the adventurers are stuck and need a more overt hint, Yaqob, who is a gondolier and sees and hears a lot of things as a result, can mention a local priest who exerts an inordinate amount of control over his local flock, and it's the same man who accosted him and Pelegrina.

entries: When they arrive at St. Francesco, they find a neighborhood festival in full swing in the church's courtyard. Locals devoted to the church, as well as monks from the monastery, serve food and drinks while a group of musicians play. Cristofolo emerges and gives a sermon, using a {@spell prestidigitation} spell to elicit cheers. If Cristofolo is confronted, he will politely offer to speak to the party inside the church. He then attacks them there, and {@dice 1d6} paintings on the walls animate and attack as well (use the {@creature shadow} stat block). Additionally, {@dice 2d4} {@creature imp||imps} (if they survived) attack the party, too. Cristofolo will fight until he has only 10 or fewer hit points left and then will sue for peace, offering magic items to the party to let him go.

entries.name: Here There May be Dragons

entries: {@b Recommended Level:} 5
{@b District Locations:} Murano

{@b Quest Summary:} An unorthodox priest needs help resurrecting a dead dragon. The adventurers can either convince the priest to stop his foolish plan, or they can aid in his madcap scheme—which leads to strange, and potentially dangerous, results.
{@b Possible Rewards:} 1,000 gd

Pietro Salvalo (CN, human male, late 50s, {@creature clergyman|EchoesOfRenaissance|priest of Venice, clergyman}) is the priest of the Basilica of St. Mary and St. Donatus on the island of Murano. However he is dedicated not to the church he presides over and its congregation per se, but is instead dedicated to the skeletal remains that decorate the back of the church. He believes the rib bones are evidence of true dragons in the world and wants to find a way to research and resurrect the creature. He has long sermons on the mighty "Wyrms of Christ" and how St. Donatus was actually working with the dragon that he is said to have slain. It would be heretical to preach such things...if anyone took him seriously. Parishioners love listening to Pietro's entertaining and apocryphal interpretations of the Biblical tales.

Pietro has a mighty amount of coin (1,000 gd) he has scrimped, saved, and stolen to fund his project of resurrecting the dragon...all he lacks is any discernible talent for arcane matters. He'll gladly ask the adventurers' aid in securing a way to raise the dragon, giving them half of the savings (500 gd) up front, and the other half after they successfully resurrect the dragon. If the party is willing, they will have to get inventive or track down a ritual capable of pulling off such powerful magic: spells like {@spell raise dead} or {@spell animate dead} won't quite do the trick. Questions of the dangers of necromancy will be brushed aside by Pietro as irrelevant, as he plans to train the dragon to burn sinners for the Lord!

entries.name: Developments
entries: If the party is able to help Pietro resurrect the creature, unfortunately for the priest, the bones are not those of a dragon, but a few rib bones of a Pleistocene giant camel, which, if raised, will not burn any sinners but will be very irritable (use the {@creature giant elk} stat block). Depending on where the creature is raised, it could prove to be a danger to the glassmaking foundries on the island, as it might panic and run amok. Moreover, the ceremony is a powerful one and also results in a dangerous Spell Rebound, which results in the resurrection of the remains of St. Donatus (if the party was not careful enough to sequester the 'dragon' bones). St. Donatus (undead {@creature mage}) will be none too happy that he's been brought back as an undead creature, and will attack those who brought these abominations into the world.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Pietro will be angry and disappointed that the bones were not actually those of a dragon, but it won't deter him from thinking dragons are real and that they serve God. He will give the adventurers the rest of their reward, which is 500 gd (1,000 gd total).

entries.name: The Coven Never Forgets

entries: {@b Recommended Level:} 5–6
{@b District Locations:} Cannaregio and Castello

{@b Quest Summary:} Chiara the tavern worker makes magical paintings on the side. She sells those paintings to a prominent male artist who passes them off as his own. However, people who purchase the paintings begin having horrible nightmares, and bodies start dropping. The painter is blamed, but he's innocent. Is Chiara also innocent, or is something else going on?
{@b Possible Rewards:} {@item Nolzur's marvelous pigments||marvelous pigments}, consumable uncommon/rare magic items, 100 gd per month

News floods the markets and streets: a nobleman was found dead in his study, his eyes burned away. This is the second case like this in the past month, and the government is rattled. The state inquisitors and Council of Ten suspect some sort of witchcraft, and they are scouring the city for any signs or suspicious persons. The adventurers can pick up this case by either getting hired by the government, hired by the family of the dead noble, or hired by Giorgio Arianiti (CN, human male, early 30s, painter), a noble artist of Albanian heritage.

entries.name: Scene of the Crime
entries: The Gonzaga family is originally from Mantua, but a branch lives in sestiere Cannaregio for much of the year. Ercole was an older man, in his late 60s, but was, according to his family, still sharp and spry. His body was found in his study and has since been taken to the local church to be cleaned and prepared for burial. The adventurers can inspect the scene; on a successful {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) or Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check, they find barely perceptible burn marks resembling goat hoof prints in the carpet leading from a section of the wall towards the chair where the noble was found dead. The prints are so faint that they blend in with the designs of the Mamluk carpet. The area of the wall where the prints originate holds a painting which Ercole apparently recently purchased: it depicts Saturn (Chronos) devouring his son. A successful {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check reveals that the painting is magical; an {@spell identify} spell reveals that it is cursed and that some being is inside the painting. Casting {@spell dispel magic} or attacking the painting in any way will lead to the creature emerging: {@creature Il Mazaròl|EchoesOfRenaissance|Il Mazaròl, The Impaled Eye}. It fights to the death and will not divulge why it killed the noble.

If the adventurers decide to inspect Ercole's body in the local church before it is buried, they find that his eyes have been destroyed, as if someone jabbed two searing hot pokers into the sockets. The body is also covered in puncture wounds. A {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine}) or Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check reveals that the wounds are unnatural.

If the adventurers trace the ownership of the painting, they find that Ercole purchased it from an up-and-coming painter named Teodoro Arianiti, and it was never owned by the other dead noble. Therefore, there must be multiple paintings housing murderous creatures.

entries.name: Investigating the Budding Artist
entries: Teodoro works out of a modest workshop attached to his family home. The Arianitis are a family originally from Albania who have lived in Venice for the past two generations. If the adventurers question Teodoro, it becomes apparent very quickly that he does not have the knowledge or skill to have painted the Saturn painting. On a successful {@dc 12} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}, {@skill Deception}, or {@skill Intimidation}) check, the party can get Teodoro to admit that he buys them from a "truly talented but perilously shy woman" and sells them as his own. The true artist is named Chiara, who works in the kitchen of an osteria in sestiere Castello.

entries.name: The Troubled Artist
entries: The trail leads to Osteria Seppe (Cuttlefish Tavern), a very popular spot for delicious seafood. Giorgios is welcoming to the adventurers but becomes circumspect when they ask about Chiara. If the party mentions why they have come or succeeds on a {@dc 16} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}, {@skill Deception}, or {@skill Intimidation}) check, Giorgios will allow them back to talk to Chiara, but warns them: "Chiara has a very good heart. Do not judge her on her appearance. And if anything should befall her, I will kill you."

Chiara (CG, tiefling female, early 20s, {@creature disciple|EchoesOfRenaissance|malandante disciple}) is painfully shy. When told that her paintings are cursed, she turns pale: "I simply paint what I see in my dreams! I truly never wanted anyone to get hurt!" She explains that she was once a disciple in a coven of malandanti witches but escaped. The adventurers can use magic to discern that Chiara herself has been cursed to dream up horrible things and put them in her paintings. The {@spell remove curse} spell will get rid of the specific affliction, but to stop the cycle of torment, the adventurers will have to seek out the malandanti coven.

entries.name: Fair is Foul, and Foul is Fair
entries: The malandanti coven occupies a swampy area in the northern section of the Venetian Lagoon. The adventure can be concluded in two main ways:

items: {@b Kill the malandanti.} It is a tough fight on swampy ground with fog. The leader is a {@creature witch of the night|EchoesOfRenaissance|malandante, witch of the night}, accompanied by 2 {@creature disciple|EchoesOfRenaissance|malandanti, disciples} and 1 {@creature walker on the rotten path|EchoesOfRenaissance|malandante, walker on the rotten path}.
{@b Make a deal.} The witches will demand a high price for Chiara's safety. Roll on or choose from the table below:

entries.caption: Witches' Demands
rows: One of the character's first born children.
The head and liver of an adult dragon, preferably a metallic one.
Two magical items in the characters' possession.
A sample of blood from a {@creature Sanctae Romane Ecclesiae|EchoesOfRenaissance|sanctae romanae ecclesiae}, cardinal of the Roman Church.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: If Chiara is saved, she will give the adventurers {@item Nolzur's marvelous pigments||marvelous pigments} and will offer them free paintings they can sell whenever they need some extra coin (100 gd per month). The government will also award the characters a magical item in return for their silence.

entries.name: Trompe-l'oeil

entries: {@b Recommended Level:} 6–7
{@b District Locations:} San Polo
{@b Quest Summary:} The master painter Tintoretto is looking for bodyguards for a most unusual reason: his paintings are attacking him while he is trying to complete them.
{@b Possible Rewards:} 200 gd each, coral candlestick

Jacopo Robusti, known better by his nickname Tintoretto ("little dyer's boy"), is currently painting a series of works for the Scuola Grande di San Rocco. Tintoretto (use the {@creature royal artist|EchoesOfRenaissance} stat block) has already completed a series of paintings in the Sala dell'Albergo upstairs, and a cycle above the Scarpagnino staircase; he is now working in the upper Sala Capitolare (Chapter Room). However, for the past three days, each time he works, figures leap out of his finished paintings to attack him! Tintoretto seeks experienced, discreet adventurers to guard him while he paints and silence the attackers for good.

entries.name: First Wave
entries: Tintoretto works on {@i Agony in the Garden}. A haunting song sung by a female voice fills the halls, warning of "boils and pestilence and suffering upon all who steal from me." Six angels (use the {@creature imp} stat block) fly off the Old Testament paintings above the staircase and attack. When killed, they turn to dust and reappear in their paintings at the next dawn.

entries.name: Second Wave
entries: {@dice 1d4} more angels (use the {@creature bearded devil} stat block) drop from the ceiling paintings, while 2 pale, emaciated apostolic figures (use the {@creature ghoul} stat block) climb out of nearby paintings and try to strangle Tintoretto.

If the adventurers fend off this attack, an angry screech echoes from a locked side portal ({@dc 15} Dexterity with thieves' tools) leading upstairs to the Treasury. Beyond is a black metal door ({@dc 17} Dexterity with thieves' tools). Behind it lies an elegant candlestick made of red coral. A {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check or {@spell detect magic} reveals it is cursed.

Touching the candlestick triggers the haunting female voice to scream, demanding freedom. The candlestick holds a {@creature hex-bender|EchoesOfRenaissance|malandante, hex-bender}. She claims a "good-for-nothing servant of Venice" trapped her and gifted the candlestick to the Scuola. If released by destroying the candlestick, she attacks the party. If dispelled with {@spell dispel magic} cast at 4th level or above, she is forcibly returned to her coven, leaving behind an enchanted, uncursed coral candlestick.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Tintoretto pays each of the adventurers 200 gd. Additionally, they can keep the coral candlestick from the Treasury.

entries.name: Rotten Flesh, Rotten Hearts

entries: {@b Recommended Level:} 7–8
{@b District Locations:} San Polo, Other Islands

{@b Quest Summary:} There are gruesome experiments being conducted on the Lazzaretto Vecchio in the name of plague prevention, and the adventurers are tasked with getting to the bottom of them. This leads them to confront Brother Luca and his minions.
{@b Possible Rewards:} four flasks of {@item Holy Water (flask)|PHB|holy water}, two 2nd level spell scrolls, 400 gd, and {@item Lazarus flail|EchoesOfRenaissance}

The Lazzaretto Vecchio (old quarantine island) contains a hospital for plague victims and a leper colony. Brother Luca (NE, human male, late 30s, {@creature mortidanti|EchoesOfRenaissance|plague doctor, mortidanti}) leads a group of plague doctors and priests tending to the sick, calling them The Castaways (I Naufraghi). On the surface, Brother Luca is helping the Confraternity of St. Roch find a cure; in secret, he has been feeding his loyal Castaways flesh from dead plague victims, turning them into ravenous abominations locked in the northeastern sector of the island.
This quest can be pursued as a continuation of {@i Trompe-l'oeil} or as a standalone adventure.

entries.name: An Argument
entries: At the Scuola Grande di San Rocco, adventurers overhear an argument between Lundardo di Mazi (NE, {@creature mortidanti|EchoesOfRenaissance|plague doctor, mortidanti}) and Ambrogio Bragadin (LN, human male, late 60s, {@creature Old House Patrizio|EchoesOfRenaissance|patrizio, old house}). On a successful {@dc 15} Charisma check, Ambrogio reveals he leads the Hounds of St. Roch, dedicated to curing the plague. He hired Brother Luca, but suspects Luca's experiments have created monstrous abominations, and hires the party to investigate the island and eradicate any threats.

entries.name: Lazzaretto Vecchio
entries: At the island's entrance, three Knights of St. Lazarus led by Emanuele Acritano (LG, human male, {@creature knight||crusader knight}, no shield) demand entry after being barred by Brother Luca. Emanuele asks the party for help investigating.

Inside, Brother Luca refuses to let anyone into the northeastern wing, claiming it is under renovation. If pressed, Luca attacks alongside 2 {@creature mortidanti|EchoesOfRenaissance|plague doctor, mortidanti} assistants and {@dice 3d8} Castaways (use the {@creature commoner of Venice|EchoesOfRenaissance} stat block). With his dying breath, Luca pleads: "Don't kill my children. They are the key."

In Luca's office, research notes detail his horrific experiments and mention a grey-skinned visitor with pointed ears (a {@creature ladropaura|EchoesOfRenaissance} that gave him the trapped malandante hex-bender).

entries.name: Developments
entries: Unlocking the northeastern wing ({@dc 17} Dexterity with thieves' tools or Luca's keys) reveals {@dice 2d8} {@creature ghoul||ghouls} and {@dice 2d6} {@creature ghast||ghasts}, led by Brother Luca's first creation, Yugra ({@creature flesh golem} with INT 10 and the ability to speak). If informed, Emanuele and 5 {@creature knight||crusader knights} will fight alongside the party.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The adventurers find 4 flasks of {@item Holy Water (flask)|PHB|holy water} and two 2nd-level spell scrolls in Brother Luca's chambers. Emanuele rewards them with a {@item Lazarus flail|EchoesOfRenaissance}. Ambrogio pays 400 gd for their efforts and their silence, subsequently petitioning the government to place the Order of St. Lazarus in charge of the Lazzaretto.

entries.name: Sidequests
entries: These quests can take place within the adventure module {@i A Serenade for the Damned} or can be treated as standalone adventures.
Creature names followed by the symbol 🔔 are from the 5e SRD. Creature names followed by the symbol ⁜ are from previous Historica Arcanum releases.

entries.name: Lurking Dread

entries: {@b Recommended Level:} 2
{@b District Locations:} Santa Croce
{@b Quest Summary:} A narrow canal hidden from direct sunlight is known for its unlucky nature. Gondoliers have gone missing, and it is up to the adventurers to get to the bottom of the problem.
{@b Possible Rewards:} 50 gd, common magic item

Tucked deep within sestiere Santa Croce is a narrow canal that rarely sees direct sunlight. Gondoliers who use it know that the useful shortcut it provides must be weighed against grave dangers. The canal is believed to be haunted, and a few gondoliers and passengers have disappeared over the past few years. Many of the gondoliers refuse to believe the stories, but even locals living in nearby buildings have heard strange noises and drowned cries on certain evenings. The adventurers are tasked with getting to the bottom of what is going on, and eliminating or expelling the danger. If the adventurers are aware of Angós, the Disrupter of Waves and think to ask about it, the gondoliers will either not know who the adventurers are referring to, or they will say, "Angós would never kill gondoliers. This must be something else."

entries.name: Developments
entries: The adventurers need to stake out the canal, preferably during one of the darkest nights of the month. No fire light illuminates the canal normally, so if the adventurers do not have their own illumination or darkvision, the area will be heavily obscured. A {@creature canali plaguebeast|EchoesOfRenaissance} lurks in the waters, but it is an opportunistic hunter. It won't attack a full party unless it is defending itself: it will prefer to grab someone set apart from the group or someone who appears smaller and weaker. The canal is only 7 feet wide; the buildings on either side are over 30 feet tall, and the water is only 6 feet deep.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The gondoliers will offer a monetary reward for getting rid of the threat, either killing the beast or forcing it to leave (50 gd). You can also have the guild offer the adventurers a common magic item if it suits your game.

entries.name: What Do Shadows Think?

entries: {@b Recommended Level:} 2
{@b District Locations:} San Marco
{@b Quest Summary:} Gasparo the wine seller is spooked; he needs help quieting a haunting voice that is ruining his business.
{@b Possible Rewards:} {@item goblet of perspicacity|EchoesOfRenaissance}, {@item decanter of endless wine|EchoesOfRenaissance}

Gasparo, who sells wine under St. Mark's Bell Tower (Campanile) in the Piazza San Marco, is usually a cheery and garrulous man—quick with a smile and a story. He calls the cups of wine he sells ombra, after the shadow of the bell tower that he moves with throughout the day. However, lately he sits glumly in the sun across the piazza from the tower, watching the shadow intently. If asked about his change of mood and location, he will say "the shadow is cursed. It won't leave me alone!" If the adventurers convince Gasparo to tell them more, he will say that he started hearing a "chill voice from beyond the grave."

Gasparo is being haunted by the {@creature ghost} of a young noble woman who was killed by her lover. The ghost knows Gasparo is well-known for his good company, his stories of romance and lost love, and that he is known for not spreading lies. Thus, the ghost has been bothering Gasparo to tell the truth about her story so that her murderer will see justice. On a successful {@dc 13} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Intimidation}) check, the adventurers can convince Gasparo to head back to the bell tower's shadow, where the ghost immediately tries to reach out again. Alternatively, the adventurers could try to reach out to the chill voice themselves, and if they have a reputation of doing good in the city, the ghost can be convinced to speak with them. During the day, when the bell tower casts a shadow, she is able to communicate with the party; however, she is only visible at night and only makes herself visible to those she fully trusts.
The ghost will give the following information to the characters or to Gasparo:

items: Her name in life was Agatia di Selino. She was originally from Candia (Crete), but she and her mother moved to Venice recently. As each day passes, she loses more grip on her past life, so she is desperate to see her killer brought to justice.

She was working as a cleaner and assistant for the Dolfin family, and started a relationship with one of the family's scions, Giovanni Dolfin (LE, human male, early 20s, {@creature Old House Patrizio|EchoesOfRenaissance|patrizio, old house}). Their relationship was secret, but Giovanni promised her much. She knew that nobles are not allowed to marry outside of the noble families, but she had held out hope that true love would triumph.
Her natural talents in math led to her being asked to count stores and calculate costs to help the family's business.

She discovered discrepancies in the numbers and brought these to Giovanni's attention. He promised her that he would look into it. That night, he invited Agatia on a romantic gondola ride. He strangled her in the covered gondola and paid the gondolier to help him dispose of her body.

She doesn't expect Giovanni to be punished by the government for her disappearance, but she wants his reputation destroyed, as she now suspects he was responsible for the discrepancies in the family's accounts.

entries: The adventurers have several ways they could approach a solution to this quest. They could convince Gasparo to spread the story of Agatia and what Giovanni did to her, though it could lead to Gasparo being arrested for "spreading lies" if the party does not have concrete evidence to back up the stories. Evidence or no, the tale of Agatia's murder and the cold-blooded noble lover begins to spread quickly if Gasparo is convinced to spin the tale with a successful {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Intimidation}) check. Alternatively, the party can confront Giovanni directly and avenge Agatia, which would be the fastest solution but one which would lead to more problems for the party. Giovanni travels with {@dice 1d4} condottieri guards at all times. If they go this route, Giovanni will deny any wrongdoing unless he is about to be killed; then he will plead for his life and reveal where he hid her body. He will admit that he was afraid his indiscretions would be exposed, so he silenced her. He, along with another young noble named Bernardo Nani (LE, human male, early 20s, {@creature New House Patrizio|EchoesOfRenaissance|patrizio, new house}) are investing in the slavery trade, buying prisoners from Candia and selling them to Spain, among other locations.

If the party does not want to risk confronting a powerful noble, they could do their own investigations into the Dolfin family's business. If they sneak into the Palazzo Dolfin, they can potentially find the incriminating records in the warehouses on the ground floor (piano terra). A successful {@dc 16} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) check will get the party past the 2 condottieri guards, and a successful {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check will give the party all the details they need to reveal that Giovanni and an outside partner have been funneling money away from the family for another venture. Alternatively, the party could pose as merchants wanting to do business with the Dolfins and talk their way in and out of the palazzo. A successful {@dc 14} Charisma ({@skill Deception}) check will get them into the palazzo for a meeting with the patriarch, Delfino Dolfin (LN, human male, late 50s, {@creature Old House Patrizio|EchoesOfRenaissance|patrizio, old house}).

entries.name: Developments
entries: The adventurers can collect enough information to land Giovanni in serious trouble, though mostly due to embezzlement rather than the murder or horrid trade he was involved in. He will be arrested for embezzlement and conspiracy, and he will be disowned by his family. Delfino Dolfin will pay reparations to Agatia's mother, who works as a washer woman at an osteria, and pay for a proper burial for Agatia's body, which, if the party doesn't find it, will be found after Giovanni confesses to everything in custody. Agatia will thank the party before departing the bell tower's shadow.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: For their help and dedication to uncovering the truth, Gasparo will award the adventurers with a {@item goblet of perspicacity|EchoesOfRenaissance} and a {@item decanter of endless wine|EchoesOfRenaissance}.

entries.name: The Merchant Who Loved Me

entries: {@b Recommended Level:} 3
{@b District Locations:} San Marco, Other Islands (Burano and Mazzorbo)

{@b Quest Summary:} A merchant of the Fondaco dei Tedeschi has gone missing, and both Venice and the Holy Roman Empire suspect him of espionage. Either side will pay handsomely for his apprehension, dead or alive.
{@b Possible Rewards:} 250 gd, one use of the {@spell bless} spell each, one common/uncommon magic item

Nikolaus Herel (LN, human male, early 20s, {@creature merchant of Venice|EchoesOfRenaissance}) is a merchant in the Fondaco dei Tedeschi, the headquarters for all Germanic merchants in Venice. The building sits right next to the Rialto Bridge on the Grand Canal. It has warehouses on its ground floor, along with a large courtyard, and upper floors house offices and living quarters of all official Germanic merchants in the city.

Spies of the Council of Ten suspect that Nikolaus was more than just a merchant, however; they believe he was supplying merchant guilds in the Holy Roman Empire with state secrets about lacemaking and other industries. They have records of his visits to the island of Burano, the lacemaking center of Venice, as he and some other merchants were working on exporting Burano lace (legally) to the Holy Roman Empire, but they could find no evidence of any wrongdoing. Now he has disappeared into thin air, apparently—no one in the Fondaco knows where he has gone. In fact, Nikolaus is only a spy in the sense that every merchant shares what they know will give their businesses an advantage, or if the Empire demands it. However, Nikolaus was not a particularly important asset—not until now, at least. His disappearance has alarmed Holy Roman emissaries in the Fondaco, who fear that he discovered very lucrative secrets and has absconded to France or somewhere else with his knowledge. The truth is that neither government is correct: Nikolaus fell head over heels in love, and will do anything for the object of his affection—even scuttle his own career and risk his life.

If the adventurers investigate, either on the Venetian government's or the Fondaco's behalf, they will be followed by the other side: there are spies everywhere in Venice, after all. If the adventurers are hired by the Fondaco, they are allowed to inspect Nikolaus's quarters; if they are working for the Council of Ten, they will have to talk their way, or sneak, into the Fondaco upper floors ({@dc 16}) and break into the room ({@dc 15} Strength [{@skill Athletics}] or thieves' tools). Inside the spartan bedchambers, a successful {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check reveals a loose panel in a wardrobe, behind which is a strip of lace cloth with a note written in what appears to be charcoal, {@i "please, you have kind eyes, good sir. Take me away from here."} The note appears to have been written by someone new to writing, or with a potential physical ailment, as the penmanship is clumsy.

Signs point to the island of Burano and the lacemaking houses. If the adventurers did not find the clue in the bedchambers or were unable to enter the room (if they are working for the Council of Ten, for instance), you can have one of the Council of Ten spies tell them that a young woman from Burano has also gone missing, having not shown up for work today. Burano lies to the northeast of Venice, in an area of the lagoon that was more prominent in earlier centuries when Venice had closer ties to Constantinople; the nearby islands of Torcello and Mazzorbo were especially prominent. When the adventurers pull up to the docks of Burano, they find a sleepy island with a small community of colorful houses, and soon thereafter the sounds of chatting women working at needlepoint can be heard coming from several of the houses lining the fondamente. If the adventurers are working for the Council of Ten, they can head straight for the house with the missing woman; if they are working for the Fondaco, they can procure a list of the houses the merchants visited, and from there discover that a young woman is missing from one of them.

If the adventurers question the workers—all very young women working for an older madam—they can make a {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check. On a success, they find that, although it is normal to be concerned for a missing person, the workers are overly nervous. If they are pressed, they will reveal the following:

items: The missing young woman's name is Bella. She never mentioned a family name.
She arrived recently, and she had no memory of her past.
Her embroidery skills are second to none. However, she never seemed happy.
The women will say that being around Bella made them cheerier, more satisfied with their work, and now that she's gone, everything seems even more laborious and tiresome.

entries: The workers have not seen Nikolaus since the German merchants visited in an official capacity a few days ago. If the adventurers get permission, they can search the living quarters where the women sleep, and search Bella's bunk. They find a piece of cloth, torn by a knife or other sharp object, and a piece of charcoal under her pillow. A {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana} or {@skill Investigation}) or Wisdom ({@skill Perception} or {@skill Survival}) check will pick up a trail leading behind the house and along the back canal; you can tailor the trail to your party. For instance, with a Survival or Perception check, it is the strong scent of wildflowers; with Arcana or Investigation, it is a faint trail of magic, almost like dust caught in the light.

This trail leads to the narrow channel between Burano and the island of Mazzorbo, an island mostly consisting of farmland. Have the adventurers make a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check; on a success, they can follow the trail to Chiesa di Santa Caterina (Church of St. Catherine); however, they also notice that they are being followed by a group of {@dice 1d4} {@creature ombra|EchoesOfRenaissance|ombra, royal spies}. Nikolaus and Bella are hiding in the church and preparing to leave for the mainland at night. They will not fight the party, but they will beg the adventurers to look the other way and let them go. Nikolaus fell in love with Bella at first sight, and Bella needed a ticket out of the lagoon. She doesn't remember her past, but she knows she is not safe here, and every day that passes fills her with more anxiety. A {@spell detect magic} spell will indicate that Bella herself gives off a magical aura; if she is pressed on the issue, she will eventually reveal that she is an {@creature lone one|EchoesOfRenaissance|angelo, lone one}, a type of celestial creature. If she is asked why she didn't escape on her own, she will say that she does not know why, but she saw a vision (with a divination spell) that she must leave with a "person with sandy hair and sad eyes" or she will be trapped forever. She has no destination in mind except to get away from the lagoon.

entries.name: Developments
entries: The adventurers can complete this quest in a number of ways: turning Nikolaus in to the Fondaco or the Council of Ten; turning both of the escapees in; letting them escape; or helping them get to the mainland.

items: If Nikolaus is brought back to the Fondaco dei Tedeschi, he will not be tried for treason, but he will be fired and forced to return to the Holy Roman Empire. On his way out of the city, he will try to escape and return to Bella, but he is shot with crossbow bolts after jumping into the lagoon and trying to swim away. Bella, meanwhile, sadly returns to her work unless one of the party members fits the physical description of "sandy hair and sad eyes"; if that is the case, she will beg them to help her escape. If they do not, she sadly returns to work, and two days later a {@creature hinthial|EchoesOfRenaissance|hinthial, etruscan shade} appears and kills her—its reasons for doing so are unknown. The party will be rewarded 250 gd.

If Nikolaus is turned in to the Council of Ten, they will interrogate him for days, ultimately finding that he did not steal any lacemaking secrets. Bella, meanwhile, sadly returns to her work unless one of the party members fits the physical description of "sandy hair and sad eyes"; if that is the case, she will beg them to help her escape. If they do not, she sadly returns to work, and while Nikolaus is still in a Pozzi prison cell in the Doge's Palace, a {@creature hinthial|EchoesOfRenaissance|hinthial, etruscan shade} appears and kills her. The party will be rewarded 250 gd.

If the adventurers let Nikolaus and Bella escape, they are eternally grateful. Nikolaus will give them 50 gd, and Bella will give them a blessing: each of the adventurers has 1 use of the {@spell bless} spell, which they can cast without needing spell slots or spellcasting ability. The ombra spies that were following the party, if they have not been shaken, will follow Nikolaus and Bella and apprehend them if the adventurers do not stop them.

If the adventurers offer to accompany Nikolaus and Bella to the mainland, Bella will be grateful but nervous, as it is not what she saw in her vision. They will have to take boats or traverse several marshy islands between Mazzorbo and the mainland. A {@creature hinthial|EchoesOfRenaissance|hinthial, etruscan shade} will attack them. It can walk on water, so the boats do not hinder it. If the hinthial is defeated, the adventurers can gain one common or uncommon magic item, which falls out of the hinthial's nets.

entries.name: In the Murk and Mire

entries: {@b Recommended Level:} 2–3
{@b District Locations:} San Marco, Castello, Other Islands

{@b Quest Summary:} A beloved engineer has not returned home, and his wife will reward the adventurers if they look into it. The quest leads to inquiring with the fishermen at Riva degli Schiavoni before it ends at the lair of some sea monsters at the mouth of the Adriatic.
{@b Possible Rewards:} {@item +1 rapier}, 250 gd and 120 sl

Bartolomea (NG, human female, late 30s, {@creature merchant of Venice|EchoesOfRenaissance}) runs the White Lion Tavern (Osteria di Leon Bianco) while her husband Massimo, an engineer, often travels to other parts of the Venetian territories for construction projects. He recently went to Zara (Zadar) and was expected to return a few days ago. If the adventurers frequent the White Lion, they will notice that Bartolomea is not her usual cheerful self, and if they offer to help her, she will point them to the fishermen and merchants at the Riva degli Schiavoni, the long waterfront promenade in sestiere Castello where many of the ships come into the city. "I have checked in with sailors there the past few days, but there has been no word of Massimo's ship. There have also been reports of strange sightings near the mouth of the lagoon. The sailors are spooked. Will you dig deeper for me and look for my husband? I'm no adventurer, and I can't afford to shut this place down for days. But I can compensate you for your time."

If the adventurers agree to help Bartolomea, she will point them towards Ivano di Traù, or Ivan of Trogir (LN, human male, early 40s, seafarer, {@creature commoner of Venice|EchoesOfRenaissance}), a fisherman who runs an unofficial guild of sailors who are schiavoni (originating from Dalmatia) but are not wealthy enough to join the more established social organizations in the city. Ivano is wary of talking to strangers, but a 10 sl bribe or successful {@dc 13} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Intimidation}) check will get him to reveal that the local sailors are scared because there are "sea monsters" attacking smaller vessels near the mouth of the lagoon, on the Adriatic Sea side. Ivano thinks these monsters might be the reason Massimo's ship never returned. No fisherman is willing to risk his ship on a journey out there without getting paid at least 10 gd; at the same time, the gondoliers do not travel that far. If the adventurers are serious about their intention to take care of the monster problem, Ivano will give them each a {@item potion of water breathing|DMG}.

Once the adventurers find their way out to the mouth of the lagoon and enter the Adriatic, the weather turns dark, and the sea turns choppy. Have the adventurers make a {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check to pilot the ship without getting dashed against the shore. The boat will be attacked by 2 {@creature merrow}, who focus their attention on trying to pull the characters into the water and drowning them. If the adventurers put up a good fight and manage to severely injure one or more of the merrow, the creatures will escape to their nearby lair. If the characters wish to find out what happened to Massimo, they will have to follow, which requires a {@dc 11} Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check in the stormy seas.

entries.name: Developments
entries: The merrow have made their lair in a pocket of karst limestone about 20 minutes north of the site of the attack and about 50 feet under the surface. Outside the entrance are strewn bits of ships with remains of sailors fastened to them, perhaps to ward off other denizens of the briny depths. Inside the lair is quite rudimentary, consisting of only one large chamber where the merrow sleep and keep their booty. There are {@dice 1d4} {@creature merrow} here in total.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: If the merrow are defeated, the party can take a total of 200 gd and 120 sl. They also find a {@item rapier +1|DMG|+1 rapier} among the treasure.

The remains of Massimo and the rest of the crew that traveled with him are here; the merrow have been feeding on them. Massimo can be identified by the ring on his finger and a note in his pocket that has a minor enchantment on it so that it cannot be waterlogged; the note reads:
Our love was a crossing where two lonely people met, in order to protect and guide each other. — B.

If the adventurers return to Bartolomea with the news of her husband's demise, she will reward them with 50 gd. It is all she can spare, but she will also always offer the party a place to stay with clean beds and hearty fare, free of charge.

Additionally, the remains of another tavernkeeper's husband fell victim to this group of merrow. Dionosio, husband of Winifred la Grassetta at All'estero (see City of Venice: Locations, sestiere Castello), went fishing with some friends about a year ago and never returned. His remains and those of his friends, skeletal at this point, are in the lair. Dionosio's ring and brooch, given to him by Winifred, can be recovered and returned to her.

entries.name: Missing Armor, Missing Armoire

entries: {@b Recommended Level:} 3
{@b District Locations:} San Marco, San Polo

{@b Quest Summary:} The Blacksmith's Guild and the Mercer's Guild are accusing each other of stealing prized creations. If the adventurers don't get to the bottom of this, it may escalate into a neighborhood battle.
{@b Possible Rewards:} 400 gd, +1 armor, +1 weapon, consumable common/uncommon items

In the heart of sestiere San Marco, between the Rialto Bridge and the Piazza San Marco, lie the bustling streets of Calle dei Fabbri and Mercerie, where many of the most important trades and shops are located. These streets, almost mini-districts of their own, are the domains of the Blacksmith's Guild (the Calle dei Fabbri area) and the Mercer's Guild (Mercerie way). Though they are not in direct competition with each other for business, the neighbors have a mutual feeling of superiority over the other and believe their profession is more vital to the city. More recently, rivalries are threatening to spill over into actual conflict.

Both guilds are missing valuable creations and blame each other for the disappearances. The Mercer's Guild is missing an ornate armoire filled with exotic silks—both the wardrobe and its contents are "priceless," says Prudentia di Filippi (LN, human female, late 40s, {@creature merchant of Venice|EchoesOfRenaissance}), the sharp and distrustful head of the guild. Meanwhile, the Blacksmiths, led by Fabrizio Buffon (LN, human male, late 40s, {@creature merchant of Venice|EchoesOfRenaissance}) are missing a prize suit of armor covered in gold filigree, which was going to be a gift that Venice would present to the King of England, Henry VIII. Each guild will pay handsomely for the return of its item, and each will pay extra if the party is able to find evidence that the opposing guild was responsible.

When the adventurers inspect the crime scenes and question members of the guild, they learn that each of the guilds, independently, had a new member join their ranks—the same person. Since the guilds do not share notes on their inner workings, and since the member's noble pedigree checked out, there were no suspicions raised. However, this "noble" is actually a master thief posing as a younger noble from the reputable Badoer family. The man, going by the name Marino Badoer, is actually an {@creature aamon|EchoesOfRenaissance}. The fiend has seen a vision of the future which requires several, disparate items of great value to be gathered for some inscrutable purpose. The aamon has also foreseen the interference of the party; it will switch up its disguise and pose as commoners and deliver cryptic messages to the party: "Armor of gold you wish to behold, lies with treasures which unfold" and "The silks and wood of precious places East, find new life amidst a movable feast." These riddles are not extremely helpful, but what is helpful is the material the clues are written on: pieces of sail. As the GM, feel free to drop these messages wherever it seems appropriate: in the rooms where the missing items were stolen from; on the streets nearby where the adventurers "just happen" to find them; or in the adventurers' pockets if their passive Perception skills are not too high. The goal here is that the aamon wants the party to find it so that its vision of the future moves another step closer to fruition.

entries.name: Developments
